children.translated_text: <s>Laghubhāgavatāmṛta</s>

First Part: <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇāmṛta</s> (The Nectar of Śrī Kṛṣṇa), First Section:
Determination of the tattva of <s>Bhagavān</s> as characterized by <s>svayaṃrūpa</s> (original form), <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime form), <s>svāṃśa</s> (personal expansion), <s>āveśa</s> (empowered form), and <s>prakāśa</s> (manifestation).
Oṃ. Salutations to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> —
Salutations to that <s>Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa</s>, of unobstructed intelligence,

children.text: yo dhatte sarva-bhūtānām abhavāyośatīḥ kalāḥ // Lbh_1,1.1 //
children.translated_text: who manifests auspicious arts (<s>kalā</s>) for the liberation of all beings.
Of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-complexion, but with a non-dark (<s>akṛṣṇa</s>) effulgence, accompanied by His limbs, sub-limbs, weapons, and associates —

children.text: yajñaiḥ saṅkīrtana-prāyair yajanti hi su-medhasaḥ // Lbh_1,1.2 //
children.translated_text: Him the wise worship with <s>yajñas</s> (sacrifices) consisting predominantly of <s>saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting).
Swollen with the flood of nectar flowing from the lotus-mouth —
may the cooing of <s>Mukunda</s>'s flute milk forth my bliss!
The syllables '<s>Hare Kṛṣṇa</s>' issuing from the mouth of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s> —

children.text: majjayanto jagat premṇi vijayantāṃ tad-āhvayāḥ // Lbh_1,1.4 //
children.translated_text: plunging the world in divine love (<s>prema</s>) — may those invocations be ever victorious!
The <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavatāmṛta</s>, which was expanded by the lotus-feet of the revered master (<s>Prabhupāda</s>, i.e. <s>Sanātana Gosvāmin</s>) —

children.text: yad-vyatāni tad evedaṃ saṅkṣepeṇa niṣevyate // Lbh_1,1.5 //
children.translated_text: that very same is here relished in abridged form.
This <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) is twofold, relating to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> and His devotees;

children.text: ādau kṛṣṇāmṛtaṃ tatra suhṛdbhyaḥ pariveṣyate // Lbh_1,1.6 //
children.translated_text: first, the nectar of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is served herein to well-wishers.
Releasing the constraint of extensive argumentation here by me,

children.text: pradhānatvāt parmāṇeṣu śabda eva pramāṇyate // Lbh_1,1.7 //
children.translated_text: since among the <s>pramāṇas</s> (means of valid knowledge), <s>śabda</s> (scriptural testimony) alone is primarily authoritative.
Since they (the great sages) accepted the authoritativeness of <s>śabda</s> alone,
based on the logical demonstration that '<s>śāstra</s> is the source [of knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>]' (<s>śāstra-yonitvāt</s>).
Moreover, from the precept 'since reasoning has no firm ground' (<s>tarkāpratiṣṭhānāt</s>),

children.text: amībhir eva suvyaktaṃ tarkasyānādaraḥ kṛtaḥ // Lbh_1,1.9 //
children.translated_text: by these very authorities, the disregard for mere reasoning has been clearly established.
Now, in order to declare the supremacy among objects of worship, from the perspective of supreme excellence,

children.text: kṛṣṇasya tat-svarūpāṇi nirūpyante kramād iha // Lbh_1,1.10 //
children.translated_text: the essential forms (<s>svarūpa</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are here determined in sequence.
<s>Svayaṃ rūpa</s> (the original form), <s>tad-ekātma-rūpa</s> (the form identical in essence with Him), and that named <s>āveśa</s> (the empowered) —

children.text: ity asau trividhaṃ bhāti prapañcātīta-dhāmasu // Lbh_1,1.11 //
children.translated_text: thus He shines forth in three ways in the realms beyond the material world.

children.text: ananyāpekṣi yad rūpaṃ svayaṃ-rūpaḥ sa ucyate // Lbh_1,1.12 //
children.translated_text: That form which is independent of all else is called the <s>svayaṃrūpa</s> (original form).
Of these, the <s>svayaṃrūpa</s> (original form):
<s>Īśvara</s> (the Supreme Controller) is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the supreme, whose form is <s>sac-cid-ānanda</s> (being-consciousness-bliss);
without beginning, yet the beginning of all, <s>Govinda</s>, the cause of all causes.
Thus (<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.1).
Here, the <s>tad-ekātma-rūpa</s> (form identical in essence):
That form which shines non-differently, in its own essential nature,
yet appears otherwise in appearance (<s>ākṛti</s>) and the like — He is called <s>tad-ekātma-rūpa</s>;

children.text: sa vilāsaḥ svāṃśa iti dhatte bheda-dvayaṃ punaḥ // Lbh_1,1.14 //
children.translated_text: He further bears a twofold distinction as <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime form) and <s>svāṃśa</s> (personal expansion).
Of these, the <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime form):

children.text: svarūpam anyākāraṃ yat tasya bhāti vilāsataḥ |
children.translated_text: That own form which shines forth in another appearance, as a pastime (<s>vilāsa</s>),

children.text: prāyeṇātma-samaṃ śaktyā sa vilāso nigadyate // Lbh_1,1.15 //
children.translated_text: being generally equal to Himself in power — He is called a <s>vilāsa</s>.
As the Lord of <s>Parama-vyoma</s> (the supreme sky) is considered in relation to <s>Govinda</s>,
and <s>Vāsudeva</s> is such in relation to the Lord of <s>Parama-vyoma</s>.
The <s>svāṃśa</s> (personal expansion):

children.text: tādṛśo nyūna-śaktiḥ yo vyanakti svāṃśa īritaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is similar but manifests lesser power is called the <s>svāṃśa</s> (personal expansion) —
such as <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and others, <s>Matsya</s> (the Fish) and others, in their respective abodes.
Of these, the <s>āveśa</s> (empowered incarnation):
Those in whom <s>Janārdana</s> enters by a portion of His knowledge-power (<s>jñāna-śakti</s>) and the like —

children.text: ta āveśā nigadyante jīvā eva mahattamāḥ // Lbh_1,1.18 //
children.translated_text: they are called <s>āveśas</s> (empowered ones); they are indeed <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) who are the greatest.
In <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> too, such as <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and the <s>Sanaka</s> brothers;
and these are also proclaimed in the Tenth Canto, in the example of <s>Akrūra</s>'s vision.
Thus the threefold distinction.

children.text: prakāśas tu na bhedeṣu gaṇyate sa hi no pṛthak // Lbh_1,1.20 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prakāśa</s> (manifestation), however, is not counted among the distinctions, for it is not separate.
And thus:
The simultaneous manifestation of one single form in many places —

children.text: sarvathā tat-svarūpaiva sa prakāśa itīryate // Lbh_1,1.21 //
children.translated_text: being entirely identical to His own form in every way — that is called <s>prakāśa</s> (manifestation).
As <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was directly visible in <s>Dvārakā</s>, in every palace —

children.text: citra bataitad ity ādi-pramāṇena sa setsyati // Lbh_1,1.22 //
children.translated_text: by the evidence beginning with 'How wonderful is this!' — that will be established.
Even when He sometimes assumes a four-armed form, He does not abandon His <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-nature;

children.text: ataḥ prakāśa eva syāt tasyāsau dvibhujasya ca // Lbh_1,1.23 //
children.translated_text: therefore, that too is merely a <s>prakāśa</s> (manifestation), even of His two-armed form.
That these abodes are beyond the material world (<s>prapañcātīta-dhāma</s>) is,
in scriptures of various kinds, including the <s>Uttara-khaṇḍa</s> of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, clearly evident.
Thus ends the determination of the <s>tattva</s> of <s>Bhagavān</s> characterized by <s>svayaṃrūpa</s>, <s>vilāsa</s>, <s>svāṃśa</s>, <s>āveśa</s>, and <s>prakāśa</s>. ||1||
Second Section
Determination of <s>puruṣāvatāras</s> (puruṣa incarnations) and <s>guṇāvatāras</s> (guṇa incarnations).

children.text: athāvatārāḥ kathyante kṛṣṇo yeṣu ca puṣkalāḥ // Lbh_1,2.1 //
children.translated_text: Now the incarnations (<s>avatāras</s>) are described, in whom <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is fully (<s>puṣkala</s>) present.
Their definition:

children.text: pūrvoktā viśva-kāryārthaṃ apūrvā iva cet svayam |
children.translated_text: The aforementioned forms, if for the sake of cosmic duties, as if appearing anew,

children.text: dvārāntareṇa vāviḥsyur avatārās tadā smṛtāḥ // Lbh_1,2.2 //
children.translated_text: whether directly or through another medium — they are then called <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations).

children.text: tac ca dvāraṃ tad-ekātma-rūpas tad-bhakta eva ca |
children.translated_text: And that medium is either a <s>tad-ekātma-rūpa</s> (form identical in essence) or His devotee —
as for example <s>Śeṣaśāyī</s> (the one lying on <s>Śeṣa</s>) and <s>Vasudeva</s> and others.

children.text: puruṣākhyā guṇātmano līlātmānaś ca te tridhā // Lbh_1,2.4 //
children.translated_text: They are of three kinds: named <s>puruṣa</s> (cosmic person), <s>guṇātma</s> (presiding over the <s>guṇas</s>), and <s>līlātma</s> (of pastimes).

children.text: prāyaḥ svāṃśās tathāveśā avatārā bhavanty amī |
children.translated_text: These <s>avatāras</s> are generally <s>svāṃśas</s> (personal expansions) or <s>āveśas</s> (empowered incarnations);

children.text: atra yaḥ syāt svayaṃrūpaḥ so'gre vyaktībhaviṣyati // Lbh_1,2.5 //
children.translated_text: herein, whichever may be the <s>svayaṃrūpa</s> (original form) will be manifest hereafter.
He who, though one alone, yet by modifications of His form-divisions, experiences the qualities in manifold ways,
though pure, appears as if impure,
endowed with knowledge, the maker of all existential powers —
to that <s>Puruṣa</s>, eternally imperishable, I bow!
Of these, the definition of the <s>puruṣa</s>, as in the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> (6.8.61):
Thus.

children.text: tasyaivānupūrvoktāt parameśvarāt samanantaram iti svāmī // Lbh_1,2.6 //
children.translated_text: 'Of that same' — meaning immediately after the aforementioned <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord) — thus the commentator (<s>Svāmī</s>).
Here the verse summary:
He who, being a partial form of <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord), appears as if possessing the primary <s>guṇas</s>,
whose acts include 'glancing' (<s>īkṣā</s>) and the like, who is the source of many <s>avatāras</s> — He is known as <s>puruṣa</s>.
'The first <s>avatāra</s> of the Supreme is the <s>puruṣa</s>.'
That He is an <s>avatāra</s> is stated in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, Second Canto:
His varieties, as stated in the <s>Sātvata Tantra</s>:

children.text: viṣṇos tu trīṇi rūpāṇi puruṣākhyāny atho viduḥ |
children.translated_text: Three forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s> are known, called <s>puruṣa</s>:

children.text: ekaṃ tu mahataḥ sraṣṭṛ dvitīyaṃ tantu-saṃsthitam |
children.translated_text: one is the creator of the <s>mahat</s> (cosmic intelligence), the second is situated within the cosmic thread (<s>tantu</s>),
the third dwells in all beings — knowing these, one is liberated.
Thus.
With the five elements self-created,
having fashioned the universal city (<s>virāj</s>), therein
entering by His own portion (<s>svāṃśa</s>), He who obtained the designation <s>puruṣa</s> —
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the primordial deity.
Of these, the first, as stated in the Eleventh Canto [<s>BhP</s> 11.4.3]:

children.text:
brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ [5.10-13] ca -
tasminn āvirabhūl liṅge mahā-viṣṇur jagat-patiḥ ||
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> [5.10-13]:
'In that <s>liṅga</s> (cosmic form), <s>Mahā-viṣṇu</s>, the Lord of the universe, manifested' —
beginning with 'The <s>Puruṣa</s> of a thousand heads' —

children.text: nārāyaṇaḥ sa bhagavān āpas tasmāt sanātanāt |
children.translated_text: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the waters from that eternal one,
manifested as the causal ocean (<s>kāraṇārṇa</s>), of the nature of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>;

children.text: yoga-nidrāṃ gatas tasmin sahasrāṃśaḥ svayaṃ mahān ||
children.translated_text: He entered <s>yoganidrā</s> (mystic sleep) therein, being Himself great, with a thousand-fold portion.'

children.text:
tad-roma-bila-jāleṣu bījaṃ saṅkarṣaṇasya ca |
haimāny aṇḍāni jātāni mahā-bhūtāvṛtāni tu || īty etad antam // Lbh_1,2.11 //
children.translated_text:
'In the networks of the pores of His body, the seeds of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>,
golden eggs were born, covered by the great elements.' — up to this.
The <s>liṅga</s> here is stated to be a limb-division of the <s>svayaṃrūpa</s> (original form).

children.text: pratyaṇḍam evam ekāṃśād viśati svayam // Lbh_1,2.13 //
children.translated_text: 'Into each cosmic egg, He enters by one portion of Himself.'
The second, as stated there [<s>BrS</s> 5.14], immediately after:
Thus.
The one lying in the ocean of the cosmic womb (<s>garbhodakaśāyī</s>), the lotus-naveled one, is <s>Aniruddha</s>;
thus it is stated in the <s>Nārāyaṇopākhyāna</s> of the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>;
He is the controller of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> being in the state of <s>Pradyumna</s>.

children.text: atha yat tu tṛtīyaṃ syād rūpaṃ tac cāpy adṛśyata |
children.translated_text: Now the third form — that too appeared;
some say 'within His own body' — from the verse of the Second Canto.
Now the <s>guṇāvatāras</s> (incarnations presiding over the <s>guṇas</s>) are described; from the <s>puruṣa</s> here:

children.text: viṣṇur brahmā ca rudraś ca sthiti-sargādi-karmaṇe // Lbh_1,2.16 //
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> — for the purposes of maintenance, creation, and so on.

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tama iti prakṛter guṇās tair
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, <s>tamas</s> — the <s>guṇas</s> of <s>prakṛti</s> (material nature); endowed with these,
the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, though one alone, assumes here
the designations <s>Hari</s>, <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā), and <s>Hara</s> — for maintenance and the like;

children.text: śreyāṃsi tatra khalu sattva-tanor nṝṇāṃ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: of these, the auspicious fruits for people come from Him whose body is of <s>sattva</s>.
As stated in the First Canto (1.2.23):
Thus.
Here the verse summary:
Connection (<s>yoga</s>) with the <s>guṇas</s> is said to be in the capacity of controller (<s>niyāmakatā</s>);

children.text: ataḥ sa tair na yujyate tatra svāṃśaḥ parasya yaḥ // Lbh_1,2.18 //
children.translated_text: therefore, He is not actually conjoined with them — there, that one is a <s>svāṃśa</s> (personal expansion) of the Supreme.
Of these, <s>Brahmā</s>:
<s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, the subtle one here; the gross one is called <s>Vairāja</s>;

children.text: bhogāya sṛṣṭaye cābhūt padmabhūr iti sa dvidhā // Lbh_1,2.19 //
children.translated_text: He became <s>Padmabhū</s> (lotus-born) — thus twofold, for enjoyment and for creation.

children.text: vairāja eva prāyaḥ syāt sargādy-arthaṃ caturmukhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The four-faced one is generally the <s>Vairāja</s> alone, for the purpose of creation and the like;

children.text: kadācid bhagavān viṣṇur brahmā san sṛjati svayam // Lbh_1,2.20 //
children.translated_text: sometimes <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s> Himself, being <s>Brahmā</s>, creates.
And thus in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: bhavet kvacin mahākalpe brahmā jīvo'py upāsanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: In some great cosmic cycles (<s>mahākalpa</s>), <s>Brahmā</s> is a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) elevated by worship;

children.text: kvacid atra mahāviṣṇur brahmatvaṃ pratipadyate // Lbh_1,2.21 //
children.translated_text: in some, <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s> Himself assumes the role of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Thus.

children.text: viṣṇur yatra mahā-kalpe sraṣṭṛtvaṃ ca prapadyate |
children.translated_text: In those great cycles where <s>Viṣṇu</s> assumes the role of creator,

children.text: tatra bhuṅkte taṃ praviśya vairājaḥ saukhya-sampadam |
children.translated_text: there, the <s>Vairāja</s>, entering into Him, enjoys the wealth of bliss;

children.text: ato jīvatvam aiśyaṃ ca brahmaṇaḥ kāla-bhedataḥ // Lbh_1,2.22 //
children.translated_text: therefore, <s>Brahmā</s>'s status as <s>jīva</s> or as Lord varies according to the cosmic age.
In view of his lordship, his <s>avatāra</s>-status is declared in the scriptures;
by virtue of his collective nature (<s>samaṣṭitva</s>), he is said to be close to <s>Bhagavān</s>;
his <s>avatāra</s>-status is regarded by some as <s>āveśa</s> (empowered incarnation) and by others differently.
Just as the sun manifests its own radiance to some degree

children.text: svīyam kiyat prakaṭayaty api tadvad atra |
children.translated_text: in its own gem-fragments, similarly here —
this <s>Brahmā</s>, who is the architect of the cosmic egg,

children.text: govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi // Lbh_1,2.24 //
children.translated_text: I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Thus in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.49):
Thus.

children.text: kadācit śrūyate nīrāt tejovātādikād api // Lbh_1,2.25 //
children.translated_text: sometimes it is heard to be from water, from light, from wind, and so on.
His birth is from the lotus sprung from the navel of the one lying in the cosmic waters (<s>Garbhodaśāyī</s>);
<s>Rudra</s> has an eleven-fold array (<s>vyūha</s>), and also eight forms (<s>aṣṭatanu</s>);

children.text: prāyaḥ pañcānanas tryakṣo daśa-bāhur udīryate // Lbh_1,2.26 //
children.translated_text: he is generally described as five-faced, three-eyed, with ten arms.
Occasionally, the special <s>jīva</s>-nature of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) is stated, as in the case of <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā);

children.text: tat tu śeṣavad evāstāṃ tad-aṃśatvena kīrtanāt // Lbh_1,2.27 //
children.translated_text: but let that stand as in the case of <s>Śeṣa</s>, since he is also celebrated as a portion of the Supreme.

children.text: haraḥ puruṣa-dhāmatvān nirguṇaḥ prāya eva saḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hara</s>, by virtue of being an abode of the <s>puruṣa</s>, is generally beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>nirguṇa</s>);
here, he is perceived by all as subject to modification, due to his association with <s>tamas</s>.

children.text: śivaḥ śakti-yutaḥ śaśvat triliṅgo guṇa-saṃvṛtaḥ // Lbh_1,2.28 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Śiva</s>, united with <s>śakti</s>, ever bearing the three attributes (<s>triliṅga</s>), enveloped by the <s>guṇas</s>.'
As stated in the Tenth Canto (<s>BhP</s> 10.88.3):
Thus.
Just as milk becomes yogurt through a special transformation,

children.text: sañjāyate na hi tataḥ pṛthag asti hetoḥ |
children.translated_text: and yet does not exist separately from its cause —

children.text: yaḥ śambhutām api tathā samupaiti kāryād
children.translated_text: He who similarly assumes the state of <s>Śambhu</s> for the purpose of a task —
I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>.
As in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.45):
Thus.
His birth is sometimes from the forehead of <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), sometimes from the Lord of <s>Kamalā</s> (Viṣṇu);

children.text: kālāgni-rudraḥ kalpānte bhavet saṅkarṣaṇād api // Lbh_1,2.30 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kālāgni-Rudra</s> at the end of the cosmic cycle (<s>kalpa</s>) arises also from <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>.
The form called <s>Sadāśiva</s>, devoid of even a trace of <s>tamas</s>,
being the cause of everything, is a limb of the Lord Himself;
this same is shown in <s>Śivaloka</s> in the <s>Vāyavya</s> and other Purāṇas.
And thus in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>, in the description of the primordial <s>Śiva</s> (5.8):

children.text: niyatiḥ sā ramā devi tat-priyā tad-vaśaṃ tadā |
children.translated_text: '<s>Niyati</s> (fate) is she, <s>Ramā</s> the goddess, His beloved, under His control;
His emblem (<s>liṅga</s>) is <s>Bhagavān Śambhu</s>, of luminous form, eternal;

children.text: yā yoniḥ sāparā śaktiḥ ity ādi // Lbh_1,2.32 //
children.translated_text: and that which is the source (<s>yoni</s>) is the supreme power (<s>śakti</s>)' — and so on.

children.text: tal loka-padmaṃ sa u eva viṣṇuḥ
children.translated_text: That cosmic lotus — He, <s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself,
entered, illuminating all qualities;
therein, the self-born (<s>Svayambhū</s>) creator, consisting of the <s>Vedas</s>,
whom they call <s>Svayambhū</s> — He came to be.
<s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>, as stated in the Third Canto (3.8.16):
Thus.

children.text: yo viṣṇuḥ paṭhyate so'sau kṣīrāmbudhiśayo mataḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Viṣṇu</s> who is recited here is understood to be the one lying in the ocean of milk (<s>Kṣīrābdhiśāyī</s>);
He, being a <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime expansion) of <s>Garbhodaśāyī</s>, is thus stated by the sages;

children.text: nārāyaṇo virāḍ antaryāmī cāyaṃ nigadyate // Lbh_1,2.34 //
children.translated_text: He is called <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the <s>Virāṭ</s> (cosmic form), and the <s>Antaryāmī</s> (inner controller). || Lbh 1.2.34 ||
The abodes (<s>puras</s>) of the manifestations of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which are described in the <s>Viṣṇu-dharmottara</s> and other texts as existing within the cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa</s>),

children.text: santi viṣṇu-prakāśānāṃ tāḥ kathyante samāsataḥ // Lbh_1,2.35 //
children.translated_text: Are described here in brief. || Lbh 1.2.35 ||
As follows —
Above <s>Rudra</s>'s realm, at a distance of fifty thousand [<s>yojanas</s>],
Inaccessible to all worlds, the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is proclaimed. || Lbh 1.2.36 ||
Above that is the shell of <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (the cosmic egg), endowed with golden brilliance.

children.text: meros tu pūrva-dig-bhāge madhye tu lavaṇodadheḥ |
children.translated_text: To the east of <s>Meru</s>, in the middle of the salt ocean,
The great abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is said to be situated within the waters. || Lbh 1.2.37 ||
There the God of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>, sleeps on the warm waters,
Ever accompanied by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, resting on the couch of <s>Śeṣa</s>. || Lbh 1.2.38 ||

children.text: meroś ca pūrva-dig-bhāge madhye kṣīrārṇavasya ca |
children.translated_text: To the east of <s>Meru</s> and in the middle of the ocean of milk,

children.text: kṣīrāmbu-madhyagā śubhrā devasyānyā tathā purī // Lbh_1,2.39 //
children.translated_text: There is another resplendent city of the Lord, situated within the milk-waters. || Lbh 1.2.39 ||
The Lord dwells there accompanied by <s>Lakṣmī</s>, seated on the throne of <s>Śeṣa</s>;

children.text: tatrāpi caturo māsān suptas tiṣṭhati vārṣikān // Lbh_1,2.40 //
children.translated_text: Even there He sleeps for four months during the rainy season. || Lbh 1.2.40 ||

children.text: tasminn avāci dig-bhāge madhye kṣīrārṇavasya tu |
children.translated_text: In the southern quarter of that, in the middle of the ocean of milk,
Twenty-five thousand <s>yojanas</s> in circumference,
Is the supremely beautiful island known as <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (White Island). || Lbh 1.2.41 ||
The people there have the radiance of the sun and the appearance of the cool-rayed moon;

children.text: tejasā durnirīkṣyāś ca devānām api yādava // Lbh_1,2.42 //
children.translated_text: They are difficult to behold even for the gods due to their brilliance, O <s>Yādava</s>. || Lbh 1.2.42 ||
And in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> Purāṇa —

children.text: śveto nāma mahān asti dvīpaḥ kṣīrābdhi-veṣṭitaḥ |
children.translated_text: There is a great island called <s>Śveta</s>, encircled by the ocean of milk,
A hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent, most delightful, entirely golden. || Lbh 1.2.43 ||
With heaps of rolling waves resembling jasmine, moonlight, and white lotuses,
Endowed with spotless rocky shores washed by the ocean of milk on all sides. || Lbh 1.2.44 ||
Thus.

children.text: kiṃ ca viṣṇu-purāṇādau mokṣa-dharme ca kīrtitam |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, it is proclaimed in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> and elsewhere, and in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>,

children.text: kṣīrābdher uttare tīre śveta-dvīpo bhaved iti // Lbh_1,2.45 //
children.translated_text: That <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> lies on the northern shore of the ocean of milk. || Lbh 1.2.45 ||

children.text: śuddhodād uttare śvetadvīpaṃ syāt pādma-sammatam // Lbh_1,2.46 //
children.translated_text: North of <s>Śuddhodā</s>, <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> would be — this is accepted in the <s>Padma</s> Purāṇa. || Lbh 1.2.46 ||

children.text: viṣṇuḥ sattvaṃ tanotīti śāstre sattva-tanuṃ smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> extends <s>sattva</s> (goodness), hence He is known in the scriptures as having a <s>sattva</s>-body;
His group of incarnations (<s>avatāras</s>) also have <s>sattva</s>-bodies;

children.text: bahiraṅgam adhiṣṭhānam iti vā tasya tat tanuḥ // Lbh_1,2.47 //
children.translated_text: Or, His external presiding form — that is His body. || Lbh 1.2.47 ||

children.text: ato nirguṇatā samyak sarva-śāstre prasidhyati // Lbh_1,2.48 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, His transcendence to the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature) is properly established in all scriptures. || Lbh 1.2.48 ||
As stated in <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, Tenth Canto (10.88.4) —

children.text: harir hi nirguṇaḥ sākṣāt puruṣaḥ prakṛteḥ paraḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> is directly <s>nirguṇa</s> (beyond material qualities), the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature);

children.text: sa sarva-dṛg upadraṣṭā taṃ bhajan nirguṇo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: He is the all-seeing witness (<s>upadraṣṭā</s>) — by worshipping Him, one becomes <s>nirguṇa</s>.

children.text: tena sattva-tanor asmāt śreyāṃsi syur itīritam // Lbh_1,2.50 //
children.translated_text: Therefore it is said that from this <s>sattva</s>-bodied Lord arise all auspicious things. || Lbh 1.2.50 ||

children.text: ity ato vihitā śāstre tad-bhakter eva nityatā // Lbh_1,2.51 //
children.translated_text: Hence devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to Him alone is enjoined as eternal in the scriptures. || Lbh 1.2.51 ||
As stated in the <s>Padma</s> Purāṇa —

children.text: smartavyaḥ satataṃ viṣṇur vismartavyo na jātucit |
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s> is always to be remembered, never to be forgotten;

children.text: sarve vidhi-niṣedhāḥ syur etayor eva kiṅkarāḥ // Lbh_1,2.52 //
children.translated_text: All injunctions and prohibitions are servants of these two [principles]. || Lbh 1.2.52 ||

children.text: vyāmohāya carācarasya jagatas te te purāṇāgamās
children.translated_text: Let the various <s>Purāṇas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s> proclaim until the end of the <s>kalpa</s>

children.text: tāṃ tām eva hi devatāṃ paramikāṃ jalpantu kalpāvadhi |
children.translated_text: This or that deity as supreme, for the bewilderment of the moving and stationary world;

children.text: siddhānte punar eka eva bhagavān viṣṇuḥ samastāgama-
children.translated_text: But in the final conclusion, it is <s>Bhagavān Viṣṇu</s> alone who is ascertained
When all scriptural enterprises are subjected to discriminating analysis. || Lbh 1.2.53 ||
And therefore in that same text (<s>Padma Purāṇa</s> 4.93.26) —
<s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, First Canto (1.2.26) —
Those who seek liberation, abandoning the fearsome lords of beings (<s>bhūtapatis</s>),
Worship the peaceful <s>kalās</s> (portions) of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, being free from envy.

children.text: atra svāṃśā harer eva kalā-śabdena kīrtitāḥ // Lbh_1,2.55 //
children.translated_text: Here, by the word '<s>kalā</s>' (portion), the <s>svāṃśas</s> (own expansions) of <s>Hari</s> are indicated. || Lbh 1.2.55 ||
Therefore, the inferiority of all celestials — <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), and others —
Compared to the <s>svāṃśa</s>-expansions of <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s> is demonstrated. || Lbh 1.2.56 ||
Offered with worship by <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) to the world,
Purifies along with <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>); who else other than <s>Mukunda</s>
Is in this world worthy of the designation '<s>Bhagavat</s>' (divine)? || Lbh 1.2.57 ||

As stated in the same text (1.18.21) —
Moreover, the water emanating from the nails of His feet,
Thus.
And in the <s>Mahāvārāha</s> Purāṇa —
The Fish, Tortoise, Boar, and other [incarnations] are equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, being non-different from Him;

children.text: brahmādyām asamāḥ proktāḥ prakṛtis tu samāsamā // Lbh_1,2.58 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and others are declared unequal; and <s>Prakṛti</s> is both equal and unequal. || Lbh 1.2.58 ||
Thus.
Here, by the word '<s>Prakṛti</s>' is meant the <s>cit-śakti</s> (spiritual potency);
Since she has both identical and distinct forms, she is called 'equal and unequal.' || Lbh 1.2.59 ||
Thus ends the examination of the <s>Puruṣāvatāra</s> and <s>Guṇāvatāra</s>. ||2||
Third Chapter.
Examination of the <s>Līlāvatāras</s> (Pastime Incarnations).

children.text: atha līlāvatārāś ca vilikhyante yathā mati |
children.translated_text: Now the <s>Līlāvatāras</s> are described according to [my] understanding,
Following primarily the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>. || Lbh 1.3.1 ||
Among them, <s>Śrī Catuḥsana</s> (the Four Kumāras) — in the First Canto (1.3.6) —

children.text: sa eva prathamaṃ devaḥ kaumāraṃ sargam āśritaḥ |
children.translated_text: That very Lord, first assuming the creation of the <s>Kumāras</s>,

children.text: cacāra duścaraṃ brahmā brahmacaryam akhaṇḍitam // Lbh_1,3.2 //
children.translated_text: Practiced difficult, unbroken <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy). || Lbh 1.3.2 ||
Thus.

children.text: caturbhir avatāro'yam eka eva satāṃ mataḥ |
children.translated_text: This incarnation of four [Kumāras] is considered by the pious as a single entity;

children.text: sama-śabdāt caturṣv eva catuḥsana iti smṛtaḥ // Lbh_1,3.3 //
children.translated_text: Due to the word '<s>sama</s>' (equal), applied to the four, he is known as <s>Catuḥsana</s>. || Lbh 1.3.3 ||
He descended for the propagation of pure knowledge (<s>śuddha-jñāna</s>) and devotion (<s>bhakti</s>);
With the appearance of five or six-year-old boys, golden, born from the lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>). || Lbh 1.3.4 ||
<s>Śrī Nārada</s> — in the same text (1.3.8) —

children.text: tṛtīyam ṛṣi-sargaṃ vai devarṣitvam upetya saḥ |
children.translated_text: In the third creation, the sage-creation, having assumed the state of a divine sage (<s>devarṣi</s>),

children.text: tantraṃ sātvatam ācaṣṭa naiṣkarmyaṃ karmaṇāṃ yataḥ // Lbh_1,3.5 //
children.translated_text: He taught the <s>Sātvata Tantra</s>, from which comes freedom from [binding] action (<s>naiṣkarmya</s>). || Lbh 1.3.5 ||
For the propagation everywhere in this world of devotion to Himself,

children.text: harir devarṣi-rūpeṇa candra-śubhro vidher abhūt // Lbh_1,3.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, in the form of the divine sage, moon-white, became the son of <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>). || Lbh 1.3.6 ||

children.text: āvirbhūyād idme brāhme kalpa eva catuḥsanaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Catuḥsana</s> appears in this present <s>Brāhma Kalpa</s> alone,

children.text: nāradaś cānuvartete kalpeṣu sakaleṣv api // Lbh_1,3.7 //
children.translated_text: While <s>Nārada</s> continues in all <s>kalpas</s> without exception. || Lbh 1.3.7 ||
<s>Śrī Varāha</s> — in the same text (1.3.7) —
For the second creation, to uplift the earth which had gone to <s>Rasātala</s> (the netherworld),

children.text: uddhariṣyann upādatta yajñeśaḥ saukaraṃ vapuḥ // Lbh_1,3.8 //
children.translated_text: The Lord of sacrifices (<s>Yajñeśa</s>) assumed the body of a boar. || Lbh 1.3.8 ||
When He arose to lift the surface of the earth, bearing
The boar-form, which was the embodiment of all sacrifices, the infinite One —
The primeval demon who had come within the great ocean,

children.text: taṃ daṃṣṭrayādrim iva vajra-dharo dadāra // Lbh_1,3.9 //
children.translated_text: Him He tore with His tusk like a mountain, as <s>Vajradhara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) [strikes with his bolt]. || Lbh 1.3.9 ||
And in the Second Canto (2.7.1) —
Thus.
He appeared twice in this <s>kalpa</s>: first, in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> period (<s>manvantara</s>),

children.text: ghrāṇād vidher dharoddhṛtyai cākṣuṣīye tu nīrataḥ // Lbh_1,3.10 //
children.translated_text: From the nostrils of <s>Vidhi</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) for uplifting the earth; and in the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> period, from the waters. || Lbh 1.3.10 ||
The foremost of tusked beings, to slay <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> during the earth's upliftment —

children.text: catuṣpāt śrī-varāho'sau nṛ-varāhaḥ kvacin mataḥ // Lbh_1,3.11 //
children.translated_text: This <s>Śrī Varāha</s> was four-legged; sometimes he is considered <s>Nṛvarāha</s> (man-boar). || Lbh 1.3.11 ||
Sometimes dark as a rain-cloud, sometimes moon-white —
This sacrificial-formed (<s>Yajña-mūrti</s>), most massive one, is known as having two colors. || Lbh 1.3.12 ||
The creation by <s>Dakṣa</s>, son of the <s>Pracetas</s>, is heard of in the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> period;

children.text: atas tatraiva janmāsya hiraṇyākṣasya yujyate // Lbh_1,3.13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore the birth of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> in that very period is fitting. || Lbh 1.3.13 ||
As stated in the Fourth Canto (4.30.49) —

children.text: cākṣuṣe tv antare prāpte prāk-sarge kāla-vidrute |
children.translated_text: When the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> period arrived, in the prior creation when time had elapsed,

children.text: yaḥ sasarja prajā iṣṭāḥ sa dakṣo daiva-coditaḥ // Lbh_1,3.14 //
children.translated_text: It was <s>Dakṣa</s> who, impelled by the divine, created the desired progeny. || Lbh 1.3.14 ||
Thus.
In the lineage of <s>Uttānapāda</s>, as a son of the <s>Pracetases</s>,

children.text: dakṣasyaiva ditiḥ putrī hiraṇākṣo diteḥ sutaḥ // Lbh_1,3.15 //
children.translated_text: <s>Diti</s> was the daughter of that very <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was <s>Diti</s>'s son. || Lbh 1.3.15 ||

children.text: kalpārambhe tadā nāsti sutotpattir manor api |
children.translated_text: At the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>, at that time, there was not even the birth of <s>Manu</s>'s children;

children.text: kvāsau prācetaso dakṣaḥ kva ditiḥ kva diteḥ // Lbh_1,3.16 //
children.translated_text: Where then was <s>Dakṣa</s> the <s>Prācetasa</s>? Where was <s>Diti</s>? Where was <s>Diti</s>'s [son]? || Lbh 1.3.16 ||
Therefore, the exploits of <s>Śrī Varāha</s>, which arose at two different times,
Were narrated together by <s>Maitreya</s> in accordance with <s>Kṣattā</s>'s (<s>Vidura</s>'s) questions. || Lbh 1.3.17 ||

children.text: madhye manvantarasyaiva muneḥ śāpān manuṃ prati |
children.translated_text: In the middle of the <s>manvantara</s>, due to the sage's curse upon <s>Manu</s>,

children.text: pralayo'sau babhūveti purāṇe kvacid īryate // Lbh_1,3.18 //
children.translated_text: That dissolution occurred — so it is stated in some <s>Purāṇa</s>. || Lbh 1.3.18 ||
This was a sudden dissolution occurring during the <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s>'s period —

children.text: pralayaḥ padmanābhasya līlayeti ca kutracit // Lbh_1,3.19 //
children.translated_text: A <s>pralaya</s> (dissolution) brought about by the play of <s>Padmanābha</s> — so it is stated elsewhere. || Lbh 1.3.19 ||
At the end of every <s>manvantara</s>, dissolution certainly occurs;

children.text: viṣṇu-dharmottare tv etat mārkaṇḍeyena bhāṣitam // Lbh_1,3.20 //
children.translated_text: This is spoken by <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> in the <s>Viṣṇu-dharmottara</s>. || Lbh 1.3.20 ||
As follows —
When a <s>manvantara</s> is exhausted, the gods who are the lords of the <s>manvantara</s>
Ascend to <s>Maharloka</s> and remain there, free from impurity. || Lbh 1.3.21 ||

children.text: manuś ca saha śakreṇa devāś ca yadunandana |
children.translated_text: <s>Manu</s> together with <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and the gods, O joy of the <s>Yadus</s>,
Attain <s>Brahmaloka</s>, from which return is difficult. || Lbh 1.3.22 ||
The earth with its nether worlds — O <s>Vajra</s> — the great Lord in the form of water,

children.text: ūrmi-mālī mahāvegaḥ sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati // Lbh_1,3.23 //
children.translated_text: Garlanded with waves, of great velocity, covering everything, remains. || Lbh 1.3.23 ||

children.text: bhūrlokam āśritaṃ sarvaṃ tadā naśyati yādava |
children.translated_text: At that time, everything situated on <s>Bhūrloka</s> (the earth) is destroyed, O <s>Yādava</s>;

children.text: na vinaśyanti rājendra viśrutāḥ kula-parvatāḥ // Lbh_1,3.24 //
children.translated_text: But the famous principal mountains (<s>kulaparvatas</s>) are not destroyed, O great king. || Lbh 1.3.24 ||

children.text: naur bhūtvā tu tadā devī mahī yadu-kulodvaha |
children.translated_text: At that time, the goddess Earth, becoming a boat, O upholder of the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty,

children.text: dhārayaty atha bījāni sarvāṇy evāviśeṣataḥ // Lbh_1,3.25 //
children.translated_text: Carries all the seeds without distinction. || Lbh 1.3.25 ||

children.text: bhaviṣyaś ca manus tatra bhaviṣyā ṛṣayas tathā |
children.translated_text: The future <s>Manu</s>, and the future sages,

children.text: tiṣṭhanti rāja-śārdūla sapta te prathitā bhuvi // Lbh_1,3.26 //
children.translated_text: Remain there, O tiger among kings — those seven renowned on earth. || Lbh 1.3.26 ||
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, assuming the form of a fish, the Lord of the universe, becoming horned,

children.text: ākarṣati tu tāṃ nāvaṃ sthānāt sthānaṃ tu līlayā // Lbh_1,3.27 //
children.translated_text: Draws that boat from place to place in His play. || Lbh 1.3.27 ||
The Lord of the universe tethered the boat to the peak of <s>Himādri</s> (the Himālaya);

children.text: matsyas tv adṛśyo bhavati te ca tiṣṭhanti tatragāḥ // Lbh_1,3.28 //
children.translated_text: The Fish then became invisible, and they remained there. || Lbh 1.3.28 ||

children.text: kṛta-tulyaṃ tataḥ kālaṃ yāvat prakṣālanaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: For a time equal to the <s>Kṛta</s> [Yuga], until the cleansing is completed,

children.text: āpaḥ śamam atho yānti yathā-pūrvaṃ narādhipa |
children.translated_text: The waters subside to their former state, O lord of men;

children.text: ṛṣayaś ca manuś caiva sarvaṃ kurvanti te tadā // Lbh_1,3.29 //
children.translated_text: Then the sages and <s>Manu</s> carry out everything at that time. || Lbh 1.3.29 ||
Thus.

children.text: manor ante layo nāsti manave'darśi māyayā |
children.translated_text: There is no dissolution at the end of a <s>Manu</s>; it was shown to <s>Manu</s> by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s <s>māyā</s> —

children.text: viṣṇuneti bruvāṇais tu svābhir naiṣa manyate // Lbh_1,3.30 //
children.translated_text: Those who say this, with their own [arguments], are not accepted. || Lbh 1.3.30 ||
<s>Śrī Matsya</s> (the Fish incarnation) — in the First Canto (1.3.15) —
He assumed the form of a fish at the time of the flood at the end of the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> [Manu's period];

children.text: nāvy āropya mahī-mayyām apād vaivasvataṃ manum // Lbh_1,3.31 //
children.translated_text: Having placed <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> upon the boat together with the earth, He protected [him]. || Lbh 1.3.31 ||
The Fish, obtained by <s>Manu</s> at the end of the <s>yuga</s>,
The shelter of all living beings, made of earth,
Having received the <s>Vedic</s> paths scattered in the great fear into the waters

children.text: ādāya tatra vijahāra ha veda-mārgān // Lbh_1,3.32 //
children.translated_text: From my mouths, He sported there. || Lbh 1.3.32 ||
And in the Second Canto (2.7.22) —
And in the <s>Padma</s> Purāṇa —
Thus addressed by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (the Lord of the senses), the Supreme Lord,
Assuming the Fish form, entered the great ocean. || Lbh 1.3.33 ||
The Fish also appeared twice in this <s>kalpa</s>, like the Boar:

children.text: ādau svāyambhuvīyasya daityaṃ ghnann āharac chrutīḥ |
children.translated_text: First, during the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> [period], slaying the demon and retrieving the scriptures;

children.text: ante tu cākṣuṣīyasya kṛpāṃ satyavrate'karot // Lbh_1,3.34 //
children.translated_text: And at the end of the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> [period], showing grace to <s>Satyavrata</s>. || Lbh 1.3.34 ||
The latter half-verse describes the exploits of the first [appearance],

children.text: pūrva-sārdhena cāntyasya matsyo jñeyo varāhavat // Lbh_1,3.35 //
children.translated_text: And the first half-verse those of the latter — the Fish should be understood like the Boar. || Lbh 1.3.35 ||
This serves as an indication for other <s>manvantaras</s> as well;
From the <s>Viṣṇu-dharmottara</s>, fourteen appearances should be known. || Lbh 1.3.36 ||
<s>Śrī Yajña</s> — in the First Canto (1.3.22) —
Having attained the state of king of the gods, desiring to accomplish the work of the gods,

children.text: samudra-nigrahādīni cakre vīryāṇy ataḥ param // Lbh_1,3.37 //
children.translated_text: He performed heroic deeds such as the restraining of the ocean, and others thereafter. || Lbh 1.3.37 ||
Thus.
Because He removed the great suffering of the three worlds,

children.text: mātāmahena manunā harir ity api śabditaḥ // Lbh_1,3.38 //
children.translated_text: He was also called <s>Hari</s> by His maternal grandfather <s>Manu</s>. || Lbh 1.3.38 ||
<s>Śrī Nara-Nārāyaṇa</s> — in the same text (1.3.9) —
In the fourth creation of the portions of <s>Dharma</s>, becoming the sages <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,
He performed arduous austerities, endowed with self-pacification. || Lbh 1.3.39 ||
Thus.
In the scriptures, the two called <s>Hari</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are remembered as their brothers.

children.text: ebhir eko'vatāraḥ syāt caturbhiḥ sanakādivat // Lbh_1,3.40 //
children.translated_text: By these four, there would be one <s>avatāra</s> (incarnation), like <s>Sanaka</s> and the others. // Lbh_1,3.40 //
<s>Śrī Kapila</s> — in the same text (1.3.10):
The fifth, named <s>Kapila</s>, the lord of <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings), to <s>Āsuri</s> expounded
the <s>Sāṅkhya</s> system, the determination of the categories of reality, which had been lost to time. // Lbh_1,3.41 //
Thus.
He manifested from <s>Kardama</s> in <s>Devahūti</s>;
He was called <s>Kapila</s> by <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā) because of His tawny (<s>kapila</s>) complexion. // Lbh_1,3.42 //
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: kapilo vāsudevāṃśas tattvaṃ sāṅkhyaṃ jagāda ha |
children.translated_text: <s>Kapila</s>, a portion of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, taught the true <s>Sāṅkhya</s>,

children.text: brahmādibhyaś ca devebhyo bhṛgvādibhyas tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: to <s>Brahmā</s> and other gods, and to <s>Bhṛgu</s> and other sages,
and likewise to <s>Āsuri</s>, enriched with the meanings of all the <s>Vedas</s>. // Lbh_1,3.43 //
But another <s>Kapila</s> taught a <s>Sāṅkhya</s> that is contrary to all the <s>Vedas</s>,
to <s>��suri</s> — that false system, bolstered by specious reasoning. // Lbh_1,3.44 //
<s>Śrī Datta</s> — in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, Second Canto (2.7.4):
When <s>Atri</s> desired offspring, the Lord, pleased, said

children.text: datto mayāham iti yad bhagavān sa dattaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I am given (<s>datta</s>) by Me' — thus the Lord is called <s>Datta</s>;
those whose bodies were purified by the pollen of His lotus feet —
<s>Yadu</s>, <s>Haihaya</s> and others — attained the twofold <s>yoga-ṛddhi</s> (yogic perfection). // Lbh_1,3.45 //
And in the First Canto (<s>Śrī Prathame</s>, 1.3.11):
The sixth — He accepted the state of being <s>Atri</s>'s son, obtained through <s>Anasūyā</s>;
He taught <s>Ānvīkṣikī</s> (the science of inquiry) to <s>Alarka</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s> and others. // Lbh_1,3.46 //
In the <s>Śrī Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>, it is said that, having been entreated by <s>Anasūyā</s>, the wife of <s>Atri</s>,

children.text: prārthito bhagavān atrer apatyatvam upeyivān // Lbh_1,3.47 //
children.translated_text: the Lord accepted the state of being <s>Atri</s>'s son. // Lbh_1,3.47 //
As follows:
Having granted a boon to <s>Anasūyā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who pervades all worlds,
became the son of <s>Atri</s> in her, assuming a human form by His own will,
known as <s>Dattātreya</s>, adorned in the guise of an ascetic. // Lbh_1,3.48 //
<s>Śrī Hayaśīrṣā</s> (Hayagrīva) — in the Second Canto (2.7.11):
At my sacrifice, the Lord appeared in the form of <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> (Horse-Headed),
He Himself, the <s>Yajña-puruṣa</s> (personification of sacrifice), of golden hue,
embodiment of the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic metres) and of sacrifice, the Self of all deities —

children.text: vāco babhūvur uśatīḥ śvasato 'sya nastaḥ // Lbh_1,3.49 //
children.translated_text: beautiful hymns issued forth from His nostrils as He breathed. // Lbh_1,3.49 //
Thus.
Having manifested from the sacrificial fire, He slew the two <s>Dānavas</s> (demons), <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Kaiṭabha</s>,

children.text: hatvā prayānayad vedān punar vāgīśvarī-patiḥ // Lbh_1,3.50 //
children.translated_text: and restored the <s>Vedas</s> — the Lord of <s>Vāgīśvarī</s> (Sarasvatī). // Lbh_1,3.50 //
<s>Śrī Haṃsa</s> (the Divine Swan) — in the Second Canto (2.7.19):

children.text: tubhyaṃ ca nārada bhṛśaṃ bhagavān vivṛddha-
children.translated_text: To you, O <s>Nārada</s>, the Lord, well-pleased
by your greatly developed devotion, taught <s>Yoga</s>,
<s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), and the <s>Bhāgavata</s> teaching, the lamp illuminating the true nature of the Self —
which those who take refuge in <s>Vāsudeva</s> come to know directly. // Lbh_1,3.51 //
Thus.
Indicating 'I am capable of discerning everything,

children.text: iti vyañjann ayaṃ rāja-haṃso vyaktiṃ jalād gataḥ // Lbh_1,3.52 //
children.translated_text: as a <s>rājahaṃsa</s> (royal swan) separates milk from water,' He manifested from the water in visible form. // Lbh_1,3.52 //
<s>Śrī Dhruva-priya</s> (Beloved of Dhruva) — in the same text (2.7.8):
Pierced by the barbed words hurled by his co-mother in the presence of the king,
though a mere child, he went to the forest for austerities;
to him, who was singing His praises, the Lord, pleased, gave the <s>dhruva-gati</s> (the immovable station),

children.text: divyāḥ stuvanti munayo yad upary-adhastāt // Lbh_1,3.53 //
children.translated_text: which the divine sages praise, that which is above and below all. // Lbh_1,3.53 //
Thus.
Since the mention of the incarnation is in the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> period, and His name is not stated there,
and since <s>Yajña</s> and others are mentioned there,
by the evidence of elimination, He is known by the name <s>Pṛśni-garbha</s>;

children.text: hantāyam adrir ity ādau padye govardhanādrivat // Lbh_1,3.54 //
children.translated_text: just as in the verse beginning 'This is a mountain,' <s>Govardhana</s> mountain is meant. // Lbh_1,3.54 //
Similarly, in the Tenth Canto (10.3.32):

children.text: tvam eva pūrva-sarge 'bhūḥ pṛśniḥ svāyambhuve sati |
children.translated_text: You were <s>Pṛśni</s> in the previous creation during the <s>Svāyambhuva</s> period;
at that time, this one named <s>Sutapā</s> was the sinless <s>Prajāpati</s>;

children.text: ahaṃ suto vām abhavaṃ pṛśnigarbha iti smṛtaḥ // Lbh_1,3.55 //
children.translated_text: I became your son, known as <s>Pṛśnigarbha</s> (born from Pṛśni's womb). // Lbh_1,3.55 //
Thus.

children.text: asyātra caritānuktyā nāmānuktyā ca tatra vai |
children.translated_text: Since His deeds are not mentioned here and His name is not mentioned there,

children.text: parasparam apekṣitvād yuktā caikatra saṅgatiḥ // Lbh_1,3.56 //
children.translated_text: because they are mutually dependent, their identification at one place is fitting. // Lbh_1,3.56 //
If mere arrival constituted being an <s>avatāra</s> (incarnation),
then it would apply elsewhere too — one could designate it as one pleases. // Lbh_1,3.57 //
<s>Śrī Ṛṣabha</s> — in the First Canto (1.3.13):

children.text: aṣṭame merudevyāṃ tu nābher jāta urukramaḥ |
children.translated_text: The eighth — <s>Urukrama</s> (the great-strider) was born from <s>Nābhi</s> in <s>Merudevī</s>,
showing the path revered by all <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life) to the wise. // Lbh_1,3.58 //
The pure Lord, to make known the <s>dharma</s> of the <s>paramahaṃsas</s> (supreme renouncers),

children.text: vyakto guṇair variṣṭhatvād vikhyāta ṛṣabhākhyayā // Lbh_1,3.59 //
children.translated_text: became manifest, and due to His supreme excellence, became famous by the name <s>Ṛṣabha</s>. // Lbh_1,3.59 //
<s>Śrī Pṛthu</s> — in the same text (1.3.14):

children.text: ṛṣibhir yācito bheje navamaṃ pārthivaṃ vapuḥ |
children.translated_text: Requested by the sages, He assumed the ninth, a kingly body;

children.text: dugdhemām oṣadhīr viprās tenāyaṃ sa uśattamaḥ // Lbh_1,3.60 //
children.translated_text: O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, He milked this earth of its herbs — therefore He is the best of the desirable. // Lbh_1,3.60 //
Thus.
When the sages churned the left arm of <s>Vena</s>,
the great king <s>Pṛthu</s> manifested, with the luster of pure gold. // Lbh_1,3.61 //

children.text: ādye vyaktāḥ kumārādyāḥ pṛthv-antāś ca trayodaśa |
children.translated_text: In the First Canto, the thirteen from <s>Kumāra</s> to <s>Pṛthu</s> are made manifest;

children.text: keloamatsyau punar vyaktiṃ cākṣuṣīye tu jagmatuḥ // Lbh_1,3.62 //
children.translated_text: while <s>Matsya</s> (Fish) and <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise) came to manifestation in the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> <s>Manvantara</s>. // Lbh_1,3.62 //
Now, <s>Śrī Nṛsiṃha</s> (Man-Lion) — in the same text (1.3.18):
The fourteenth — assuming the form of <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, He tore apart the mighty lord of <s>Daityas</s> (demons)

children.text: dadāra karajair ūrāv erakāṃ kaṭa-kṛd yathā // Lbh_1,3.64 //
children.translated_text: on His lap with His nails, as one splits an <s>erakā</s> (reed) while making a mat. // Lbh_1,3.64 //
In the sixth <s>Manvantara</s>, before the churning of the ocean, <s>Nṛhari</s> (Man-Lion) was already established;

children.text: ataḥ prāg eṣa kūrmāder vyaktiṃ ṣaṣṭhe'ntare gataḥ // Lbh_1,3.65 //
children.translated_text: therefore, He preceded <s>Kūrma</s> and others and came to manifestation in the sixth <s>Manvantara</s>. // Lbh_1,3.65 //
<s>Śrī Kūrma</s> (Tortoise) — in the same text (1.3.16):
When the gods and demons were churning the ocean with <s>Mandara</s> mountain,

children.text: dadhre kamaṭha-rūpeṇa pṛṣṭha ekādaśe vibhuḥ // Lbh_1,3.66 //
children.translated_text: the all-pervading Lord bore it on His back in the form of a tortoise, in the eleventh <s>Manvantara</s>. // Lbh_1,3.66 //
Thus.

children.text: pādme proktaṃ dadhe kṣauṇīmayam evārthitaḥ suraiḥ |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> it is said: He bore the earth, requested by the gods.

children.text: śāstrāntare tu bhūdhārī kalpādau prakaṭo'bhavat // Lbh_1,3.67 //
children.translated_text: In another scripture, the Upholder of the earth became manifest at the beginning of the <s>kalpa</s>. // Lbh_1,3.67 //
<s>Śrī Dhanvantari</s> and <s>Mohinī</s> — in the same text (1.3.17):
The twelfth was <s>Dhanvantara</s>, and the thirteenth —

children.text: apāyayat surān anyān mohinyā mohayan striyā // Lbh_1,3.68 //
children.translated_text: He gave the gods their drink while deluding the others with <s>Mohinī</s>, the enchantress. // Lbh_1,3.68 //
Thus.

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe ca saptame cāyaṃ dvirāvirbhāvam āgataḥ // Lbh_1,3.69 //
children.translated_text: He appeared twice, in the sixth and seventh <s>Manvantaras</s>. // Lbh_1,3.69 //
Concerning <s>Śrī Dhanvantari</s>:
In the sixth <s>Manvantara</s>, from the churning of the ocean, He emerged holding the nectar-vessel,
two-armed, dark-complexioned, the originator of <s>Āyurveda</s>.
And in the seventh, in the same form, He became the son of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>. // Lbh_1,3.70 //
<s>Śrī Mohinī</s>:
He, the unconquered one, for the delusion of the <s>Daityas</s> (demons) and for the delight of <s>Dhurjaṭi</s> (Śiva),
appeared twice in the form of <s>Mohinī</s>. // Lbh_1,3.71 //

children.text: iti ṣaṣṭhe'tra catvāro nṛsiṃhāyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ // Lbh_1,3.72 //
children.translated_text: Thus, in the sixth <s>Manvantara</s>, four incarnations from <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> onward are proclaimed. // Lbh_1,3.72 //
<s>Śrī Vāmana</s> (the Dwarf) — in the same text (1.3.19):
The fifteenth — assuming the form of <s>Vāmana</s> (the Dwarf), He went to the sacrifice of <s>Bali</s>,
requesting three paces of land, desiring to reclaim heaven. // Lbh_1,3.73 //
Thus.
<s>Vāmana</s> manifested three times in this <s>kalpa</s>.
First, He went to the sacrifice of the <s>Dānava</s> lord <s>Vāskala</s>;

children.text: tato vaivasvatīye'smin dhundhor makham asau gataḥ |
children.translated_text: then, in this <s>Vaivasvata</s> period, He went to the sacrifice of <s>Dhundhu</s>;
born from <s>Kaśyapa</s> in <s>Aditi</s>, in the seventh <s>caturyuga</s> of this <s>Manvantara</s>;

children.text: pratigraha-kṛte jātās traya eva trivikramāḥ // Lbh_1,3.74 //
children.translated_text: three <s>Trivikramas</s> (striders of three worlds) were born for the purpose of receiving gifts. // Lbh_1,3.74 //
<s>Śrī Bhārgava</s> (Paraśurāma) — in the same text (1.3.20):
In the sixteenth incarnation, seeing the kings hostile to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

children.text: triḥ-sapta-kṛtvaḥ kupito niḥ-kṣatrām akaron mahīm // Lbh_1,3.75 //
children.translated_text: enraged, He rendered the earth devoid of <s>Kṣatriyas</s> twenty-one times. // Lbh_1,3.75 //
Thus.
Born from <s>Reṇukā</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>, fair-complexioned, He came to manifestation.

children.text: prāhuḥ saptadaśe kecid dvāviṃśe'nye caturyuge // Lbh_1,3.76 //
children.translated_text: Some say in the seventeenth <s>caturyuga</s>, others in the twenty-second. // Lbh_1,3.76 //
<s>Śrī Rāghavendra</s> (Rāma) — in the same text (1.3.22):
Having attained the state of a human king, with the desire to accomplish the gods' purpose,

children.text: samudra-nigrahādīni cakre vīryāṇy ataḥ param // Lbh_1,3.77 //
children.translated_text: He performed heroic deeds such as bridging the ocean and more. // Lbh_1,3.77 //
Thus.
Born from <s>Kausalyā</s> and <s>Daśaratha</s>, with the luster of fresh <s>dūrvā</s> (green grass) blades,
He appeared in <s>Tretā Yuga</s>, in the twenty-fourth <s>caturyuga</s>,

children.text: bharatena sumitrāyā nandanābhyāṃ ca saṃyutaḥ // Lbh_1,3.78 //
children.translated_text: accompanied by <s>Bharata</s> and the two sons of <s>Sumitrā</s>. // Lbh_1,3.78 //

children.text: asya śāstre trayo vyūhā lakṣmaṇaādyā amī smṛtāḥ |
children.translated_text: In scripture, His three <s>vyūhas</s> (emanations) are known as <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and the others.
<s>Bharata</s> here is dark like a dense cloud; <s>Saumitrī</s> (sons of Sumitrā) are of golden luster. // Lbh_1,3.79 //
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>Bharata</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s> are declared to be the <s>Śaṅkha</s> (conch) and <s>Cakra</s> (discus);

children.text: śrī-lakṣmaṇas tu tatraiva śeṣa ity abhiśabditaḥ // Lbh_1,3.80 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Lakṣmaṇa</s> is declared in the same text to be <s>Śeṣa</s>. // Lbh_1,3.80 //
<s>Śrī Vyāsa</s> — in the same text (1.3.21):
Then, as the seventeenth, He was born in <s>Satyavatī</s> from <s>Parāśara</s>;

children.text: cakre veda-taroḥ śākhā dṛṣṭvā puṃso 'lpa-medhasaḥ // Lbh_1,3.81 //
children.translated_text: He made branches of the tree of the <s>Vedas</s>, seeing that people were of limited intelligence. // Lbh_1,3.81 //
Thus.

children.text: dvaipāyano'smi vyāsānām iti śaurir yad ūcivān |
children.translated_text: Since <s>Śauri</s> (Kṛṣṇa) said 'Among <s>Vyāsas</s>, I am <s>Dvaipāyana</s>,'
therefore in the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> and others, he is described with special prominence. // Lbh_1,3.82 //
As stated (ViP 3.4.5; MBh 12.346.11):
Know <s>Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa</s> to be <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself;

children.text: ko hy anyaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣān mahābhārata-kṛd bhavet ||
children.translated_text: for who else but the lotus-eyed one could be the author of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>?
It is heard that <s>Apāntaratama</s> became <s>Dvaipāyana</s>.

children.text: kiṃ sāyujyaṃ gataḥ so'tra viṣṇv-aṃśaḥ so'pi vā bhavet |
children.translated_text: Did he attain <s>sāyujya</s> (absorption) with the Lord here, or was he too a portion of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?

children.text: tasmād āveśa evāyam iti kecid vadanti ca // Lbh_1,3.84 //
children.translated_text: Therefore some say that this is merely an <s>āveśa</s> (empowered incarnation). // Lbh_1,3.84 //
Now <s>Śrī Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — in the First Canto (1.3.23):
In the nineteenth and twentieth births, appearing in the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> dynasty,

children.text: rāma-kṛṣṇāv iti bhuvo bhagavān aharad bharam // Lbh_1,3.85 //
children.translated_text: the Lord, as <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, removed the burden of the earth. // Lbh_1,3.85 //
Thus.
<s>Śrī Rāma</s> (Balarāma):
He manifested through two mothers and from one father, <s>Vasudeva</s>;
He who is like the essence of a fresh rain-cloud, always dressed in dark blue garments. // Lbh_1,3.86 //

children.text: saṅkarṣaṇo dvitīyo yo vyūhaḥ rāmaḥ sa eva hi |
children.translated_text: <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, the second <s>vyūha</s> — He is indeed <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma);

children.text: pṛthvī-dhareṇa śeṣeṇa sambhūya vyaktim īyivān // Lbh_1,3.87 //
children.translated_text: combining with <s>Śeṣa</s> the earth-bearer, He came to manifestation. // Lbh_1,3.87 //

children.text: śeṣo dvidhā mahīdhārī śyyārūpaś ca śārṅgiṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s> is twofold: the earth-bearer and the couch-form of the bow-wielding Lord.
The earth-bearer, due to the empowerment (<s>āveśa</s>) of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, is considered <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>;
the couch-form similarly has the disposition of being His friend and servant. // Lbh_1,3.88 //
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>:
He manifested from His mother <s>Devakī</s> and His father <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (Vasudeva),
dark-complexioned, two-armed yet also four-armed. // Lbh_1,3.89 //
<s>Śrī Buddha</s> — in the same text (1.3.24):
Then, at the onset of <s>Kali</s> (age), for the delusion of the enemies of the gods,
<s>Buddha</s> by name, the son of <s>Añjanā</s>, will appear among the <s>Kīkaṭas</s>. // Lbh_1,3.90 //
Thus.
He manifested when two thousand years of <s>Kali</s> had passed;
His form is of pinkish complexion, two-armed, without a topknot. // Lbh_1,3.91 //

children.text: yadā sūtaḥ kathām āha tadā buddhasya bhāvitā |
children.translated_text: When <s>Sūta</s> narrated the account, <s>Buddha</s>'s manifestation was in the future tense;

children.text: adhunā vṛtta evāyaṃ dharmāraṇye yad udgataḥ // Lbh_1,3.92 //
children.translated_text: now this event has already occurred, since He arose in <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> (the Forest of Dharma). // Lbh_1,3.92 //
<s>Śrī Kalki</s> — in the same text (1.3.25):
Then, at the juncture of the <s>yugas</s> (ages), when kings have become like robbers,

children.text: janitā viṣṇu-yaśaso nāmnā kalkir jagat-patiḥ // Lbh_1,3.93 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kalki</s> by name, the lord of the world, will be born as the son of <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>. // Lbh_1,3.93 //
Thus.

children.text: pūrvaṃ manur daśaratho vasudevo'py asāv abhūt |
children.translated_text: Previously, <s>Manu</s> became <s>Daśaratha</s> and <s>Vasudeva</s>;

children.text: bhāvī viṣṇu-yaśās cāyam iti pādme prakīrtitam // Lbh_1,3.94 //
children.translated_text: and he will become <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s> — thus it is proclaimed in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>. // Lbh_1,3.94 //

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ kalkinas tasya brahmāṇḍe suṣṭhu varṇitam |
children.translated_text: The glory of <s>Kalki</s> is well described in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>.

children.text: kaiścit kalau kalau buddhaḥ syāt kalkī cety udīryate // Lbh_1,3.95 //
children.translated_text: Some say that in each <s>Kali</s> age, there will be a <s>Buddha</s> and a <s>Kalki</s>. // Lbh_1,3.95 //
These eight, from <s>Vāmana</s> onward, are described in the <s>Vaivasvata Manvantara</s>. // Lbh_1,3.96 //
These twenty-five are described as <s>kalpa-avatāras</s> (incarnations of the cosmic cycle),

children.text: pratikalpaṃ yataḥ prāyaḥ sakṛt prādurbhvaty amī // Lbh_1,3.97 //
children.translated_text: because they mostly manifest once per <s>kalpa</s>. // Lbh_1,3.97 //
Thus ends the determination of the <s>Līlāvatāras</s> (Pastime Incarnations). ||
Fourth Chapter: Now the <s>Manvantarāvatāras</s> (Incarnations of the Manvantara Periods)
The <s>Manvantarāvatāra</s> is mostly the manifestation of <s>Mukunda</s> among the gods

children.text: tat-sahāyo mukundasya prādurbhāvaḥ sureṣu yaḥ // Lbh_1,4.1 //
children.translated_text: as their ally, for the slaying of the enemies of <s>Indra</s>. // Lbh_1,4.1 //
When the designation of <s>kalpa-avatāra</s> is apt for <s>Yajña</s> and others, clearly,
Their status as <s>Manvantara-avatāras</s> (incarnations presiding over <s>Manu</s>-periods) is due to their protecting until the end of each respective <s>Manvantara</s>. (Lbh 1.4.2)
In the <s>Manvantaras</s>, beginning from the <s>Svāyambhuvīya</s>, in order,

children.text: avatārās tu yajñādyā bṛhad-bhānv-antimā matāḥ // Lbh_1,4.3 //
children.translated_text: the <s>avatāras</s> beginning with <s>Yajña</s> and ending with <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s> are recognized. (Lbh 1.4.3)

children.text: yajñas tu pūrvam evoktas tenātra na vilikhyate // Lbh_1,4.4 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yajña</s> has already been described earlier; therefore He is not written about here. (Lbh 1.4.4)
In the first, the <s>Svāyambhuvīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Yajña</s> —
As stated in the Eighth Canto (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.1.21-22):

children.text: ṛṣes tu vedaśirasas tuṣitā nāma patny abhūt |
children.translated_text: The wife of the sage <s>Vedaśiras</s> was named <s>Tuṣitā</s>;

children.text: tasyāṃ jajñe tato devo vibhur ity abhiviśrutaḥ // Lbh_1,4.5 //
children.translated_text: from her was born a god celebrated as <s>Vibhu</s>. (Lbh 1.4.5)
Eighty-eight thousand sages of firm vows
followed the vow of that one, who was a lifelong <s>brahmacārī</s> (celibate student) from boyhood. (Lbh 1.4.6)
Thus.
In the third, the <s>Auttamīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Satyasena</s> — (8.1.25-26):
From <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Sūnṛtā</s>, the Supreme Person (<s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Puruṣottama</s>),

children.text: satyasena iti khyāto jātaḥ satyavrataiḥ saha // Lbh_1,4.7 //
children.translated_text: known as <s>Satyasena</s>, was born, together with the <s>Satyavratas</s>. (Lbh 1.4.7)
He, with his companion <s>Satyajit</s>, slew the <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s> who had false vows and bad conduct,
who harmed living beings, and the hosts of <s>Bhūtas</s>. (Lbh 1.4.8)
Thus.
In the fourth, the <s>Tāmasīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Hari</s> (8.1.30):
There too the Lord was born from <s>Hariṇī</s> and <s>Harimedhas</s>,

children.text: harir ity āhṛto yena gajendro mocito grahāt // Lbh_1,4.9 //
children.translated_text: called <s>Hari</s>, by whom the king of elephants was liberated from the crocodile. (Lbh 1.4.9)
Thus.
He is always remembered in the morning by those devoted to righteous conduct,
<s>Hari</s>, the liberator of the lord of elephants, for the destruction of all misfortunes. (Lbh 1.4.10)
In the fifth, the <s>Raivatīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> (8.5.4-5):
<s>Vikuṇṭhā</s>, wife of <s>Śubhra</s>, together with the <s>Vaikuṇṭhas</s>, the best among the gods;

children.text: tayoḥ sva-kalayā jajñe vaikuṇṭho bhagavān svayam // Lbh_1,4.11 //
children.translated_text: from them, the Lord <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> Himself was born by His own <s>kalā</s> (potency). (Lbh 1.4.11)
<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, by whom the world honored by all worlds was established,
was prayed to by <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), the goddess, desiring His pleasure. (Lbh 1.4.12)
Thus.
The manifestation of the great <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> world, which is all-pervading and of imperishable nature,
its establishment above <s>Satya</s>(-loka) is what is called 'creation.' (Lbh 1.4.13)
In the sixth, the <s>Cākṣuṣīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Ajita</s> (BhP 8.5.9-10):
There too, from <s>Devasambhūti</s>, a son of <s>Vairāja</s> was born —

children.text: ajito nāma bhagavān aṃśena jagataḥ patiḥ // Lbh_1,4.14 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ajita</s> (the Unconquered) by name, the Lord, the master of the universe, by a portion of Himself. (Lbh 1.4.14)

children.text: payodhiṃ yena nirmathya surāṇāṃ sādhitā sudhā |
children.translated_text: By whom the ocean was churned and <s>sudhā</s> (nectar) was obtained for the gods;
Mount <s>Mandara</s>, whirling in the waters, was upheld in the form of a tortoise. (Lbh 1.4.15)
Thus.
In the seventh, the <s>Vaivasvatīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Vāmana</s> —
In the <s>Vaivasvata Manvantara</s>, the manifest <s>Vāmana</s> has already been described.

children.text: bhaviṣyāḥ sapta kathyante te sāvarṇyantarādiṣu // Lbh_1,4.16 //
children.translated_text: Seven future ones will now be told, in the <s>Sāvarṇya Manvantara</s> and others. (Lbh 1.4.16)
In the eighth, the <s>Sāvarṇanīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Sārvabhauma</s> (BhP 8.13.17):
From <s>Devaguhya</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the Lord known as <s>Sārvabhauma</s>;

children.text: sthānaṃ purandarād dhṛtvā balaye dāsyatīśvaraḥ // Lbh_1,4.17 //
children.translated_text: having taken the position from <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>), the Lord will give it to <s>Bali</s>. (Lbh 1.4.17)
Thus.
In the ninth, the <s>Dakṣa-Sāvarṇanīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s> (8.13.20):
From <s>Āyuṣmat</s> and <s>Ambudhārā</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, a <s>kalā</s> (potency) of the Lord,

children.text: bhavitā yena saṃrāddhāṃ tri-lokīṃ bhokṣyate 'dbhutaḥ // Lbh_1,4.18 //
children.translated_text: will be born — wondrous, by whom the three worlds, fully prosperous, will be enjoyed. (Lbh 1.4.18)
Thus.
In the tenth, the <s>Brahma-Sāvarṇanīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Viṣvaksena</s> (8.13.23):

children.text: viṣvakseno viṣūcyāṃ tu śambhoḥ sakhyaṃ kariṣyati |
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, born from <s>Viṣūcī</s>, will establish friendship with <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva),

children.text: jātaḥ svāṃśena bhagavān gṛhe viśvasṛjo vibhuḥ // Lbh_1,4.19 //
children.translated_text: the Lord, born by His own portion in the house of <s>Viśvasṛj</s>, all-pervading. (Lbh 1.4.19)
Thus.
In the eleventh, the <s>Dharma-Sāvarṇanīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Dharmasetu</s> (8.13.26):

children.text: āryakasya sutas tatra dharmasetur iti smṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Āryaka</s> there is remembered as <s>Dharmasetu</s>;

children.text: vaidhṛtāyāṃ harer aṃśas tri-lokīṃ dhārayiṣyati // Lbh_1,4.20 //
children.translated_text: born from <s>Vaidhṛtā</s>, a portion of <s>Hari</s>, he will sustain the three worlds. (Lbh 1.4.20)
Thus.
In the twelfth, the <s>Rudra-Sāvarṇanīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Sudhāmā</s> (8.13.29):
A portion of <s>Hari</s> named <s>Svadhāmā</s> will accomplish that <s>Manu</s>'s

children.text: antaraṃ satya-sahasaḥ sunṛtāyāḥ suto vibhuḥ // Lbh_1,4.21 //
children.translated_text: <s>Manvantara</s>, the all-pervading son of <s>Satyasahas</s> and <s>Sunṛtā</s>. (Lbh 1.4.21)
In the thirteenth, the <s>Deva-Sāvarṇanīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Yogeśvara</s> (8.13.32):
The son of <s>Devahotra</s>, the bestower of gifts to the lord of heaven,

children.text: yogeśvaro harer aṃśo bṛhatyāṃ sambhaviṣyati // Lbh_1,4.22 //
children.translated_text: <s>Yogeśvara</s>, a portion of <s>Hari</s>, will be born from <s>Bṛhatī</s>. (Lbh 1.4.22)
Thus.
In the fourteenth, the <s>Indra-Sāvarṇanīya Manvantara</s>, <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s> (8.13.35):
The son of <s>Satrāyaṇa</s>, <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s>, then <s>Hari</s>,
born from <s>Vitānā</s>, O great king, will extend the threads of ritual action. (Lbh 1.4.23)
Since <s>Yajña</s> and <s>Vāmana</s> have already been mentioned among these,
the <s>Manvantara-avatāras</s> are said to be twelve in number. (Lbh 1.4.24)
Thus ends the delineation of the <s>Manvantara-avatāras</s>.
Now the <s>Yuga-avatāras</s> (incarnations for the ages):
<s>Hari</s> is described by color and name: white in the <s>Satya-yuga</s>,

children.text: raktaḥ śyāmaḥ kramāt kṛṣṇas tretāyāṃ dvāpare kalau // Lbh_1,4.25 //
children.translated_text: red, dark, and black respectively in <s>Tretā</s>, <s>Dvāpara</s>, and <s>Kali</s>. (Lbh 1.4.25)
For the purpose of the specific modes of worship in the <s>Satya</s> and other <s>yugas</s>,
the <s>Manvantara-avatāra</s> descends in sequence. (Lbh 1.4.26)
The <s>avatāras</s> who ordain the manifestations for <s>Kalpas</s>, <s>Manvantaras</s>, and <s>Yugas</s>

children.text: avatārā ime tv eka-catvāriṃśad udīritāḥ // Lbh_1,4.27 //
children.translated_text: are declared to be forty-one in total. (Lbh 1.4.27)

children.text: vṛttā brāhmādayaḥ kalpāḥ pādmāntās te sahasraśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>Kalpas</s> beginning with <s>Brāhma</s> and ending with <s>Pādma</s> have passed, numbering thousands.

children.text: vartamānas tu kalpo'yaṃ śveta-vārāha ucyate // Lbh_1,4.28 //
children.translated_text: The present <s>Kalpa</s> is called <s>Śveta-Vārāha</s> (White Boar). (Lbh 1.4.28)
In the first creation of the <s>Brāhma Kalpa</s>, in the <s>Svāyambhuva Manvantara</s>,
<s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and others manifested; and from the <s>Cākṣuṣīya</s> onward, those described subsequently. (Lbh 1.4.29)

children.text: prāyaḥ svāyambhuvādyākhyāḥ kalpe kalpe bhavanty amī |
children.translated_text: Generally, these <s>Manus</s> with names beginning from <s>Svāyambhuva</s> recur in every <s>Kalpa</s>,

children.text: manavas te'vatārāś ca tathā yajñādi-nāmakāḥ // Lbh_1,4.30 //
children.translated_text: as do those <s>avatāras</s> with names beginning from <s>Yajña</s>. (Lbh 1.4.30)
Thus in the <s>Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara</s>, the question of <s>Śrī Rudra</s>:

children.text: ya ete bhavatā proktā manavaś ca caturdaśa |
children.translated_text: 'These fourteen <s>Manus</s> that you have described —

children.text: nityaṃ brahma-dine prāpte eta eva kramād dvija |
children.translated_text: do these very same ones always appear when each day of <s>Brahmā</s> arrives, in order, O twice-born?

children.text: bhavanty utānye dharmajña etaṃ me chindhi saṃśayam // Lbh_1,4.31 //
children.translated_text: Or are there others, O knower of <s>dharma</s>? Dispel this doubt of mine.' (Lbh 1.4.31)
The reply of <s>Śrī Mārkaṇḍeya</s>:

children.text: eta eva mahārāja manavaś ca caturdaśa |
children.translated_text: 'These very fourteen <s>Manus</s>, O great king,

children.text: kalpe kalpe tvayā jñeyā nātra kāryā vicāraṇā // Lbh_1,4.32 //
children.translated_text: should be known by you as recurring in every <s>Kalpa</s>; there is no need for deliberation here. (Lbh 1.4.32)

children.text: eka-rūpās tvayā proktā jñātavyāḥ sarva eva hi |
children.translated_text: Those you have described as being of one form — all of them should be understood thus;

children.text: kecit kiñcid vibhinnāś ca māyayā parameśituḥ // Lbh_1,4.33 //
children.translated_text: some differ slightly, by the <s>māyā</s> (illusory power) of the Supreme Lord.' (Lbh 1.4.33)
Thus.

children.text: avatārāś caturdhā syur āveśāḥ prābhavā api |
children.translated_text: The <s>avatāras</s> are fourfold: <s>āveśa</s> (empowered), <s>prābhava</s> (partial),

children.text: athaiva vaibhavāvasthāḥ parāvaasthāś ca tatra te // Lbh_1,4.34 //
children.translated_text: and also <s>vaibhava</s> (majestic) states and <s>para</s> (supreme) states — these are they. (Lbh 1.4.34)
Among these, the <s>āveśa-avatāras</s> (empowered incarnations) should be understood in the manner previously described.
Such as <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Devarṣi</s> (<s>Nārada</s>), <s>Veṇa</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Prabhāva</s>, and others. (Lbh 1.4.35)

children.text: āviṣṭo'bhūt kumāreṣu nārade ca harir vibhuḥ // Lbh_1,4.36 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, the all-pervading Lord, entered into the <s>Kumāras</s> and into <s>Nārada</s>. (Lbh 1.4.36)
As stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: āviveśa pṛthuṃ devaḥ śaṅkhī cakrī caturbhujaḥ // Lbh_1,4.37 //
children.translated_text: The God, bearing conch and discus, four-armed, entered into <s>Pṛthu</s>. (Lbh 1.4.37)
As stated there also:

children.text: āviṣṭo bhārgave cābhūd iti tatraiva kīrtitam // Lbh_1,4.38 //
children.translated_text: And He entered into <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>) — this too is proclaimed there. (Lbh 1.4.38)
Thus it is said:

children.text: etat te kathitaṃ devi jāmadagner mahātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This, O Goddess, has been told to you — the deeds of <s>Jāmadagni</s>'s son, the great soul,
who was an <s>avatāra</s> empowered by the <s>śakti</s> (energy) of the Lord who bears the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow.' (Lbh 1.4.39)
Thus.
The <s>āveśa</s> nature of <s>Kalki</s> too is seen in the <s>Viṣṇudharma</s>. (Lbh 1.4.40)
As stated:
'<s>Hari</s> is not seen in the <s>Kali</s> age assuming a visible form directly,

children.text: kṛtādiṣv iva tenaiva tri-yugaḥ paripaṭhyate // Lbh_1,4.41 //
children.translated_text: as in the <s>Kṛta</s> and other ages — therefore He is called <s>Tri-yuga</s> (Lord of three ages). (Lbh 1.4.41)

children.text: kaler ante ca samprāpte kalkinaṃ brahma-vādinam |
children.translated_text: At the end of <s>Kali</s>, having arrived, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, entering into <s>Kalki</s>,
a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, maintains the world. (Lbh 1.4.42)

children.text: pūrvotpanneṣ bhūteṣu teṣu teṣu kalau prabhuḥ |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kali</s> age, the Lord, entering into those beings previously born,

children.text: kṛtvā praveśaṃ kurute yad abhipretam ātmanaḥ // Lbh_1,4.43 //
children.translated_text: accomplishes whatever is His own intention.' (Lbh 1.4.43)
Thus.
Therefore, the <s>avatāra</s> status of these is ultimately only figurative. (Lbh 1.4.44)
Now the <s>prābhava</s> and <s>vaibhava</s> categories:
Those who are of the essential form of <s>Hari</s> but lesser than the <s>para</s> (supreme) state,

children.text: śaktīnāṃ tāratamyena kramāt te tat-tad-ākhyakāḥ // Lbh_1,4.45 //
children.translated_text: according to the gradation of their <s>śaktis</s> (powers), are successively designated by their respective names. (Lbh 1.4.45)

children.text: prābhavāś ca dvidhā tatra dṛśyante śāstra-cakṣuṣā |
children.translated_text: The <s>prābhava</s> (partial) incarnations are seen to be of two kinds in the vision of scripture.
Some are not manifest for very long and are not of widely spread fame;

children.text: te mohinī ca haṃsaś ca śuklādyāś ca yugānugāḥ // Lbh_1,4.46 //
children.translated_text: they are <s>Mohinī</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, and the <s>Śukla</s> and others who accompany each <s>Yuga</s>. (Lbh 1.4.46)
Others are makers of <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures), generally appearing in the guise of sages;

children.text: dhanvantary-ṛṣabhau vyāso dattaś ca kapilaś ca te // Lbh_1,4.47 //
children.translated_text: they are <s>Dhanvantari</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Datta</s> (<s>Dattātreya</s>), and <s>Kapila</s>. (Lbh 1.4.47)

children.text: atha syur vaibhavāvasthās te ca kūrmo ṛṣādhipaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now the <s>vaibhava</s> (majestic) states: they are <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise), the lord of sages,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> the companion of <s>Nara</s>, <s>Śrī Varāha</s> (Boar), and <s>Hayānana</s> (<s>Hayagrīva</s>), (Lbh 1.4.48)
<s>Pṛśnigarbha</s>, the slayer of <s>Pralamba</s>, <s>Yajña</s> and the other fourteen;

children.text: ity amī vaibhavāvasthā ekaviṃśatir īritāḥ // Lbh_1,4.49 //
children.translated_text: thus these <s>vaibhava</s> states are declared to be twenty-one. (Lbh 1.4.49)
<s>Kroḍa</s> (Boar) and <s>Hayagrīva</s> are mentioned within the <s>Nava-vyūha</s> (nine emanations),
and four preeminent ones among the <s>Manvantara-avatāras</s>. (Lbh 1.4.50)
They are <s>Śrī Hari</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, and likewise <s>Ajita</s> and <s>Vāmana</s>;

children.text: ṣaḍ amī vaibhavāvasthāḥ parāvasthopamā matāḥ // Lbh_1,4.51 //
children.translated_text: these six <s>vaibhava</s> states are considered comparable to the <s>para</s> (supreme) state. (Lbh 1.4.51)
The abodes of some of these are described according to the vision of the scriptures.
Wherever they shine forth, within the <s>Brahmāṇḍa</s> (cosmic egg),
the statements of the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s> and other texts are authoritative. (Lbh 1.4.52)
In the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>:
'Above those two, another of the same measurement;
the fifth, called <s>Mahātala</s>, with red-colored earth —
there is a lake ten thousand <s>yojanas</s> in extent;

children.text: svayaṃ ca tatra vasati kūrma-rūpa-dharo hariḥ // Lbh_1,4.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> Himself dwells there, bearing the tortoise form.' (Lbh 1.4.53)
'Above those two, another of the same measurement;
there is a divine lake three hundred <s>yojanas</s> in extent;

children.text: tasyāṃ sa vasate devo matsya-rūpa-dharo hariḥ // Lbh_1,4.54 //
children.translated_text: in it the Lord dwells, bearing the fish form.' (Lbh 1.4.54)
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the companion of <s>Nara</s>, dwells at <s>Badarī</s> (Badarikāśrama). (Lbh 1.4.55)
The abode of <s>Nṛ-Varāha</s> (the Man-Boar) is declared in <s>Mahar-loka</s>;
its measurement is three hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>. (Lbh 1.4.56)

children.text: ayutāni ca pañcāśat śeṣa-sthānaṃ manoharam // Lbh_1,4.57 //
children.translated_text: Fifty thousand — the beautiful abode of <s>Śeṣa</s>. (Lbh 1.4.57)

children.text: sa eva loko vārāhaḥ kathitas tu svayaṃ prabhaḥ |
children.translated_text: That very world is called <s>Vārāha</s>, proclaimed by the Lord Himself.
This world, attached to the cosmic egg, most beautiful, the lowest of all,
the Lord in boar form, bearing a white form, dwelt there. (Lbh 1.4.58)
'Above those two, another of the same measurement;
the fourth, with yellow-colored earth, known as <s>Gabhasti-tala</s> —
there the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> abides, bearing the horse-head,
resembling a hundred moons in radiance, adorned with golden ornaments.' (Lbh 1.4.59)
The abode of <s>Pṛśnigarbha</s> is above the world of <s>Brahmā</s>. (Lbh 1.4.60)

children.text: vāsas tatra pralambārer yatraivāgharipor bhavet // Lbh_1,4.61 //
children.translated_text: The abode of the slayer of <s>Pralamba</s> is where the enemy of <s>Agha</s> (i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) dwells. (Lbh 1.4.61)
A portion-form of this very one dwells in <s>Pātāla</s>,
always with the palm-tree banner, eloquent, adorned with a forest garland,
always bearing on his head a crest of hoods brilliant with gems,
holding a plow, a pestle, and a sword, adorned in blue garments. (Lbh 1.4.62)

children.text: brahma-lokopariṣṭāc ca harer loko virājate // Lbh_1,4.63 //
children.translated_text: Above <s>Brahma-loka</s>, the world of <s>Hari</s> shines forth. (Lbh 1.4.63)
The abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the great-souled <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, is in <s>Svar-loka</s>;

children.text: tathā vaikuṇṭha-loke ca svayam āviṣkṛto hi yaḥ // Lbh_1,4.64 //
children.translated_text: and in <s>Vaikuṇṭha-loka</s>, He has manifested Himself. (Lbh 1.4.64)
The dwelling of <s>Ajita</s> is established in <s>Dhruva-loka</s>.

children.text: bhuvar-loke tu vasatir vāmanasya mahātmanaḥ // Lbh_1,4.65 //
children.translated_text: The abode of the great-souled <s>Vāmana</s> is in <s>Bhuvar-loka</s>. (Lbh 1.4.65)
The abode of <s>Trivikrama</s> is declared in <s>Tapo-loka</s>.
And His divine shelter of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is situated in <s>Brahma-loka</s>;
and an abode created by Him is above <s>Brahma-loka</s>. (Lbh 1.4.66)

children.text: hari-vaṃśe surendreṇa kahtito yaḥ surarṣaye // Lbh_1,4.67 //
children.translated_text: As described by <s>Surendra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) to the celestial sage in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>. (Lbh 1.4.67)
Thus in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> (2.70.37):

children.text: idaṃ bhuṅktvā mahīyaṃ tu bhagavan viṣṇunā kṛtam |
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed this great earth, made by Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: upary upari lokānāṃ adhikaṃ bhuvanaṃ mune // Lbh_1,4.68 //
children.translated_text: above all the worlds is a realm superior, O sage. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.4.68 //
Thus.
The most wondrous abodes of all <s>avatāra</s>-s (incarnations) shine forth

children.text: nivāsāḥ paramāścaryā iti śāstre nirūpyate // Lbh_1,4.69 //
children.translated_text: in <s>para-vyoman</s> (the supreme sky, i.e. Vaikuṇṭha) — thus it is established in scripture. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.4.69 //
As stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
In the eternal <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> realm dwell the greatly resplendent ones —
all the <s>avatāra</s>-s, beginning with <s>Matsya</s> (Fish) and <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise), reside there always. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.4.70 //
Thus concludes the determination of the <s>avatāra</s>-s and their abodes.

Fifth Section:
Determination of the Supreme State (<s>Parāvasthā</s>)

children.text: atha kṛṣṇo nara-bhrātur avatāra iti kvacit |
children.translated_text: Now, some say that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is an <s>avatāra</s> of <s>Nara</s>'s brother (Nārāyaṇa);

children.text: upendrasyeti ca kvāpi bhrātāsau nātikovidām // Lbh_1,5.1 //
children.translated_text: and elsewhere, that He is <s>Upendra</s>'s brother — these are views of those who are not very learned. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.1 //
As stated in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>:
<s>Dharma</s>'s two sons, portions of <s>Hari</s>, named <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>,

children.text: candra-vaṃśam anu prāpya jātau kṛṣṇārjunāv ubhau // Lbh_1,5.2 //
