children.translated_text: having descended into the <s>Candra</s> (lunar) dynasty, were born as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.2 //
And in <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, Fourth Canto (4.1.59):

children.text: tāv imau vai bhagavato harer aṃśāv ihāgatau |
children.translated_text: These two are indeed portions of the Lord <s>Hari</s>, who have come here —

children.text: bhāra-vyayāya ca bhuvaḥ kṛṣṇau yadu-kurūdvahau // Lbh_1,5.3 //
children.translated_text: for relieving the earth's burden — the two <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-s (dark ones), the foremost of the <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Kuru</s> clans. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.3 //
Having worshipped the best of divine sages, the ancient sage,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the companion of <s>Nara</s>, as prompted by propriety,
addressing him with measured, nectarean, and pleasing speech,

children.text: prāha prabho bhagavate karavāma he kim // Lbh_1,5.4 //
children.translated_text: said: 'O Lord, what shall we do for the <s>Bhagavān</s> (the Blessed One)?' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.4 //
Corroborating this is the passage in the Tenth Canto (10.69.16):
His being an <s>avatāra</s> of <s>Upendra</s> is stated in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, in <s>Śakra</s>'s words (2.70.34):

children.text: aindraṃ vaiṣṇavam asyaiva mune bhāgam ahaṃ dadau |
children.translated_text: 'I gave to him the share of <s>Indra</s> that belongs to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O sage;

children.text: yavīyāṃsam ahaṃ premnā kṛṣṇaṃ praśyāmi nārada // Lbh_1,5.5 //
children.translated_text: I lovingly regard <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as my younger brother, O <s>Nārada</s>.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.5 //
Thus.

children.text: tad etad ubhayatvaṃ na bhavet kṛṣṇe virodhataḥ |
children.translated_text: This dual characterization cannot apply to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, since it would be contradictory.

children.text: aṃśatvaṃ hi tayor uktaṃ parāvasthatvam asya tu // Lbh_1,5.6 //
children.translated_text: For the status of being a partial manifestation (<s>aṃśa</s>) is attributed to those two (<s>Nara</s>-<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and <s>Upendra</s>), whereas <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s is the supreme state (<s>parāvastha</s>). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.6 //
The partial status of <s>Nara</s>'s brother is expressed by 'these are portions,' which will be explained;

children.text: upendrasya tathātvaṃ ca harivaṃśe'pi dṛśyate // Lbh_1,5.7 //
children.translated_text: and the partial nature of <s>Upendra</s> is also seen in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.7 //
As stated in the words of the divine sage (<s>Harivaṃśa</s> 2.71.21-23):
The great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s> was formerly propitiated by <s>Aditi</s> through austerity.
Pleased by her, He offered her a boon, and <s>Aditi</s> was gratified.

children.text: tayoktas tvādṛśaṃ putram icchāmīti surottama // Lbh_1,5.8 //
children.translated_text: She told Him: 'I desire a son like You, O best of gods.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.8 //
He said: 'There is no other person in the world equal to Me.

children.text: aṃśena tu bhaviṣyāmi putraḥ khalv aham eva te // Lbh_1,5.9 //
children.translated_text: But by a portion of Myself, I shall indeed become your son.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.9 //
Thus.
Now the supreme state (<s>parāvasthā-bhāva</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> will be clearly stated hereafter.

children.text: parāvasthaś c a sampūrṇāvasthaḥ śāstre prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The supreme state is declared in scripture to be the complete, perfect state (<s>sampūrṇāvastha</s>).

children.text: tasmād-aṃśatvam evāsya viruddhaṃ sphuṭam īkṣate // Lbh_1,5.10 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, the attribution of partial status (<s>aṃśatva</s>) to Him is clearly seen to be contradictory. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.10 //

children.text: arthagatyantaraṃ teṣāṃ vacanānāṃ ca dṛśyate // Lbh_1,5.11 //
children.translated_text: An alternative meaning of those statements is also seen. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.11 //
Regarding the verse '<s>Dharma</s>'s two sons' etc., the explanatory verse:
'Having assimilated <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> into Themselves,

children.text: kṛṣṇārjunau candra-vaṃśam anu prakaṭatāṃ gatau // Lbh_1,5.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s> descended into and became manifest in the lunar dynasty.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.12 //
Regarding 'These two' etc., the explanatory verse:

children.text: kartārau tau harer aṃśau nara-nārāyaṇāv iha |
children.translated_text: The doers, <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, who are portions of <s>Hari</s>, here
at the end of <s>Dvāpara</s> age came as agents of action, as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.13 //
Regarding 'Having worshipped' etc., the explanatory verses:
He who is called the ancient sage because He was the first teacher of all;

children.text: nārāṇāṃ puruṣāṇāṃ yas trayāṇām āśrayaḥ sa tu ||
children.translated_text: He who is the refuge of the three categories of persons (<s>nara</s>);
being Himself the companion of <s>Nara</s> (i.e. human beings) in the mortal worlds,
imitating the <s>dharma</s> of that role, He worshipped that sage;
although <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by the portion named <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, is that sage's superior,
He nevertheless worshipped <s>Nārada</s> as part of His <s>kṣatriya</s> play (<s>līlā</s>). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.14 //
Regarding '<s>Indra</s>'s share' etc., the explanatory verse:
<s>Indra</s> spoke thus out of jealousy and lack of full understanding;

children.text: tasmāt kṛṣṇasya no tat-tad-rūpatvaṃ ghaṭate kvacit // Lbh_1,5.15 //
children.translated_text: therefore the status of being those various forms does not apply to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in any way. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.15 //
In <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the sixfold divine qualities (<s>ṣāḍguṇya</s>) are fully manifest.

children.text: parāvasthās tu te tasya dīpād-utpanna-dīpavat // Lbh_1,5.16 //
children.translated_text: These are the supreme states of the Lord, like lamps lit from a lamp. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.16 //
Now, the supreme states (<s>parāvasthā</s>-s). As stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
<s>Śrī Nṛsiṃha</s> (from <s>Bhāvārtha-dīpikā</s> 1.1.1, 10.87.1):
I bow to <s>Hari</s> who delights the heart of <s>Prahlāda</s>, who tears apart the ignorance of devotees,
who has the radiance of the autumn moon and the face of the king of beasts (<s>Nṛsiṃha</s>). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.17 //

children.text: vāgīśā yasya vadane lakṣmīr yasya ca vakṣasi |
children.translated_text: <s>Sarasvatī</s> (goddess of speech) dwells on His tongue, <s>Lakṣmī</s> on His chest,

children.text: yasyāste hṛdaye saṃvit taṃ nṛsiṃham ahaṃ bhaje // Lbh_1,5.18 //
children.translated_text: and pure consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>) in His heart — I worship that <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.18 //
His deep roaring stupefied <s>Brahmā</s> (the lotus-born);
the fury of the Son of the Pillar was aroused by the sage, O King. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.19 //
The clouds, shaken off by His mane, fell away;
the planets, robbed of their luster by His gaze, grew dim;
the oceans, struck by His breath, were agitated;
the guardian elephants of the directions trumpeted in terror at His roar. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.20 //
As stated in the Seventh Canto (7.8.32-33):
The sky became crowded with celestial chariots tossed up by His mane;
the earth sank, pressed down by His feet;
mountains were uprooted by His momentum;

children.text: tat-tejasā khaṃ kakubho na rejire // Lbh_1,5.21 //
children.translated_text: by His splendor, neither the sky nor the quarters of space could shine. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.21 //
Thus.
Though fierce, this Man-Lion is gentle to His own devotees,
like a lion to its own cubs, while terrifying in form to all others. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.22 //
From <s>Śrīdhara Svāmī</s>'s commentary to 7.9.1.
The greatness of this divine <s>Siṃha</s> (Lion), who is swollen with supreme bliss,
is made manifest in the <s>Śrīman Nṛsiṃha-Tāpanīya Upaniṣad</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.23 //
The abode of the great-souled <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> is in <s>Janaloka</s>,

children.text: sarvopariṣṭāc ca tathā viṣṇuloke prakīrtitaḥ // Lbh_1,5.24 //
children.translated_text: and is also declared to be in <s>Viṣṇuloka</s>, above all other worlds. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.24 //
<s>Śrī Rāghavendra</s> (Lord Rāma):
Even more than the former (<s>Nṛsiṃha</s>), this moon of the flawless nectar of sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>)
shines resplendent, lofty with His assemblage of auspicious qualities — <s>Śrī Raghu-puṅgava</s> (the best of the Raghu dynasty). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.25 //
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
We worship the great Lord (<s>Maheśāna</s>) who broke <s>Hara</s>'s (Śiva's) bow,
the sandalwood-delight of <s>Jānakī</s>'s heart — <s>Raghunandana</s> (joy of the Raghu clan). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.26 //
The festival of His birth is described in the <s>Śrī Rāmārcana-candrikā</s>: // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.27 //

children.text: uccasthe graha-pañcake sura-gurau sendau navamyāṃ tithau
children.translated_text: When five planets were in exaltation, with <s>Jupiter</s> and the Moon together, on the ninth <s>tithi</s> (lunar day),

children.text: lagne karkaṭake punar vasumate meghaṃ gate pūṣaṇi |
children.translated_text: in the <s>Karkaṭa</s> (Cancer) ascendant, with the earth rich and the sun behind a cloud,
all the <s>palāśa</s> (Butea) sacrificial sticks of the holy <s>Ayodhyā</s> fire-altar were ready to be kindled —

children.text: āvirbhūtam abhūd apūrva-vibhavaṃ yat kiñcid ekaṃ mahaḥ // Lbh_1,5.28 //
children.translated_text: there appeared an unprecedented, singular radiance of supreme glory. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.28 //
Abandoning royal sovereignty and <s>Lakṣmī</s> desired even by the gods — so difficult to renounce —
that most righteous one, at the word of a noble elder, went to the forest.
He pursued the illusory deer desired by His beloved.
I bow to the lotus feet of that great <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.29 //
In the Eleventh Canto (11.5.34):
This fame of <s>Raghupati</s> (Lord of the Raghus) is not His true glory — He whose playful form was assumed at the gods' request,
whose abode is freed from any who could be His superior or equal —
the slaying of demons, the bridging of the ocean, with hosts of weapons —

children.text: kiṃ tasya śatru-hanane kapayaḥ sahāyāḥ // Lbh_1,5.30 //
children.translated_text: what need had He of monkeys as allies to destroy His enemies? // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.30 //
In the Ninth Canto (9.11.20-21):
by sages as that which destroys sin — fame like the elephant-guard of the directions —
I take refuge in <s>Raghupati</s>, whose lotus feet are adorned by the crowns
of the guardians of heaven and the rulers of the earth. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.31 //
He whose spotless fame is still sung today in royal assemblies
Thus.
Here the explanatory verse:
'Assumed' means 'manifested' — the playful form is a form made of <s>līlā</s> (divine play);

children.text: yena tasyeti sāmyeti svārthe ṣyañ pratyayo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'of Him' — thus 'equality' (<s>sāmya</s>), where the suffix <s>ṣyañ</s> is understood in the reflexive sense.
The term '<s>dhāman</s>' (abode/splendor) should be understood as His intrinsic nature, from 'superior' and 'equal';
'freed from any superior or equal' — this establishes that His glory is superior to all,

children.text: yasyādhikaḥ samaś cātra kvāpi nāstīti niścayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.32 //
children.translated_text: and the conclusion is that nowhere is there anyone greater or equal to Him. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.32 //
<s>Nākapāla</s>-s are <s>Mahendra</s> and other guardians of heaven; <s>vasupā</s>-s are rulers of the earth. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.33 //
The <s>avatāra</s>-s of the <s>Vāsudeva</s> and other forms are proclaimed;
in the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s>, <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, and others are listed in order. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.34 //

children.text: pādme tu rāmo bhagavān nārāyaṇa itīritaḥ |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>Rāma</s> is declared to be the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself;

children.text: śeṣaś cakraṃ ca śaṅkhaś ca kramāt syur lakṣmaṇādayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.35 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s>, the discus (<s>cakra</s>), and the conch (<s>śaṅkha</s>) are respectively <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and the others. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.35 //
His abode is recorded as <s>Ayodhyā</s> city in <s>Madhya-deśa</s> (the central land),
and in <s>Mahā-Vaikuṇṭha-loka</s>, the realm of <s>Rāghavendra</s> is celebrated. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.36 //
Let there be many <s>avatāra</s>-s of the Lotus-Naveled One (<s>Puṣkara-nābha</s>), all auspicious;

children.text: kṛṣṇād anyaḥ ko vā latāsv api premado bhavati // Lbh_1,5.37 //
children.translated_text: but who other than <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> bestows love (<s>prema</s>) even upon the creeper-vines? // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.37 //
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. In <s>Bilvamaṅgala</s>'s work:
An unprecedented ocean of the nectar of supreme lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>) and sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) —

children.text: devakī-nandanas tv eṣa puraḥ paricariṣyate // Lbh_1,5.38 //
children.translated_text: this son of <s>Devakī</s> will be glorified hereafter. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.38 //
His abode is celebrated in the <s>Purāṇa</s>-s and other texts in four places:

children.text: vraje madhupure dvāra-vatyāṃ goloka eva ca // Lbh_1,5.39 //
children.translated_text: in <s>Vraja</s>, in <s>Mathurā</s>, in <s>Dvāravatī</s> (Dvārakā), and in <s>Goloka</s> itself. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.39 //
Now, the equality of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> and <s>Rāma</s> with Him has clearly been established;
the procedure from the <s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> is examined here. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.40 //
There, <s>Maitreya</s>'s question in the Fourth Section (4.15.1-2):
In the form of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and in the form of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, being slain by <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: avāpa nihato bhogān aprāpyān amarair api // Lbh_1,5.41 //
children.translated_text: he obtained pleasures unattainable even by the gods. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.41 //

children.text: nālabhat tatra caiveha sāyujyaṃ sa kathaṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: He did not attain <s>sāyujya</s> (merging) either there or here; how then

children.text: samprāptaḥ śiśupālatve sāyujyaṃ śāśvate harau // Lbh_1,5.42 //
children.translated_text: did he, in the form of <s>Śiśupāla</s>, attain eternal <s>sāyujya</s> with <s>Hari</s>? // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.42 //
The reply of <s>Śrī Parāśara</s> (4.15.4-17):
For the slaying of the lord of demons, the One who creates, sustains, and destroys all worlds, previously assuming a body,

children.text: kurvatā nṛsiṃha-rūpam āviṣkṛtam || tatra ca hiraṇyakaśipor viṣṇur ayam ity etan
children.translated_text: manifested the form of <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>. And there, the thought 'This is <s>Viṣṇu</s>'

children.text: na manasy abhūt || niratiśaya-puṇya-samudbhūtam etat sattva-jātam iti |

children.translated_text: With his mind single-pointedly driven by an excess of <s>rajas</s> (passion), through the force of that contemplation, he obtained — as the consequence of his death —
an unsurpassed wealth of enjoyments in the form of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> (the Ten-Headed), surpassing all three worlds
in opulence. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.43 //
did not arise in the mind of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>. Rather: 'This is a being born of unsurpassed merit.'

children.text: na tu sa tasminn anādi-nidhane para-brahma-bhūte bhagavaty anālambini kṛte

children.translated_text: who has no support other than Himself. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.44 //
But he did not attain the dissolution of his mind into the Lord, who is the beginningless and endless Supreme <s>Brahman</s>,

children.text:
evaṃ daśānanatve'py anaṅga-parādhīnatayā jānakī-samāsakta-cetasā bhagavatā
dāśarathi-rūpa-dhāriṇā hatasya tad-rūpa-darśanam evāsīt nāyam acyuta ity āsaktir
vipadyato'ntaḥ-karaṇe mānuṣa-buddhir eva kevalam asyābhūt | punar apy
acutavinipāta-mātra-phalam akhilabhūmaṇḍala-ślāghya-cedi-rāja-kule janma

children.translated_text: and he obtained unobstructed sovereignty even in the form of <s>Śiśupāla</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.45 //

Thus, in the form of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> too, with his mind attached to <s>Jānakī</s> (Sītā) due to subjugation by lust, when he was slain by the Lord who had assumed the form of <s>Dāśarathi</s> (Rāma, son of Daśaratha), what occurred was merely the vision of that form — not the recognition 'This is <s>Acyuta</s> (the Infallible One).' In the dying inner faculty, only a human perception existed. Yet again, merely by falling at the hands of <s>Acyuta</s>, the fruit was birth in the Cedi royal dynasty, celebrated throughout the entire earth,

children.text:
tatra tv akhilānām eva sa bhagavan-nāmnāṃ tvaṅkāra-kāraṇam abhavat | tataś ca
tat-kāla-kṛtānāṃ teṣām aśeṣāṇām evācyuta-nāmnām anavaratam aneka-janmasu
vardhita-vidveṣānubandhi-citto vinindana-santarjanādiṣūccāraṇam akarot | tac ca
rūpam utphulla-padma-dalāmalākṣamaty-ujjvala-pīta-vastra-dhāry
amala-kirīṭa-keyūra-hāra-kaṭakādi-śobhitam

children.translated_text: adorned with pure crown, armlets, necklace, and bracelets, holding conch, discus, and mace in four generous arms — through the force of his deeply intensified enmity,
in all states — walking, eating, bathing, sitting, sleeping, and all other conditions — his mind never went anywhere else.

There, however, he became the cause of uttering '<s>tvaṃ</s>' (You) in all the Lord's holy names. And then, those inexhaustible names of <s>Acyuta</s>, uttered continuously over many births through the force of ever-increasing enmity, he pronounced in the course of reviling, threatening, and other acts. And that form — with eyes like spotless, full-blown lotus petals, wearing exceedingly brilliant yellow garments,

children.text: tatas tam evākrośeṣūccārayaṃs tam eva hṛdayena dhārayann ātma-vadhāya
children.translated_text: Then, while abusing Him, he was pronouncing only Him; while holding only Him in his heart, at the moment of his own death —
he beheld the Lord, radiant with the garland of rays from the discus in the Lord's hand, of imperishable splendor and form,
who is <s>Brahman</s> itself, free from the faults of hatred and all else. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.47 //

children.text: bhagavatāntam upanītas tasminn eva layam upayayau // Lbh_1,5.48 //
children.translated_text: Having been brought before the Lord, he attained dissolution in Him alone. [Lbh 1.5.48]
And then, swiftly dispatched by the Lord's discus, with his entire accumulation of sins burnt away by that remembrance,

children.text:
etat tavākhilaṃ mayābhihitam | ayaṃ hi bhagavān kīrtitaś ca saṃsmṛtaś ca
dveṣānubandhenāpi akhila-surāsurādi-durlabhaṃ phalaṃ prayacchati kim uta

children.translated_text: even through the connection of enmity, bestows a fruit difficult to attain for all <s>devas</s>, <s>asuras</s>, and others -- how much more so for those endowed with proper devotion! [Lbh 1.5.49]
All this has been related to you by me. For this Lord, whether glorified or remembered,

children.text: noktaṃ parāśareṇātra sthitau tau pārṣadāv iti |
children.translated_text: <s>Parāśara</s> did not say here that those two remained as attendants (<s>pārṣadas</s>);

children.text: kintūbhayos tayor āsīj janma-trayam itīritam // Lbh_1,5.50 //
children.translated_text: rather, it is stated that both of them had three births. [Lbh 1.5.50]

children.text: ataḥ sarveṣu kalpeṣu na tau pārṣada-jau matau |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in all <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic cycles), those two are not considered born as attendants;

children.text: anyathā na tayoḥ pātaḥ prati-kalpaṃ samañjasaḥ // Lbh_1,5.51 //
children.translated_text: otherwise, their fall in every <s>kalpa</s> would not be consistent. [Lbh 1.5.51]
The prose that <s>Parāśara</s> composed in reply to <s>Maitreya</s>,

children.text: ślokīkṛtya tad evedaṃ saṅkṣepeṇa vilikhyate // Lbh_1,5.52 //
children.translated_text: that very same is here written in summary, rendered into verse. [Lbh 1.5.52]
When the wondrous <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> form was manifested by <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: hiraṇyakaśipor asmin viṣṇu-buddhir na niścitā // Lbh_1,5.53 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> did not have the firm conviction that this was <s>Viṣṇu</s>. [Lbh 1.5.53]
Rather, he concluded that this was some being endowed with great merit,
his mind impelled by the predominance of <s>rajas</s> (passion), due to the state arising from that condition. [Lbh 1.5.54]
Then, having obtained the supreme enjoyment and prosperity, exceedingly rare,
whose sole cause was destruction, he attained it in his birth as <s>Rāvaṇa</s>. [Lbh 1.5.55]
Because of the certainty that He was <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the enmity was not excessive, and therefore the state of possession (<s>āveśa</s>) did not continue;

children.text: tāṃ vinā ca bhavet dveṣo narakāyaiva veṇavat // Lbh_1,5.56 //
children.translated_text: and without that, enmity would lead only to hell, like <s>Veṇa</s>. [Lbh 1.5.56]

children.text: kintv asya sampat-samprāptis tat-kareṇa mṛteḥ param |
children.translated_text: However, his attainment of prosperity came after death by His hand;
thus, by the word 'eva' (indeed), he recalls the virtuous qualities of the Lord. [Lbh 1.5.57]
Due to the absence of <s>āveśa</s> (divine possession), because of the non-destruction of faults, seeing only the pure,

children.text: prakaṭe'pi para-brahma-rūpe tatrāsya no layaḥ // Lbh_1,5.58 //
children.translated_text: even when the form of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> was manifest, he did not attain dissolution therein. [Lbh 1.5.58]
In his birth as <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, his mind was subjugated by great lust;

children.text: tadvan manuṣya-dhīr asya śrī-rāme'bhūn mṛtāv api // Lbh_1,5.59 //
children.translated_text: similarly, he regarded <s>Śrī Rāma</s> as merely a human, even at the time of death. [Lbh 1.5.59]

children.text: ato'sau cedirājatve punar āpottamāṃ śriyam // Lbh_1,5.60 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, in his birth as the king of <s>Cedi</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>), he again attained the highest glory. [Lbh 1.5.60]

children.text: tatra kṛṣṇe samastānām eva nāmnāṃ ramāpateḥ |
children.translated_text: There, regarding <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the causes for the application of all the names

children.text: kāraṇāni pravṛttes tu nimittāny abhavaṃs tadā // Lbh_1,5.61 //
children.translated_text: of the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) became the occasions at that time. [Lbh 1.5.61]

children.text: tena niścitya taṃ viṣṇuṃ svasya dvir-maraṇaṃ yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having ascertained Him to be <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since He had caused his death twice,
out of extreme enmity and great intensity of possession, all those names
he constantly and repeatedly uttered in abuse, threats, and such. [Lbh 1.5.62]

children.text: rūpaṃ ca tādṛśaṃ dṛṣṭvā viṣṇur eveti niścayāt |
children.translated_text: And seeing such a form, with the certainty that 'This is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>,'

children.text: nāmavat tac ca sarvatra sarvadā caiva saṃsmaran ||
children.translated_text: like the names, he constantly remembered that form everywhere and at all times;
the mass of sins born of enmity toward Him was burnt away, and when the disc was hurled, by its radiance,
his demoniac nature departed, and at the end, his vision was thus purified;

children.text: tadā tūjjvalam adrākṣīt paraṃ brahma narākṛti // Lbh_1,5.63 //
children.translated_text: then he beheld the resplendent Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form. [Lbh 1.5.63]
At that very moment, when the demoniac body was destroyed by the blow of the disc,

children.text: tad eva brahma paramam anulīnatvam āyayau // Lbh_1,5.64 //
children.translated_text: he attained complete absorption into that very Supreme <s>Brahman</s>. [Lbh 1.5.64]

children.text: ity uktvāpy atra bakyāder mokṣam apy arbha-līlayā |
children.translated_text: Having said this, the sage, reflecting also on the liberation of <s>Baka</s> and others through child's play,
and the non-liberation of <s>Kālanemi</s> and others elsewhere despite the Lord's deeds,

children.text: muniḥ smṛtvā punaḥ prākhyat ayaṃ hi bhagavān iti // Lbh_1,5.65 //
children.translated_text: then declared: 'For this is the Lord Himself.' [Lbh 1.5.65]
<s>Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> 4.15.17

children.text: hi prasiddham ayaṃ kṛṣṇo bhagavān svayam eva yat |
children.translated_text: It is well known that this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the Lord Himself (<s>Bhagavān svayam</s>);

children.text: prīṇatāṃ dviṣatāṃ cātaś cetāṃsy ākarṣati drutam |
children.translated_text: therefore He swiftly attracts the minds of both those who love Him and those who hate Him;

children.text: tasmāt kīrtita ity ādi māhātmyam citram atra na // Lbh_1,5.66 //
children.translated_text: hence, there is nothing extraordinary in the glory of being glorified and so forth. [Lbh 1.5.66]

children.text: iti vijñāya gadyānāṃ hārdaṃ sauhārdataḥ sphuñam |
children.translated_text: Having thus understood the essence of the prose passages, which is clear due to their favorable intent,

children.text: tasmāt sa eva kaimutyād bhajanīyatayeṣyate // Lbh_1,5.67 //
children.translated_text: therefore He alone is to be accepted as supremely worthy of worship, by argument from the stronger case (<s>kaimutya</s>). [Lbh 1.5.67]

children.text: athākhilānāṃ nāmnāṃ ca pravṛttau kāraṇaṃ śṛṇu // Lbh_1,5.68 //
children.translated_text: Now hear the cause for the application of all the names. [Lbh 1.5.68]
The names of the Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s> exist here both due to similarity of the cause of application

children.text: tathaiva hetubhedāc ca vartante yadu-puṅgave // Lbh_1,5.69 //
children.translated_text: and also due to difference of cause, in this best of the <s>Yadus</s>. [Lbh 1.5.69]
'Enemy of demons,' 'Lotus-eyed,' 'Bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s> (bow),' 'Whose vehicle is <s>Garuḍa</s>,'
'Clad in yellow garments,' 'Disc in hand,' 'Bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark,' 'Four-armed' --

children.text: ity ādīny atra nāmāni pravṛtter hetu-sāmyataḥ // Lbh_1,5.70 //
children.translated_text: these and other names here are due to similarity of the cause of application. [Lbh 1.5.70]
He is called <s>Vāsudeva</s> because He is the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>;

children.text: madhu-vaṃśe yato jātaḥ kathyate mādhavas tataḥ // Lbh_1,5.71 //
children.translated_text: because He was born in the <s>Madhu</s> dynasty, He is therefore called <s>Mādhava</s>. [Lbh 1.5.71]

children.text: śrī-hari-vaṃśe'pi (2.7.36)[* According to the critical edition, this is 51.36 or verse 3473.
The GM edition quotes it as 63.36.] -
children.translated_text: The GM edition quotes it as 63.36.] --

children.text: sa ca tenaiva nāmnātra kṛṣṇo vai dāma-bandhanāt |
children.translated_text: And He, by that very name here, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, because of being bound by a rope (<s>dāma</s>),

children.text: goṣṭhe dāmodara iti gopībhiḥ parigīyate // Lbh_1,5.72 //
children.translated_text: is sung by the <s>gopīs</s> in the cow-pasture as <s>Dāmodara</s>. [Lbh 1.5.72]
In the <s>Śrī Harivaṃśa</s> also (2.7.36) [* According to the critical edition, this is 51.36 or verse 3473.

children.text: tatraiva (158.30-32)[* Alternative numbering given in KṛṣṇaS 57 is 101.30-32. I haven't
yet been able to find these verses in the critical or Gita Press editions.] -
children.translated_text: yet been able to find these verses in the critical or Gita Press editions.] --
By this one lying below, moving underneath the cart,
the terrible <s>rākṣasī</s> (demoness) wearing the guise of a bird was slain;
In the same text (158.30-32) [* Alternative numbering given in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>S 57 is 101.30-32. I haven't
she was named <s>Pūtanā</s>, terrifying, of great body and great strength,

children.text: viṣa-digdhaṃ stanaṃ kṣudrā prayacchantī janārdane // Lbh_1,5.73 //
children.translated_text: the wretched one who offered her poison-smeared breast to <s>Janārdana</s>. [Lbh 1.5.73]
The forest-dwelling cowherds saw the slain <s>rākṣasī</s> there;

children.text: punar jāto'yam ity āhur uktas tasmād adhokṣajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'This one is born again!' they said, and therefore He was called <s>Adhokṣaja</s>.
Thus. [Lbh 1.5.74]

children.text: eṣo'dhaḥ śakaṭasyākṣe punar jāta ivety ataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'This one, beneath the axle of the cart, is as if born again' -- therefore

children.text: adhokṣaja iti prāhur iti ṭīkā kṛtoditam // Lbh_1,5.75 //
children.translated_text: they call Him <s>Adhokṣaja</s>, as stated in the commentary. [Lbh 1.5.75]
In the same text (2.9.45) [* Alternative numberings HV 62.43 or 4005.] --

children.text: ahaṃ kilendro devānāṃ tvaṃ gavām indratāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I am <s>Indra</s> of the <s>devas</s>; you have attained the lordship of cows;

children.text: govinda iti lokās tvāṃ gāsyanti bhuvi śāśvatam // Lbh_1,5.76 //
children.translated_text: the people on earth shall eternally sing of you as <s>Govinda</s>.' [Lbh 1.5.76]
In the same text (2.9.46) --
'As the lordship over me has been established by the cows, O Lord,

children.text: upendra iti kṛṣṇa tvāṃ gāsyanti divi devatāḥ // Lbh_1,5.77 //
children.translated_text: the <s>devas</s> in heaven shall sing of you, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, as <s>Upendra</s>.' [Lbh 1.5.77]
In the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> (5.16.23) --

children.text: yasmāt tvayaiva duṣṭātmā hataḥ keśī janārdana |
children.translated_text: 'Since by you alone the evil-souled <s>Keśī</s> was slain, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: tasmāt keśava-nāmnā tvaṃ loke jñeyo bhaviṣyasi // Lbh_1,5.78 //
children.translated_text: therefore you shall be known in the world by the name <s>Keśava</s>.' [Lbh 1.5.78]
Thus.

children.text: ity ādiny atra nāmāni pravṛtter hetu-bhedataḥ |
children.translated_text: These and other names here are due to difference in the cause of application;

children.text: eṣāṃ pravṛtter hetutvam anyad eva ramāpatau // Lbh_1,5.79 //
children.translated_text: the reason for the application of these names is different in the case of the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>). [Lbh 1.5.79]

children.text: kiṃ cāsurāṇāṃ dviṣatāṃ kṛṣṇam aprāpya nānyataḥ |
children.translated_text: Moreover, for the <s>asuras</s> who are hostile, without attaining <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and not from any other source,

children.text: kuto'pi muktir ity ākhyād eva-kāra-dvayena saḥ // Lbh_1,5.80 //
children.translated_text: liberation is never possible -- this is declared by the two occurrences of the word 'eva' (alone). [Lbh 1.5.80]
As stated in the <s>Śrī Bhagavad Gītā</s> (16.19-20) --

children.text: tān ahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrān saṃsāreṣu narādhamān |
children.translated_text: 'Those cruel haters, lowest of mankind, inauspicious ones,

children.text: kṣipāmy ajasram aśubhān āsurīṣv eva yoniṣu // Lbh_1,5.81 //
children.translated_text: I hurl perpetually into demoniac wombs alone in the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>. [Lbh 1.5.81]

children.text: āsurīṃ yonim āpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani |
children.translated_text: Attaining demoniac birth, deluded in birth after birth,

children.text: mām aprāpyaiva kaunteya tato yānty adhamāṃ gatim // Lbh_1,5.82 //
children.translated_text: without ever attaining Me, O son of <s>Kuntī</s>, they go to the lowest destination.' [Lbh 1.5.82]
Thus.

children.text: māṃ kṛṣṇa-rūpiṇaṃ yāvan nāpnuvanti mama dviṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: As long as My enemies do not attain Me in My form as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: tāvad evādhamaṃ yoniṃ prāpnuvantīti hi sphuṭam // Lbh_1,5.83 //
children.translated_text: so long they continue to attain the lowest birth -- this is clearly evident. [Lbh 1.5.83]

children.text: tasmāt trayāṇām evāyaṃ śreṣṭha ity atra vismayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the wonder here is that this one (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) alone among the three is the best;

children.text: ko vā syāt na tathā yasmāt svabhāvo'nyatra dṛśyate // Lbh_1,5.84 //
children.translated_text: who indeed would not be amazed, since such a nature is not seen elsewhere? [Lbh 1.5.84]
Therefore, in the <s>kalpa</s> of <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>, in the <s>Manvakṣara</s> <s>Āgama</s>,
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, and others are worshipped as belonging to His cyclical manifestation. [Lbh 1.5.85]
Now, this is heard in the scriptures, from the statement of the <s>Mahā-Vārāha</s>:

children.text: sarve nityāḥ śāśvatāś ca dahās tasya parātmanaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'All the forms (<s>dehas</s>) of that Supreme Self are eternal and everlasting,
free from diminution and acquisition, never born of <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature);
they are masses of supreme bliss, consisting entirely of pure consciousness,
all complete with all qualities, and free from all defects.' [Lbh 1.5.86]
Furthermore, in the <s>Nārada Pañcarātra</s> --
'Just as a gem, by differentiation, endowed with blue, yellow, and other colors,

children.text: rūpa-bhedam avāpnoti dhyāna-bhedāt tathā vibhuḥ // Lbh_1,5.87 //
children.translated_text: attains difference of form, so too the all-pervading Lord through difference of meditation.' [Lbh 1.5.87]
Thus.
Therefore, how can a hierarchy among them be explained?
To this it is said: Although all of them are complete, being the Supreme Lord,

children.text: tathāpy akhila-śaktīnāṃ prākaṭyaṃ tatra no bhavet // Lbh_1,5.88 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, the full manifestation of all powers does not occur in each of them. [Lbh 1.5.88]
The state of being a partial expansion (<s>aṃśatva</s>) means the perpetual manifestation of only a small portion of powers;
and completeness (<s>pūrṇatva</s>) means the manifestation of various powers by one's own will. [Lbh 1.5.89]
Power, sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>), sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>), compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>), brilliance (<s>tejas</s>), and such are the qualities;

children.text: śakter vyaktis tathāvyaktis tāratamyasya kāraṇam // Lbh_1,5.90 //
children.translated_text: the manifestation and non-manifestation of these powers is the cause of the hierarchy. [Lbh 1.5.90]
Even though the power is equal, as in the burning capacity of a lamp-flame and a mass of fire,
happiness comes only from the mass of fire, through the destruction of cold and such suffering. [Lbh 1.5.91]
In the same way, in accordance with the degree of manifestation of qualities and so forth,

children.text: bhava-dhvaṃsena saukhyaṃ syāt bhaktādīnāṃ yathāyatham // Lbh_1,5.92 //
children.translated_text: happiness through the destruction of material existence comes to devotees and others, each according to their capacity. [Lbh 1.5.92]

children.text: ekatvaṃ ca pṛthaktvaṃ ca tathāṃśatvam utāṃśitā |
children.translated_text: Oneness and separateness, being a partial expansion and being the source of expansions --
none of these are impossible in that one Being, due to His inconceivable and infinite powers. [Lbh 1.5.93]
Regarding this, even in oneness, separate manifestation is shown, as in the <s>Śrī Daśama</s> (Skandha) (10.69.2) --

children.text: citraṃ bataitad ekena vapuṣā yugapat pṛthak |
children.translated_text: 'How wonderful it is that He, with one body, simultaneously and separately

children.text: gṛheṣu dvy-aṣṭa-sāhasraṃ striya eka udāvahat // Lbh_1,5.94 //
children.translated_text: in sixteen thousand and eight houses, married an equal number of wives!' [Lbh 1.5.94]
Even in separateness, the attainment of one form is shown, as in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> --

children.text: sa devo bahudhā bhūtvā nirguṇaḥ puruṣottamaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'That Lord, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, who is beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, having become manifold,

children.text: ekībhūya punaḥ śete nirdoṣo harir ādikṛt // Lbh_1,5.95 //
children.translated_text: again becomes one and sleeps -- <s>Hari</s>, free from all faults, the primordial creator.' [Lbh 1.5.95]
Thus.

children.text: yajanti tva-mayās tvāṃ vai bahu-mūrty-eka-mūrtikam // Lbh_1,5.96 //
children.translated_text: 'Those who are identified with You worship You, who are of many forms and yet one form.' [Lbh 1.5.96]
As stated in the <s>Śrī Daśama</s> (Skandha) (10.40.7) --
Thus.
And in the <s>Kūrma Purāṇa</s> --

children.text: asthūlaś cānaṇuś caiva sthūlo'ṇuś caiva sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He is neither gross nor subtle, yet He is both gross and subtle in every respect;
He is said to be colorless in every way, yet He is dark-complexioned with reddish-tinged eyes;
the Lord is described with contradictory attributes due to His power of sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya-yoga</s>). [Lbh 1.5.97]
Even so, defects can never be attributed to the Supreme One;

children.text: guṇā viruddhā apy ete samāhāryāḥ samantataḥ // Lbh_1,5.98 //
children.translated_text: yet these mutually contradictory qualities can all be fully attributed to Him.' [Lbh 1.5.98]

children.text: śrī-ṣaṣṭha-skandhe [6.9.33-35] ca mitho viruddhācintya-śaktitvaṃ yathā gadyeṣu -
duravabodha ivāyaṃ tava vihāra-yogo yad aśaraṇo'śarīra idam
children.translated_text: 'This <s>yoga</s> (play) of Your pastimes (<s>vihāra</s>) is difficult to comprehend: how You, without shelter, without a body,

children.text: anavekṣitāsmat-samavāya ātmanaivāvikriyamāṇena sa-guṇam aguṇaḥ sṛjasi harasi
children.translated_text: without regard for our association, by Your own self alone, without undergoing any transformation, though beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, create, destroy,
and maintain that which possesses the <s>guṇas</s>. [Lbh 1.5.99]
In the <s>Śrī Ṣaṣṭha Skandha</s> [6.9.33-35] also, the inconceivable power of mutually contradictory attributes is shown in the prose passages --

children.text:
atha tatra bhavān kiṃ deva-dattavad iha guṇa-visarga-patitaḥ pāratantryeṇa
svakṛta-kuśalākuśalaṃ phalam upādadāti | aho svid ātmārāma upaśama-śīlaḥ
samañjasa-darśana upāste iti ha vāva na vidāmaḥ // Lbh_1,5.100 //
children.translated_text: of balanced vision, simply remain aloof? Indeed, we do not know. [Lbh 1.5.100]

Now, are You, O Lord, like an ordinary person (<s>Devadatta</s>), fallen into the creation of the <s>guṇas</s>, accepting in dependence the fruits of good and evil created by Yourself? Or do You, who delight in the Self (<s>Ātmārāma</s>), of tranquil disposition,

children.text:
na hi virodha ubhayaṃ bhagavaty aparigaṇita-guṇa-gaṇe īśvare
anavagāhya-māhātmye'rvācīna-vikalpa-vitarka-vicāra-pramāṇābhāsa-kutarka-ś
āstra-kalitāntaḥ-karaṇāśaya-duravagraha-vādināṃ vivādānavasare
uparata-samasta-māyā-maye kevala evātma-māyām antardhāya ko nv artho
children.translated_text: for Him who has withdrawn all <s>māyā</s> (illusion), who is pure spirit alone, who has concealed His own <s>māyā</s>, what purpose

children.text: durghaṭa iva bhavati svarūpa-dvayābhāvāt sama-viṣama-matīnāṃ matam anusarasi
children.translated_text: could be difficult to accomplish, since there is no duality in His nature? He follows the understanding of those with equal and unequal intellects,
just as a piece of rope follows the perceptions of those who see it as a snake and so forth.' [Lbh 1.5.101]

For there is no contradiction in both being present in the Lord, who possesses innumerable qualities, the Supreme Controller of unfathomable greatness -- a conclusion inaccessible to those whose inner faculties are corrupted by modern speculation, conjecture, deliberation, pseudo-evidence, and sophistic treatises, who are quarrelsome disputants in matters beyond dispute;
Without bodily activity, without dependence on earth and other elements,

children.text: vinā sahāyāṃs te karmāvikriyasya sudurgamam // Lbh_1,5.102 //
children.translated_text: without helpers -- Your action, O unchanging One, is very difficult to comprehend. [Lbh 1.5.102]
The creation of the <s>guṇas</s> refers to the battles between <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s> and such;

children.text: tasmin patita āsaktaḥ pāratantryas tu tad bhavet |
children.translated_text: one who has fallen into and is attached to that would be in a state of dependence;
but the subjection to the <s>devas</s> who have taken refuge in Him is brought about by compassion. [Lbh 1.5.103]
By that, does the Lord accept the fruit of His own deeds -- whether auspicious or inauspicious,

children.text: sukha-duḥkhādi-rūpaṃ kiṃ phalaṃ svīkurute bhavān // Lbh_1,5.104 //
children.translated_text: in the form of happiness or suffering? [Lbh 1.5.104]
Or, being self-delighting (<s>Ātmārāma</s>), is He utterly indifferent to all that?

children.text: na vidmaḥ kintu naivedaṃ viruddham ubhayaṃ tvayi // Lbh_1,5.105 //
children.translated_text: We do not know; but neither is this contradictory — both [aspects coexist] in You. || Lbh 1.5.105 ||

children.text: tatra hetur bhagavatīty ādi proktaṃ pada-dvayam |
children.translated_text: The reason for this is stated in the two words beginning with '<s>bhagavatī</s>' (divine potency);

children.text: tathaiveśvara ity ādi-padānāṃ pañcakaṃ matam // Lbh_1,5.106 //
children.translated_text: Likewise, the group of five words beginning with '<s>īśvara</s>' (Lord) is considered [significant]. || Lbh 1.5.106 ||
By virtue of being <s>Bhagavān</s>, omniscience and the possession of auspicious qualities [are established]; from the other [aspect],

children.text: brahmatvaṃ kevalatvena labhyate tatra ca sphuṭam // Lbh_1,5.107 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmatva</s> (the nature of Brahman) is clearly obtained through <s>kevala</s> (pure, unqualified) nature. || Lbh 1.5.107 ||
Although, on account of <s>Brahman</s>-nature, there would be <s>taṭasthatā</s> (marginal neutrality) everywhere,
Nevertheless, by virtue of the pair of primary qualities, there would be favorability toward devotees. || Lbh 1.5.108 ||

children.text: nanv ekasya svarūpasya dvairūpyaṃ katham ekadā |
children.translated_text: But how can one single essential nature have a twofold form simultaneously?
To this he replies with 'arvācīna' (recent) etc. — For such disputants,
When there is no occasion for debate, that [reality] is beyond their perception. || Lbh 1.5.109 ||
Therefore, by placing at the center that <s>acintya-ātma-śakti</s> (inconceivable self-potency), this difficult [proposition] —

children.text: ko nv arthaḥ syād viruddho'pi tathaivāsyā hy acintyatā |
children.translated_text: What meaning, even if contradictory, could not be [resolved]? For such indeed is the inconceivability of that [potency],

children.text: sā ca nānāviruddhānāṃ kāryāṇām āśrayān matā // Lbh_1,5.110 //
children.translated_text: And she is regarded as the basis of various mutually contradictory effects. || Lbh 1.5.110 ||

children.text: śrutes tu śabda-mūlatvād iti ca brahma-sūtra-kṛt |
children.translated_text: The author of the <s>Brahma-sūtras</s> [states]: 'But from scripture, since [Vedic knowledge] is rooted in the word';

children.text: acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃs tarkeṇa yojayet |
children.translated_text: 'Those things which are inconceivable should not be subjected to logical reasoning' —

children.text: iti skānda-vacas tac ca maṇyādiṣv api dṛśyate // Lbh_1,5.111 //
children.translated_text: This statement from the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, and that [inconceivability] is seen even in gems and the like. || Lbh 1.5.111 ||

children.text: tādṛśīṃ ca vinā śaktiṃ na sidhyet parameśatā |
children.translated_text: And without such a potency, supreme lordship (<s>parameśatā</s>) cannot be established,
Since His greatness is declared to be unfathomable. || Lbh 1.5.112 ||

children.text: ajñānam indra-jālaṃ vā vīkṣyate yatra kutracit |
children.translated_text: Ignorance or magic (<s>indra-jāla</s>) is observed here and there;

children.text: ato na pāramaiśvaryaṃ tena tasya prasidhyati // Lbh_1,5.113 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, supreme sovereignty is not established for Him by that [alone]. || Lbh 1.5.113 ||

children.text: tac ca tasya na hīty āha sphuṭaṃ coparatety adaḥ |
children.translated_text: That this [potency] is not absent from Him — this is clearly stated by 'and having ceased' etc.;
Likewise, for the group of six words beginning with '<s>bhagavatī</s>' etc.,

children.text: bhavet prayoga-tātparyam atra niṣphalam eva hi // Lbh_1,5.114 //
children.translated_text: The purpose of their usage would be entirely fruitless [if it were otherwise]. || Lbh 1.5.114 ||

children.text: tasmān na śāstra-yuktibhyām ubhayaṃ tad virudhyate |
children.translated_text: Therefore, neither by scripture nor by reasoning are both [aspects] contradictory.
Nevertheless, to those of varying intellects who do not know the truth as it is,

children.text: matānusārato bhāsi rajjūvat tvaṃ tathā tathā // Lbh_1,5.115 //
children.translated_text: You appear in various ways according to their views, like a rope [mistaken for a snake]. || Lbh 1.5.115 ||

children.text: nanu bhoḥ kevalaṃ jñānaṃ brahma syād bhagavān punaḥ |
children.translated_text: But, sir! <s>Brahman</s> would be mere knowledge, while <s>Bhagavān</s>
Has various attributes — thus even there a twofold essential nature is perceived.

children.text: iti prāha svarūpeti tat-svarūpasya naiva hi |
children.translated_text: To this he says with 'svarūpa' (essential nature) etc. — Of that essential nature, indeed,

children.text: kadāpi dvaitam ekasya dharma-dvayam idaṃ dhruvam // Lbh_1,5.116 //
children.translated_text: There is never duality for one [entity]; this twofold set of attributes is certain. || Lbh 1.5.116 ||
Therefore, the contradiction that is perceived among the manifestations of His potency —

children.text: tad evācintyam aiśvaryaṃ bh”ṣaṇaṃ na tu dūṣaṇam // Lbh_1,5.117 //
children.translated_text: That itself is His inconceivable sovereignty — an ornament, not a fault. || Lbh 1.5.117 ||

children.text: iyam eva virodhoktis tṛtīye'pi ca dṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: This very statement of contradiction is seen also in the Third Canto:
Activities of the actionless one, the birth of the unborn,
The taking of refuge in a fortress and flight from the fear of enemies,
The household life with women for the one who is Time itself,

children.text: svātman-rateḥ khidyati dhīr vidām iha // Lbh_1,5.118 //
children.translated_text: The distress of the intellect of the wise regarding one who delights in the Self — [all this is puzzling] here. || Lbh 1.5.118 ||
Thus.

children.text: tat tan na vāstavaṃ cet syāt vidyāṃ buddhi-bhramas tadā |
children.translated_text: If all that were not real, it would then be a delusion of the intellect —

children.text: na syād evety acintyaiva śaktir līlāsu kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: That cannot be; therefore the inconceivable potency alone is the cause of [His] pastimes.

children.text: yathā yathā ca tasyecchā sā vyanakti tathā tathā // Lbh_1,5.119 //
children.translated_text: And according to His will, she manifests accordingly. || Lbh 1.5.119 ||
Having thus spoken on a digression, the main topic is now examined.

children.text: nanu yaḥ prakṛti-svāmī yo'ntaryāmī ca puruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: But the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the master of <s>Prakṛti</s> and who is the <s>Antaryāmī</s> (inner controller) —

children.text: tābhyām adhikatā nāsya kaṃsārer upapadyate // Lbh_1,5.120 //
children.translated_text: Superiority over both of these does not befit the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> [i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>]! || Lbh 1.5.120 ||
As stated in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, First Canto (1.3.1-5) —
<s>Bhagavān</s> assumed the <s>Pauruṣa</s> (pertaining to <s>Puruṣa</s>) form, with <s>mahat-tattva</s> and other [principles],
Endowed with sixteen <s>kalās</s> (parts), in the beginning, with the desire to create the worlds. || Lbh 1.5.121 ||
Of Him who lies upon the waters, extending <s>yoga-nidrā</s> (mystic slumber),

children.text: nābhi-hradāmbujād āsīd brahmā viśva-sṛjāṃ patiḥ // Lbh_1,5.122 //
children.translated_text: From the lotus of His navel-lake arose <s>Brahmā</s>, the lord of the creators of the universe. || Lbh 1.5.122 ||
By the configurations of whose limbs the expanse of the worlds was fashioned —

children.text: tad vai bhagavato rūpaṃ viśuddhaṃ sattvam ūrjitam // Lbh_1,5.123 //
children.translated_text: That indeed is the form of <s>Bhagavān</s>, pure <s>sattva</s> (goodness), mighty. || Lbh 1.5.123 ||
They behold that form with unobstructed vision —
Wondrous, with thousands of feet, thighs, arms, and faces,
With thousands of heads, ears, eyes, and noses,
Resplendent with thousands of crowns, garments, and earrings. || Lbh 1.5.124 ||
This is the imperishable reservoir and seed of the various incarnations,
By a portion of whose portion are created the gods, animals, humans, and others. || Lbh 1.5.125 ||
Thus.
Here the explanatory verses:
In the beginning, before all incarnations, <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Puruṣottama</s>,
With <s>mahat-tattva</s> and other [principles], for the sake of creating the worlds — || Lbh 1.5.125 ||
The <s>Pauruṣa</s> form, having the form of <s>Puruṣa</s>, or called <s>Puruṣa</s>,
That form, an embodiment of bliss and consciousness, He assumed and manifested. || Lbh 1.5.126 ||
The meaning of the word '<s>sambhūta</s>' is 'truly, perfectly';

children.text: sambhūtaṃ yuktam iti vā bhuvanānāṃ sisṛkṣayā |
children.translated_text: Or '<s>sambhūta</s>' means 'fitting' — for the sake of creating the worlds;

children.text: ṣoḍaśaiva kalā yasmiṃs tat ṣoḍaśa-kalaṃ matam // Lbh_1,5.127 //
children.translated_text: That in which there are exactly sixteen <s>kalās</s> (portions) is called '<s>ṣoḍaśa-kala</s>' (having sixteen portions). || Lbh 1.5.127 ||
These sixteen <s>kalās</s> are declared by <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> based on scriptural evidence,

children.text: śaktitvena ca tā bhakti-vivekādiṣu sammatāḥ // Lbh_1,5.128 //
children.translated_text: And as potencies (<s>śaktis</s>), they are accepted in works on discrimination of devotion. || Lbh 1.5.128 ||

children.text: śrīr bhūḥ kīrtir ilā līlā kāntir vidyeti saptakam |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Bhū</s>, <s>Kīrti</s>, <s>Ilā</s>, <s>Līlā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, and <s>Vidyā</s> — these seven,

children.text: vimalādyā navety etā mukhyāḥ ṣoḍaśa śaktayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.129 //
children.translated_text: And nine beginning with <s>Vimalā</s> — these are the principal sixteen potencies (<s>śaktis</s>). || Lbh 1.5.129 ||
Thus.

children.text: tad idaṃ pauruṣaṃ rūpaṃ trividhaṃ pūrvam īritam |
children.translated_text: This <s>Pauruṣa</s> form, previously stated to be threefold —

children.text: tatra procya mahat-sraṣṭṛ-rūpam aṇḍa-stham ucyate // Lbh_1,5.130 //
children.translated_text: Having described the form that creates the <s>mahat</s>, now the form within the cosmic egg is described. || Lbh 1.5.130 ||
That He whose entry into the cosmic egg and lying on those waters

children.text: nābhihradāmbujād āsīd iti suvyaktam eva hi // Lbh_1,5.131 //
children.translated_text: Gave rise to <s>Brahmā</s> from the lotus of His navel-lake — this is indeed very clear. || Lbh 1.5.131 ||
The parts of that navel-lake lotus — pericarp and others —

children.text: saṃsthānāny atra vidyā-sa-viśeṣās tais tu kalpitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Are the specific configurations; by these was fashioned

children.text: lokānāṃ sarva-jagatāṃ vistāro vitatiḥ kila // Lbh_1,5.132 //
children.translated_text: The expansion, the extent of the worlds, of all the universes. || Lbh 1.5.132 ||

children.text: sa śete yena rūpeṇa tac chuddhaṃ sattvam ūrjitam // Lbh_1,5.133 //
children.translated_text: The form in which He lies — that is pure <s>sattva</s> (goodness), powerful. || Lbh 1.5.133 ||
With the verse beginning 'They behold' etc., this same form is distinguished;
This form is the source of the arising of the various incarnations. || Lbh 1.5.134 ||
With the five elements self-created,
Having fashioned the body of <s>Virāj</s>, in that,
Entered by His own portion, He obtained the designation '<s>Puruṣa</s>' —
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the primeval God. || Lbh 1.5.135 ||
As stated in the Eleventh Canto (11.4.3) —
Here, a verse and a half:
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> here is the Lord of <s>Parama-vyoma</s> (the supreme sky); He, by Himself,

children.text: puṃsvarūpeṇa sṛṣṭais tair bhūtaiḥ sṛṣṭvā virāṭ-tanum |
children.translated_text: Through the <s>Puruṣa</s>-form, with those elements He created, having fashioned the body of <s>Virāṭ</s>,

children.text: viṣṭaḥ svāṃśena tenaiva samprāptaḥ puruṣābhidhām // Lbh_1,5.136 //
children.translated_text: Entered by that very own portion, obtained the designation '<s>Puruṣa</s>.' || Lbh 1.5.136 ||

children.text: prastute tu kim āyātam ity āśaṅkya nigadyate |
children.translated_text: Now, lest one wonder what this has to do with the topic at hand, it is said:
That four-armed one who is a <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime expansion) of the one lying in the <s>Garbhodaka</s> (ocean within the cosmic egg),

children.text: śete praviśya lokābjaṃ viṣṇv-ākhyaḥ kṣīra-vāridhau // Lbh_1,5.137 //
children.translated_text: Who lies having entered the world-lotus, called <s>Viṣṇu</s>, on the ocean of milk. || Lbh 1.5.137 ||
And this one, having attained the status of <s>Antaryāmī</s> (inner controller) of all embodied beings

children.text: hṛdy-antaryāmitāṃ prāpto nānā-rūpa iva sthitaḥ // Lbh_1,5.138 //
children.translated_text: From creators (<s>sryas</s>) down to immobile entities, appears as if in many forms. || Lbh 1.5.138 ||

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ sarva-bhūta-stham iti viṣṇor yad ucyate |
children.translated_text: The third form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, said to be 'dwelling in all beings' —
That is accepted in the <s>Sātvata Tantra</s> as a <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime expansion) of this very one. || Lbh 1.5.139 ||
See above 1.2.9, quote from <s>Sātvata Tantra</s>.
Therefore, it is fitting that this very one, approached by the gods on the shore of the milk-ocean,

children.text: eṣa evāvatīrṇo'bhūt kṛṣṇākhya iti yujyate // Lbh_1,5.140 //
children.translated_text: Is the one who descended, named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. || Lbh 1.5.140 ||
Now, in response to the objection, the conclusion is established:

children.text: yathā śrī-daśame teṣu sureṣv evāśarīragīḥ // Lbh_1,5.141 //
children.translated_text: As in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, Tenth Canto — a bodiless voice [spoke] to those very gods: || Lbh 1.5.141 ||
'In the house of <s>Vasudeva</s>, directly, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>,
Will be born; for His pleasure, let the wives of the gods take birth.' || Lbh 1.5.142 ||
Thus (BhP 10.1.23).
Here the explanatory verses:

children.text: puruṣasya paratvena sākṣāc ca bhagavān iti |
children.translated_text: By 'Supreme' and 'directly' and '<s>Bhagavān</s>' —

children.text: etasyaiva mahat-sraṣṭā so'ṃśa ity abhiviśrutaḥ // Lbh_1,5.143 //
children.translated_text: The one who creates the <s>mahat</s> [tattva] is well-known as His <s>aṃśa</s> (portion). || Lbh 1.5.143 ||
Here even the view of <s>Śrī Svāmī-pāda</s> (<s>Śrīdhara Svāmī</s>) is seen to concur,

children.text: yad aṃśabhāgenety asya vyākhyāṃ kurvadbhir eva taiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since in his commentary on '<s>aṃśabhāgena</s>' (by a portion of a portion) —

children.text: aṃśena bhāgo māyāyā yenety aṃśo'sya puruṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Aṃśa</s>' means <s>māyā</s>'s portion, '<s>aṃśa</s>' means His <s>Puruṣa</s>,

children.text: bhāgo bhajanam ity evaṃ pūrṇatāsya sphuṭīkṛtā // Lbh_1,5.144 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhāga</s>' means <s>bhajana</s> (worship) — thus His fullness (<s>pūrṇatā</s>) is made clear. || Lbh 1.5.144 ||

children.text: kiṃ ca tatraiva devakyā kṛte stotre nirūpitam // Lbh_1,5.145 //
children.translated_text: Furthermore, in that same text, in the hymn composed for <s>Devakī</s>, it is established: || Lbh 1.5.145 ||
He by a portion of a portion of a portion of whose portion
The creation, dissolution, and re-creation of the universe occur —
O soul of the universe,

children.text: taṃ tv ādyāhaṃ gatiṃ gatā // Lbh_1,5.146 //
children.translated_text: To Him, the primeval one, I have now taken refuge. || Lbh 1.5.146 ||
As follows (10.85.31) —
Here the explanatory verse:

children.text: yasyāṃśaḥ puruṣasya syād aṃśaḥ prakṛtis tu sā |
children.translated_text: His <s>aṃśa</s> (portion) is the <s>Puruṣa</s>; His [the Puruṣa's] portion is <s>Prakṛti</s>;

children.text: tasyā aṃśā guṇās teṣāṃ bhāgenāsyodbhavādayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.147 //
children.translated_text: Her portions are the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities); by their portion arise creation and other [functions]. || Lbh 1.5.147 ||
You are not <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> — for You are the Self of all embodied beings,
The Supreme Lord, the witness of all worlds;
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is Your limb (<s>aṅga</s>), since His abode is in the waters born of the human (<s>nara</s>) [form] and the earth;

children.text: tac cāpi satyaṃ na tavaiva māyā // Lbh_1,5.148 //
children.translated_text: And even that is true, not Your <s>māyā</s> (illusion). || Lbh 1.5.148 ||
Furthermore, in the same text (10.14.14) —
Thus.
Here the explanatory verses:
Having called <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' with the verse 'of the three worlds,' and then
Having himself witnessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s wondrous supreme sovereignty —
Perceiving myriads of cosmic eggs, overwhelmed with fear,

children.text: nārāyaṇas tvaṃ nety āha sāparādha ivātmabhūḥ // Lbh_1,5.149 //
children.translated_text: <s>Ātmabhū</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), as if guilty, says: 'You are not [merely] <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>!' || Lbh 1.5.149 ||
'O Supreme Lord (<s>Adhīśa</s>)!' — The <s>Puruṣas</s> who are <s>Antaryāmīs</s> (inner controllers) dwelling in the multitude of cosmic eggs
Are lords; the one who is superior to them is the Supreme Lord. Since You are the illuminator
Of all collective beings including the <s>jīvas</s> with <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: teṣām akhila-lokānāṃ sākṣī draṣṭāpy asi svayam // Lbh_1,5.150 //
children.translated_text: You are also Yourself the witness, the seer of all those worlds. || Lbh 1.5.150 ||
Therefore, the one known as <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> because His abode is in the waters born of <s>Nara</s> (man), earth, and water —
He is Your limb, Your portion, O complete one. Through the glories of <s>cit</s> (consciousness) and <s>māyā</s> (illusion) potencies,

children.text: cātuṣpādikam aiśvaryaṃ tava tasya tu pādikam // Lbh_1,5.151 //
children.translated_text: Your sovereignty is fourfold, while His is only a quarter. || Lbh 1.5.151 ||

children.text: viṣṭabhyāham idaṃ kṛtsnam ekāṃśeneti te vacaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having pervaded this entire [creation] with one portion of Myself' — these are Your words;

children.text: tac cāṃśatvaṃ bhavet satyaṃ virāḍvan na tu māyikam // Lbh_1,5.152 //
children.translated_text: And that 'portion-hood' is true — like <s>Virāṭ</s> — not illusory. || Lbh 1.5.152 ||
Those who are lords of the cosmic eggs, living by depending
On the duration of a single breath of His —

children.text: viṣṇur mahān sa iha yasya kalā-viśeṣo
children.translated_text: The great <s>Viṣṇu</s> (Mahā-Viṣṇu) is but a specific <s>kalā</s> (portion) of Him here;

children.text: govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi // Lbh_1,5.153 //
children.translated_text: I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person. || Lbh 1.5.153 ||
In the <s>Śrī Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.48) —

children.text: ataḥ puruṣa evāsya kṛṣṇasyāṃśo bhaved yadi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, if the <s>Puruṣa</s> Himself is a portion (<s>aṃśa</s>) of this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: tad-vilāsas tu nitarāṃ bhavet kṣīrābdhi-nāyakaḥ // Lbh_1,5.154 //
children.translated_text: Then all the more would the Lord of the milk-ocean be His <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime expansion). || Lbh 1.5.154 ||

children.text: nanu dvitīya-skandhe tu yo'vatīrṇo yadoḥ kule |
children.translated_text: But in the Second Canto, is the one who descended in the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty

children.text: kiṃ vidhātrā sa hi sita-kṛṣṇa-keśatayoditaḥ // Lbh_1,5.155 //
children.translated_text: Described by the Creator as having white and black hairs? || Lbh 1.5.155 ||
Of the earth, trampled by the armies of foes of the gods,
For the removal of her affliction, with His <s>kalā</s> (art/portion), with white and black hairs,
He is born and will perform deeds whose path is imperceptible to people,
Deeds that are rooted in His own greatness. || Lbh 1.5.156 ||
As follows (2.7.26) —
Thus.

children.text: maivaṃ bhoḥ śrūyatām asya padyasārtho vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: Not so, friends! Hear — the meaning of this verse is properly construed as follows:
By '<s>kalā</s>' (meaning skillful artistry), with a special method of craftsmanship, the white

children.text: baddhāḥ kṛṣṇā atiśyāmāḥ keśā yeneti vigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: And black — that is, extremely dark — hairs are bound; the one who is thus [described] —
By this, His preeminence in special aesthetic skill is proclaimed. || Lbh 1.5.157 ||
Alternatively, the one who by His <s>kalā</s> (portion) would have white and dark hairs —
That very <s>Śrī Līlā-Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Person of pastimes) has descended here. || Lbh 1.5.158 ||
Furthermore —
In the <s>Viṣṇu-dharmottara</s>, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> clearly tells <s>Vajra</s>:

children.text: layābdhistho'niruddho'yaṃ pitā te iti kīrtitam // Lbh_1,5.159 //
children.translated_text: 'This <s>Aniruddha</s>, lying in the waters of dissolution, is your father.' || Lbh 1.5.159 ||
There, <s>Vajra</s>'s question — (1.79.1):

children.text: kas tv asau bāla-rūpeṇa kalpānteṣu punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Who is He who, in the form of a child, again and again at the ends of <s>kalpas</s>,

children.text: dṛṣṭo yo na tvayā jñātas tatra kautūhalaṃ mama // Lbh_1,5.160 //
children.translated_text: Was seen by you but not recognized? I am curious about this.' || Lbh 1.5.160 ||
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>'s reply — (1.79.2-3):

children.text: bhūyo bhūyas tva asau dṛṣṭo mayā devo jagat-patiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Again and again that God, the Lord of the universe, was seen by me.'

children.text: kalpa-kṣaye na vijñātaḥ sa mayā mohitena vai // Lbh_1,5.161 //
children.translated_text: At the end of the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle), He was not recognized by me, deluded as I was. // Lbh_1,5.161 //

children.text: kalpa-kṣaye vyatīte tu taṃ tu devaṃ pitāmahāt |
children.translated_text: When the end of the <s>kalpa</s> had passed, that god, from the grandsire (<s>Pitāmaha</s>, Brahmā),

children.text: aniruddhaṃ vijānāmi pitaraṃ te jagat-patim // Lbh_1,5.162 //
children.translated_text: <s>Aniruddha</s> — I know Him to be your father, the lord of the universe. // Lbh_1,5.162 //
Thus.
Here is a verse (<s>kārikā</s>) —
Otherwise, in the year of the sage (<s>Muni-varṣa</s>), he would have said this then:

children.text: taṃ śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ vijānāmi prapitāmaham eva te // Lbh_1,5.163 //
children.translated_text: 'I know Him to be <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the great-grandfather of yours.' // Lbh_1,5.163 //
Therefore, the misconception of His being a mere hair (<s>keśa</s>) incarnation is also thoroughly refuted. // Lbh_1,5.164 //
Granted, let there be supremacy of that enemy of sin (<s>Aghāri</s>) over <s>Puruṣa</s> and the others;
but <s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s> here, endowed with all sovereign powers,
stands as if in various forms in the three-quartered abode and the one-quartered domain.
His radiance is supremely sweet like an emerging young sun,
sometimes dark like a fresh rain-cloud, sometimes golden like <s>jāmbūnada</s> gold.
He is renowned as the <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime expansion) of the Lord of <s>Mahā-Vaikuṇṭha</s>,
the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self), endowed with strength, knowledge, valor, and splendor. // Lbh_1,5.165 //
The group of four <s>vyūhas</s> (emanations) known by the designation 'great states' (<s>mahāvasthā</s>) —
of these, this one (<s>Vāsudeva</s>) is the first, and thus He is to be meditated upon in the mind as the presiding deity,

children.text: tathā viśuddha-sattvasya yaś cādhiṣṭhānam ucyate // Lbh_1,5.166 //
children.translated_text: and He is also said to be the substrate of <s>viśuddha-sattva</s> (pure goodness). // Lbh_1,5.166 //
He whose own portion (<s>nijāṃśa</s>) is the Lord <s>Śrī Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: yasya saṅkarṣaṇo vyūho dvitīya iti sammataḥ |
children.translated_text: whose <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> <s>vyūha</s> is accepted as the second,
and who is also the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), being the locus of the manifestation of all <s>jīvas</s>. // Lbh_1,5.167 //
His radiance is supremely sweet like a full autumn moon,
He is to be meditated upon in the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego principle), and He has delegated His own portion to <s>Śeṣa</s>.
Of the enemy of <s>Smara</s> (Śiva), of <s>Adharma</s> (unrighteousness), of <s>Sarpāntaka</s> (Garuḍa), and of the enemies of the gods,
having assumed the role of inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>), He is the cause of the dissolution of the universe. // Lbh_1,5.168 //

children.text: vyūhas tṛtīyaḥ pradyumno vilāso yasya viśrutaḥ |
children.translated_text: The third <s>vyūha</s> is <s>Pradyumna</s>, whose <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime form) is renowned;
that <s>Pradyumna</s> is worshipped in the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> (intellect principle) by the wise.

children.text: stuvatyā ca śriyā devyā niṣevyate ilāvṛte |
children.translated_text: He is served by the praising goddess <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) in <s>Ilāvṛta</s>;
He is of pure golden (<s>jāmbūnada</s>) complexion, sometimes of dark rain-cloud hue.
He is the origin of the creation of the universe, having delegated His own portion to <s>Kāma</s> (the god of love);

children.text: vidheḥ prajāpatīnāṃ rāgināṃ ca smarasya ca |
children.translated_text: of <s>Vidhi</s> (Brahmā), of the <s>Prajāpatis</s> (lords of progeny), of lovers, and of <s>Smara</s> (the god of desire),

children.text: antaryāmitvam āpannaḥ sargaṃ samyak karoty asau // Lbh_1,5.169 //
children.translated_text: having assumed the role of inner controller, He properly carries out creation. // Lbh_1,5.169 //
The fourth <s>vyūha</s>, called <s>Aniruddha</s>, whose <s>vilāsa</s> is praised —
that <s>Aniruddha</s> is worshipped in the <s>manas-tattva</s> (mind principle) by the wise.
Resembling a dark rain-cloud, He is devoted to the protection of the universe;

children.text: dharmasyāyaṃ manūnāṃ ca devānāṃ bhūbhujāṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: of <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness), of the <s>Manus</s>, of the gods, and of the kings,

children.text: antaryāmitvam āsthāya kurute jagataḥ sthitim // Lbh_1,5.170 //
children.translated_text: having assumed the role of inner controller, He sustains the existence of the world. // Lbh_1,5.170 //
But in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s> is said to be the presiding deity of the mind,

children.text: aniruddhas tv ahaṅkārasyeti tatraiva kīrtitam // Lbh_1,5.171 //
children.translated_text: and <s>Aniruddha</s> of the <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego) — thus it is stated there. // Lbh_1,5.171 //

children.text: sarveṣāṃ pañcarātrāṇām apy eṣā prakriyā matā // Lbh_1,5.172 //
children.translated_text: This same system is accepted by all the <s>Pañcarātra</s> scriptures as well. // Lbh_1,5.172 //
But in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the four directions beginning with the east of the supreme sky (<s>parama-vyoma</s>),

children.text: vāsudevādayo vyūhaś catvāraḥ kathitāḥ kramāt // Lbh_1,5.173 //
children.translated_text: the four <s>vyūhas</s> beginning with <s>Vāsudeva</s> are described in order. // Lbh_1,5.173 //

children.text: tathā pāda-vibhūtau ca nivasanti kramādi me |
children.translated_text: And likewise, they dwell in the one-quartered domain in order, beginning with me:
in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> situated in the water-covering, in the city of <s>Vedavatī</s>,
in the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> world above <s>Satya</s>(-loka), in the eternal (<s>nitya</s>) city of <s>Dvārakā</s>,
in <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island) north of the pure waters, in the city of <s>Cairāvatī</s>,
and finally in the abode of <s>Kroḍa</s> (Varāha), resting on the couch, situated in the ocean of milk. // Lbh_1,5.174 //

children.text: sātvatīye kvacit tantre nava vyūhāḥ prakīrtitāḥ |
children.translated_text: In a certain <s>Sātvatīya Tantra</s>, nine <s>vyūhas</s> are proclaimed:
the four beginning with <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>,
<s>Hayagrīva</s>, <s>Mahākroḍa</s> (Great Boar), and <s>Brahmā</s> — thus nine are mentioned;

children.text: tatra brahmā tu vijñeyaḥ pūrvokta-vidhayā hariḥ // Lbh_1,5.175 //
children.translated_text: there, <s>Brahmā</s> should be understood as <s>Hari</s> in the manner previously described. // Lbh_1,5.175 //
But the four <s>vyūhas</s> are resplendent with four arms,
adorned with perpetual supreme sovereignty and sage-given ornaments. // Lbh_1,5.176 //
Here too, this <s>Vāsudeva</s> is an overflowing ocean of complete bliss,
undifferentiated from the Lord of the supreme sky in sovereignty and other attributes,

children.text: ādyānām api sarveṣām ādibhūtaḥ suparvaṇām // Lbh_1,5.177 //
children.translated_text: the primordial source of all the foremost gods. // Lbh_1,5.177 //

children.text: ity āśaṅke sa evāyaṃ kṛṣṇākhyaḥ sann avātarat |
children.translated_text: At this point one might suspect: He Himself, bearing the name <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, descended;
since as <s>Vāsudeva</s> He is well-known everywhere. // Lbh_1,5.178 //

children.text: naivaṃ yuktaṃ śṛṇu tataḥ samādhānaṃ vidhīyate |
children.translated_text: This is not right — hear then the resolution that is offered:

children.text: ādya-vyūhād api śreṣṭhaḥ kathyate devakī-sutaḥ // Lbh_1,5.179 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Devakī</s> is declared to be superior even to the first <s>vyūha</s>. // Lbh_1,5.179 //

children.text: ete cāṃśakalāḥ puṃsaḥ kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam // Lbh_1,5.180 //
children.translated_text: These are <s>aṃśas</s> (portions) and <s>kalās</s> (fractional portions) of the <s>Puruṣa</s>; but <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Supreme Lord) Himself. // Lbh_1,5.180 //
Thus in the glorious Tenth Canto (<s>Śrī Daśama</s>) —
Here are the verses (<s>kārikās</s>) —
Of the one called '<s>Puṃs</s>' (the <s>Puruṣa</s>), these — <s>Śrī Varāha</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s> and others —

children.text: aṃśāḥ atrāvatārāḥ syuḥ kumārādyāḥ kalā matāḥ ||
children.translated_text: are <s>aṃśas</s> (portions), here meaning <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations); <s>Kumāra</s> and others are considered <s>kalās</s> (fractions).
But — marked by the contrasting particle '<s>tu</s>' — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Supreme Lord), <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person),
'Himself' (<s>svayam</s>) — thus His being an incarnation of <s>Vāsudeva</s> is negated. // Lbh_1,5.181 //
Of this body of Yours, O Lord, which exists for my grace,
which is made of Your own will and not made of material elements — who can
fathom the greatness, O Mighty One, except by a mind that is
directly Yours alone? What to speak then of the experience of self-bliss? // Lbh_1,5.182 //
In the glorious Tenth Canto also, it is stated thus (10.14.2) —
Thus.
Here are the verses (<s>kārikās</s>) —

children.text: devaḥ sva-nāmni deveti khyātaṃ yasya vapuḥ sa hi |
children.translated_text: '<s>Deva</s>' — the famous designation; that body which bears the name '<s>deva</s>' is His;
the first of the <s>vyūhas</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, is considered to have a divine body (<s>deva-vapu</s>).

children.text: tato'pi mahi māhātmyaṃ sākṣād evātra te sataḥ |
children.translated_text: Even greater than that is the greatness directly of You who are present here;

children.text: ko vidhātāpy avasituṃ jñātuṃ neśe'smi na kṣamaḥ |
children.translated_text: who, even the Creator, is capable of fathoming it? 'I am unable' — I am not capable;
what to speak then of the <s>Brahman</s>-form, which is the experience of self-bliss! // Lbh_1,5.183 //
The meaning of this verse is established through the reasoning of <s>kaimutya</s> (a fortiori). // Lbh_1,5.184 //

children.text: nyūne'dhike ca kaimutyaṃ tatra nyūne bhaved yathā |
children.translated_text: The <s>kaimutya</s> (a fortiori) reasoning applies in both lesser and greater cases; in the lesser case, for example:
The <s>Kaustubha</s> gem is of great brilliance, surpassing even a hundred billion suns;

children.text: ayaṃ kim uta vaktavyaṃ pradīpād dīptimān iti // Lbh_1,5.185 //
children.translated_text: need it even be said that it outshines a mere lamp? // Lbh_1,5.185 //

children.text: athādhike yathā dhvāntaiḥ śakyo dīpo'pi nārditum |
children.translated_text: And in the greater case: a lamp cannot be extinguished by darkness;

children.text: sa tu mārtaṇḍa-koṭībhiḥ sama`y kim uta kaustubhaḥ // Lbh_1,5.186 //
children.translated_text: that same lamp equaling billions of suns — what to speak then of the <s>Kaustubha</s>? // Lbh_1,5.186 //

children.text: ato nyūnād api nyūne kaimutyam iha tu sthitam // Lbh_1,5.187 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, here the a fortiori reasoning is established from the even-lesser case. // Lbh_1,5.187 //
'Grace has been bestowed upon me' — the emphasis of grace is because

children.text: mayy eva vihito bhūyān apūrvāścarya-darśanāt // Lbh_1,5.188 //
children.translated_text: it was abundantly directed at me alone, due to the unprecedented and wondrous vision. // Lbh_1,5.188 //
'Made of His own will' — all His actions are for the desire of His devotees;

children.text: na tu bhūtamayasyeti puruṣatvaṃ ca khaṇḍitam |
children.translated_text: 'not made of material elements' — thus even His being the <s>Puruṣa</s> is set aside,

children.text: yad eṣa sarva-jīvānāṃ puruṣaḥ paramāśrayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.189 //
children.translated_text: since He is the <s>Puruṣa</s> who is the supreme refuge of all <s>jīvas</s>. // Lbh_1,5.189 //
'By a mind that is solely focused within' — meaning one-pointed concentration;

children.text: jñātuṃ syān mahimā śakyo yadyapy ebhir viśeṣaṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: although His greatness could be known through these qualifying attributes,
still 'I am unable' — this indicates His inconceivable sovereignty. // Lbh_1,5.190 //
By <s>Viriñca</s> (Brahmā), who knows that the greatness of <s>Kṛṣṇa-candra</s>
exceeds that of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and also of <s>Brahman</s>, this has been established. // Lbh_1,5.191 //
Therefore, in the meditation of the <s>Manu</s> mantra of fourteen syllables, in the <s>Svāyambhuva Āgama</s>,
the four (<s>vyūhas</s>) beginning with <s>Vāsudeva</s> are declared to be the covering (<s>āvṛti</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. // Lbh_1,5.192 //
And in the <s>Kramādī-dīpikā</s>, in the practice of the <s>Manu</s> mantra of eight syllables,
<s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others are considered as the covering of the Lord of <s>Gokula</s>. // Lbh_1,5.193 //

children.text: nanu śraiṣṭhyaṃ mukundasya brahmato yujyate katham |
children.translated_text: Now, how can the supremacy of <s>Mukunda</s> over <s>Brahman</s> be justified,

children.text: yad brahma śrībhāgaator aikyam eva prasidhyate // Lbh_1,5.194 //
children.translated_text: when the identity of <s>Brahman</s> with the Lord of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> is well established? // Lbh_1,5.194 //

children.text: puruṣaṃ paramātmā ca brahma ca jñānam ity api |
children.translated_text: <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Paramātmā</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, and also <s>Jñāna</s> (Knowledge) —

children.text: sa eko bhagavān eva śāstreṣu bahudhocyate // Lbh_1,5.195 //
children.translated_text: He, the one <s>Bhagavān</s> (Supreme Lord), is spoken of in many ways in the scriptures. // Lbh_1,5.195 //
And in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s> —
He is called <s>Bhagavān</s> and <s>Paramātmā</s> by the practitioners of <s>aṣṭāṅga-yoga</s> (eight-limbed yoga);

children.text: brahmety upaniṣan-niṣṭhair jñānaṃ ca jñāna-yogibhiḥ // Lbh_1,5.196 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> by those devoted to the <s>Upaniṣads</s>; and <s>Jñāna</s> (Knowledge) by the <s>jñāna-yogins</s>. // Lbh_1,5.196 //
And in the glorious First Canto (1.2.11) —

children.text: vadanti tat tattva-vidas tattvaṃ yaj jñānam advayam |
children.translated_text: The knowers of reality call that non-dual truth

children.text: brahmeti paramātmeti bhagavān iti śabdyate // Lbh_1,5.197 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Paramātmā</s>, and <s>Bhagavān</s>. // Lbh_1,5.197 //
Thus.

children.text: satyam uktaṃ śṛṇu tatas tṛtīye kāpilaṃ vacaḥ // Lbh_1,5.198 //
children.translated_text: Truly said — hear then the words of <s>Kapila</s> in the Third Canto. // Lbh_1,5.198 //
As follows (3.32.33) —
Just as an object possessing many qualities, perceived through the separate doorways of the senses,

children.text: eko nāneyate tadvad bhagavān śāstra-vartmabhiḥ // Lbh_1,5.199 //
children.translated_text: though one, is apprehended differently — so too the <s>Bhagavān</s> through the paths of scripture. // Lbh_1,5.199 //
Thus.
Here are the verses (<s>kārikās</s>) —

children.text: tat tat śrī-bhagavaty eva svarūpaṃ bhuvi vidyate |
children.translated_text: All those forms exist in the Lord <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> alone as His own nature (<s>svarūpa</s>);
according to the type of worship, they shine forth in the respective worshipper. // Lbh_1,5.200 //
Just as an object such as milk, which is always the repository of qualities like form, taste, etc.,

children.text: kṣīrādir eka evārtho jñāyate bahudhendriyaiḥ // Lbh_1,5.201 //
children.translated_text: though one, is known variously through the different senses, // Lbh_1,5.201 //

children.text: dṛśā śuklo rasanayā madhuro bhagavāṃs tathā |
children.translated_text: as white by the eye and sweet by the tongue — so too the <s>Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: upāsanābhir bahudhā sa eko'pi pratīyate // Lbh_1,5.202 //
children.translated_text: though one, is perceived in many ways through the various modes of worship. // Lbh_1,5.202 //

children.text: jihvayaiva yathā grāhyaṃ mādhuryaṃ tasya nāparaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Just as sweetness is to be grasped by the tongue alone and not by the other senses,

children.text: yathā cakṣur-ādīni gṛhṇanty arthaṃ nijaṃ nijam // Lbh_1,5.203 //
children.translated_text: and just as the eye and other senses each grasp their own respective objects, // Lbh_1,5.203 //
so all other forms of worship occupy the position of external sense organs,

children.text: bhaktis tu cetaḥ sthānīyā tat tat sarvārhta-lābhataḥ // Lbh_1,5.204 //
children.translated_text: while <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) occupies the position of the inner consciousness, due to its attaining all objects. // Lbh_1,5.204 //
Thus, in the foremost scriptures, from the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of that Lord,
the supremacy of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is declared due to the superiority of qualities like sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>). // Lbh_1,5.205 //
And thus in the glorious Tenth Canto (10.14.6-7) —
is fit to be known by those whose inner selves are pure,
from self-experience, as changeless, formless,
and knowable only through identity with You and not otherwise. // Lbh_1,5.206 //
Nevertheless, O Infinite One, the greatness of Your qualities
Who could be capable of measuring the qualities of You
who are the self of qualities and have descended for the welfare of all?
By whose well-fashioned calculations, in the course of time,
could the particles of earth, the snowflakes in the sky, or the rays of the celestial bodies be measured? // Lbh_1,5.207 //
Thus.
Now, since they are of material nature, like the objects of a mirage,

children.text: guṇānāṃ gaṇanā na syād iti kātra vicitratā // Lbh_1,5.208 //
children.translated_text: the counting of such qualities should not be possible — so what is remarkable here? // Lbh_1,5.208 //

children.text: maivaṃ guṇānām etasya prākṛtatvaṃ na vidyate |
children.translated_text: Not so — the material nature of these qualities of His does not exist;

children.text: teṣāṃ svarūpa-bhūtatvāt sukharūpatvam eva hi // Lbh_1,5.209 //
children.translated_text: because they are intrinsic to His essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), they are indeed of the nature of bliss. // Lbh_1,5.209 //
And thus in the <s>Brahma-tarka</s> —

children.text: guṇaiḥ svarūpa-bhūtais tu guṇy asau harir īśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, the Lord, possesses qualities that are intrinsic to His essential nature;

children.text: na viṣṇor na ca muktānāṃ kvāpi bhinno guṇo mataḥ // Lbh_1,5.210 //
children.translated_text: neither in <s>Viṣṇu</s> nor in the liberated souls is any quality considered separate. // Lbh_1,5.210 //
In the <s>Śrī Viṣṇu Purāṇa</s> (1.9.43) —

children.text: sattvādayo na santīśe yatra ca prākṛtā guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s> and the other material qualities (<s>guṇas</s>) do not exist in the Lord;

children.text: sa śuddhaḥ sarva-śuddhebhyaḥ pumān ādyaḥ prasīdatu // Lbh_1,5.211 //
children.translated_text: may that pure, primordial <s>Puruṣa</s>, purest of all pure beings, be pleased. // Lbh_1,5.211 //
And also there (6.5.79) —
Knowledge, power, strength, sovereignty, valor, and splendor — in their entirety,
