are denoted by the word '<s>Bhagavān</s>' — without the undesirable qualities and such. // Lbh_1,5.212 //
And in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> (6.255.39-40) —

children.text: yo'sau nirguṇa ity uktaḥ śāstreṣu jagad-īśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is declared '<s>nirguṇa</s>' (without qualities) in the scriptures, the Lord of the universe,

children.text: prākṛtair heya-saṃyuktair guṇair hīnatvam ucyate // Lbh_1,5.213 //
children.translated_text: is said to be devoid of the material, undesirable qualities. // Lbh_1,5.213 //
And in the First Canto (1.16.30) —

children.text: ete cānye ca bhagavan nityā yatra mahā-guṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: These and other great qualities, O Lord, which are eternal and present in You,

children.text: prārthyā mahattvam icchadbhir na viyanti sma karhicit // Lbh_1,5.214 //
children.translated_text: sought after by those desiring greatness — they never depart at any time. // Lbh_1,5.214 //
Thus.
Therefore, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, distinguished by tens of thousands of non-material qualities,
is this great power, a concentrated form of complete bliss. // Lbh_1,5.215 //
<s>Brahman</s>, devoid of specific attributes, without distinction, formless —

children.text: iti sūryopamasyāsya kathyate tat prabhopamam // Lbh_1,5.216 //
children.translated_text: that is described as comparable to the radiance of Him who is like the sun. // Lbh_1,5.216 //
And thus in the glorious <s>Bhagavad Gītā</s> (14.26-27) —
And one who serves Me with unwavering <s>bhakti-yoga</s> (devotional discipline),

children.text: sa guṇān samatītyaitān brahmabhūyāya kalpate // Lbh_1,5.217 //
children.translated_text: transcending these <s>guṇas</s> (material qualities), becomes fit for the state of <s>Brahman</s>. // Lbh_1,5.217 //
For I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>, of the immortal and imperishable,

children.text: śāśvatasya ca dharmasya sukhasyaikāntikasya ca // Lbh_1,5.218 //
children.translated_text: of eternal <s>dharma</s> and of absolute bliss. (Lbh 1.5.218)
Thus.
Here are the summarizing verses:
Having attained the state of <s>Brahman</s>, one should worship with love the playful form (<s>līlā-vigraha</s>) as the refuge,

children.text: mānānanda-ghanaṃ premṇā bhajed ity ayam āśrayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.219 //
children.translated_text: which is a dense mass of the bliss of divine honor — this is the purport. (Lbh 1.5.219)
The fruit of unswerving <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) is indeed loving service (<s>prema-sevā</s>);

children.text: kevalaṃ brahma-bhāvas tu vidveṣeṇāpi labhyate // Lbh_1,5.220 //
children.translated_text: whereas the mere state of <s>Brahman</s> is attainable even through enmity. (Lbh 1.5.220)

children.text: nanu te yādavasyāsya bhajanād brahmatā katham |
children.translated_text: Now, how can devotion to this <s>Yādava</s> (Kṛṣṇa) lead to the state of <s>Brahman</s>?

children.text: ity āha brahmaṇo hīti hi yato'haṃ puras tava ||
children.translated_text: To this He replies: 'Of <s>Brahman</s>, indeed' — 'for I stand here before you,
this form, full of manifold bliss, a dense mass of consciousness;
I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>, whose nature is pure consciousness, its supreme support' —

children.text: ravis tejo-ghanākāraḥ karaughasya yathā bhavet // Lbh_1,5.221 //
children.translated_text: just as the sun, a dense mass of light, is the source of its rays. (Lbh 1.5.221)
By 'imperishable nectar' (<s>avyaya-amṛta</s>), eternal liberation (<s>nitya-mukti</s>) is indicated;

children.text: śāśvatena tu dharmeṇa bhagavad-dharma ucyate // Lbh_1,5.222 //
children.translated_text: and by 'eternal <s>dharma</s>,' the <s>dharma</s> of the Lord (<s>bhagavad-dharma</s>) is meant. (Lbh 1.5.222)
By 'absolute bliss' (<s>aikāntika-sukha</s>), the festival of the rasa of <s>prema-bhakti</s> (loving devotion) is meant,
by which even the bliss of liberation is eclipsed. (Lbh 1.5.223)
He whose radiance is the source, in the millions upon millions of cosmic eggs,
of innumerable earths and other glories, each distinct —
that <s>Brahman</s>, undivided, infinite, all-pervading,

children.text: govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi // Lbh_1,5.224 //
children.translated_text: that primeval person <s>Govinda</s>, Him I worship. (Lbh 1.5.224)
Furthermore, in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.40):
Thus.
Here are two summarizing verses:
That which is of undivided nature and so forth, in the billions of cosmic eggs,
becomes differentiated through the glories of earth and other elements, reaching a state of distinction.

children.text: sadā prabhāva-yuktasya brahma yasya prabhā bhavet |
children.translated_text: Of Him who is ever endowed with power, <s>Brahman</s> is merely the effulgence —

children.text: taṃ govindaṃ bhajāmīti padyasyārthaḥ sphuṭīkṛtaḥ // Lbh_1,5.225 //
children.translated_text: 'That <s>Govinda</s> I worship' — the meaning of the verse is thus made clear. (Lbh 1.5.225)

children.text: nanu bhos tava bhāvo'yaṃ jñāta eva mayā dhruvam |
children.translated_text: Now, friend, this view of yours is indeed well known to me:
that <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is called an <s>avatāra</s> (descent) of the Lord of <s>Paravyoma</s> (the supreme sky). (Lbh 1.5.226)
Due to the manifestation of birth and other <s>līlās</s> (pastimes), even though He is called an <s>avatāra</s>,

children.text: prokto vilāsa eva syāt sarvotkarṣātibhūmataḥ // Lbh_1,5.227 //
children.translated_text: He should be understood as a <s>vilāsa</s> (expansion for play), due to His supreme, unsurpassed excellence. (Lbh 1.5.227)
He who is the Lord of <s>Paravyoma</s> (the supreme sky), of unequaled and unsurpassed glory,
whose supreme excellence is described in the <s>Śrutis</s>, <s>Smṛtis</s>, and the great <s>Tantras</s> —

children.text: loka-sṛṣṭeḥ purā brāhme kalpe yaḥ parameṣṭhine |
children.translated_text: He who, before the creation of the worlds, in the <s>Brāhma-kalpa</s>, to <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),
revealed His own self, situated in <s>Mahā-Vaikuṇṭha-loka</s>. (Lbh 1.5.228)
As stated in the glorious Second Canto (2.9.9-16):
showed His own abode, beyond which there is nothing higher,
free from affliction, delusion, and fear,
praised by those who have directly beheld the Self. (Lbh 1.5.229)
To him (<s>Brahmā</s>), who had duly worshipped Him, the Lord
Where neither <s>rajas</s> nor <s>tamas</s> prevails, nor

children.text: sattvaṃ ca miśraṃ na ca kāla-vikramaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>sattva</s> mixed with those two, nor the force of Time;

children.text: na yatra māyā kim utāpare harer
children.translated_text: where <s>māyā</s> does not exist — what to speak of other things? — where the devoted attendants of <s>Hari</s>,
worshipped by gods and demons alike, dwell. (Lbh 1.5.230)
all four-armed, with flashing gems,
the finest gold ornaments, of brilliant splendor,
of the hue of coral, <s>vaidūrya</s> (cat's-eye gem), and lotus stalks,
adorned with glittering earrings, diadems, and garlands. (Lbh 1.5.231)
Dark-complexioned and fair, lotus-eyed, clad in yellow garments, of beautiful complexion and fine form,
He shines, surrounded on all sides by the radiant
arrays of gleaming aerial vehicles of great souls,
illuminated by the splendor of the most excellent women —
like the sky with rows of lightning-bearing clouds. (Lbh 1.5.232)
<s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), who is present there in bodily form, at the feet of the glorious Lord,
renders service in manifold ways through her powers;
seated on a swing, attended by followers of the seasons of flowers,
being celebrated in song, she sings of the beloved deeds of the Lord. (Lbh 1.5.233)
He (<s>Brahmā</s>) beheld there the Lord of all <s>Sātvatas</s>,
the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>, Lord of sacrifices, Lord of the universe,
attended by <s>Sunanda</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Prabala</s>, <s>Arhaṇa</s>, and others,
His foremost attendants — the all-pervading Lord,
whose face was turned with grace toward His servants, whose glance was intoxicating,
whose face bore a serene smile and reddish-tinged eyes,
crowned, wearing earrings, four-armed,
clad in yellow silk, with <s>Śrī</s> (the mark of <s>Lakṣmī</s>) visible on His chest,
seated on the most worshipful throne, the Supreme,
surrounded by twenty-five powers — four, sixteen, and five,
endowed with His own eternally inherent <s>bhagas</s> (divine attributes), while elsewhere they are transient,

children.text: sva eva dhāman ramamāṇam īśvaram // Lbh_1,5.234 //
children.translated_text: the Lord, sporting in His own abode. (Lbh 1.5.234)
Thus.
Here are the summarizing verses:

children.text: yad yataḥ param utkṛṣṭaṃ padam anyan na hi kvacit |
children.translated_text: That from which there is nothing higher or more exalted anywhere —
afflictions of five kinds beginning with <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), delusion being lack of discrimination,

children.text: sādhvasaṃ pātato bhītir na santy etāni yatra tam |
children.translated_text: fear being dread of falling — where none of these exist — that realm.

children.text: sva-dṛṣṭam ātmanaḥ sākṣāt kāras tadvadbhir īḍitam // Lbh_1,5.235 //
children.translated_text: 'Seen by the Self directly' means praised by those who have directly realized it. (Lbh 1.5.235)

children.text: rajas tamaś ca no yatra sattvaṃ sadhryak tayor na ca |
children.translated_text: Where neither <s>rajas</s> nor <s>tamas</s> exists, nor <s>sattva</s> purely, nor the two combined,

children.text: guṇā yatra prakṛtijā na satnīti pradarśitam ||
children.translated_text: where the <s>guṇas</s> born of <s>Prakṛti</s> do not exist — this is demonstrated.
Where there is no force of Time, meaning the cause of universal destruction,

children.text: paraṃ mūlam anarthānāṃ yatra māyaiva nāsti hi ||
children.translated_text: where the very root of all misfortune, <s>māyā</s> itself, does not exist,

children.text: apare tatra kim uta vikārā mahad-ādayaḥ |
children.translated_text: what to speak of its derivatives — the transformations beginning with <s>mahat</s>?
Thus the eternally perfected nature of <s>Vaikuṇṭha-loka</s> is established. (Lbh 1.5.236)
The devoted followers of <s>Hari</s> there — dark, ruddy, green, and white —
have attained forms similar to the Lord of the corresponding colors whom they worship,

children.text: athavā nitya-siddhatvāt tad-rucām apy anāditā // Lbh_1,5.237 //
children.translated_text: or, since they are eternally perfected, their complexions too are beginningless. (Lbh 1.5.237)
<s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), who is the embodiment of divine opulence, present in form, born from a portion of the lotus,
renders service in manifold ways through various powers.
By the word '<s>kusumākara</s>' (flower-maker), the lord of the seasons (Spring) is understood;

children.text: tena tasyānugair grīṣma-varṣādyair ṛtubhiś ca yā ||
children.translated_text: by his followers — the seasons of summer, monsoon, and so on —
even while being specially glorified, she sings only of the beloved deeds of the Lord.

children.text: śatrantena padenātra tiṅ-antā lakṣitā kriyā // Lbh_1,5.238 //
children.translated_text: 'By the verbal ending (<s>śatṛ</s>), a finite verb action is indicated here.' (Lbh 1.5.238)
There he beheld the Lord — of what nature? 'An intoxicant of the eyes' (<s>dṛg-āsava</s>) —

children.text: sāndrānandair dṛśāṃ suṣṭhu mādakatvāt sa āsavaḥ // Lbh_1,5.239 //
children.translated_text: because His glances thoroughly intoxicate through intense bliss, He is called <s>āsava</s> (intoxicating liquor). (Lbh 1.5.239)
By the phrase 'clad in yellow silk,' His dark (<s>śyāma</s>) complexion is implied. (Lbh 1.5.240)
By the word '<s>adhyarhaṇīya</s>' (most worshipful), the throne called <s>Mahā-yoga</s> is meant;
as described in the <s>Padma-uttara-khaṇḍa</s>, it will be explained here further on. (Lbh 1.5.241)
Four powers are known: <s>Hlādinī</s>, <s>Kīrti</s>, <s>Karuṇā</s>, and <s>Tuṣṭi</s>;

children.text: śaktayaḥ ṣoḍaśātraiva pūryam eva pradarśitāḥ // Lbh_1,5.242 //
children.translated_text: the sixteen powers here are simply the city itself as previously described. (Lbh 1.5.242)

children.text: vidyāyāḥ pañca-parvāṇi sāṅkhyādīny atra pañca ca // Lbh_1,5.243 //
children.translated_text: The five divisions of <s>Vidyā</s> — <s>Sāṅkhya</s> and the others — are the five here. (Lbh 1.5.243)
Those are stated in the <s>Pañcarātra</s>:

children.text: sāṅkhya-yogau tu vairāgyaṃ tapo bhaktiś ca keśave |
children.translated_text: '<s>Sāṅkhya</s>, <s>Yoga</s>, renunciation (<s>vairāgya</s>), austerity (<s>tapas</s>), and devotion to <s>Keśava</s> —

children.text: pañca-parveti vidyeyaṃ yayā vidvān hariṃ viśet // Lbh_1,5.244 //
children.translated_text: this <s>Vidyā</s> is known as having five divisions, by which the wise one enters <s>Hari</s>.' (Lbh 1.5.244)
Thus.

children.text: ity etābhir vṛtaṃ pañca-viṃśatyā śaktibhiḥ sadā |
children.translated_text: Thus, He is always surrounded by these twenty-five powers;
endowed with the <s>bhagas</s> (divine attributes) — lordship (<s>aiśvarya</s>), righteousness (<s>dharma</s>), and so on — which are naturally and inherently His own,
while in others such as <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) these are unsteady, transient, and diminished;

children.text: sva eva dhāmni vaikuṇṭhe ratiṃ vidadhataṃ sadā |
children.translated_text: in His own abode, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, He forever delights.

children.text: kiṃ vā svarūpa-bhūtatvāt śriyas tasyāḥ svadhāmatā // Lbh_1,5.245 //
children.translated_text: Or rather, since <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) is inherent to His very nature, His abode is indeed hers. (Lbh 1.5.245)
And thus in the <s>Bhārgava-tantra</s>:
'Between the <s>Śakti</s> (power) and the <s>Śaktimān</s> (possessor of power), there is no distinction whatsoever;
though undivided, She is spoken of separately by words such as "<s>svecchā</s>" (own will) and others.'
Thus. (Lbh 1.5.246)
Furthermore, in the <s>Padma-uttara-khaṇḍa</s> (6.255.57-64):
Between <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>Parama-vyoman</s> (the supreme sky) flows the river <s>Virajā</s>,
auspicious, flowing with waters born from the perspiration of the limbs of the <s>Vedas</s>. (Lbh 1.5.247)
Beyond that river, in <s>Paravyoma</s>, the eternal, comprising three-fourths (<s>tripād</s>),

children.text: amṛtaṃ śāśvataṃ nityam anantaṃ paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: immortal, everlasting, perpetual, infinite — the supreme abode,
composed of pure <s>sattva</s> (<s>śuddha-sattva</s>), divine, imperishable — the abode of <s>Brahman</s>,
of brilliance equal to millions of suns and fires, imperishable,
consisting of all the <s>Vedas</s>, radiant, free from all dissolution,
golden, the abode of liberation, called the bliss of <s>Brahman</s>,
devoid of superior or equal, without beginning or end, auspicious,
of most wondrous splendor, delightful, an eternal ocean of bliss —

children.text: evam ādi-guṇopetaṃ tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: endowed with such primordial qualities — that is the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: na tad bhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Neither the sun illumines it, nor the moon, nor fire;

children.text: yad gatvā na nivartante tad dhāma paramaṃ hareḥ // Lbh_1,5.248 //
children.translated_text: having gone there, they do not return — that is the supreme abode of <s>Hari</s>. (Lbh 1.5.248)

children.text: tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ dhāma śāśvataṃ nityam acyutam |
children.translated_text: That supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, eternal, perpetual, imperishable —

children.text: na hi varṇayituṃ śakyaṃ kalpa-koṭi-śatair api // Lbh_1,5.249 //
children.translated_text: it cannot be described even in hundreds of billions of <s>kalpas</s>. (Lbh 1.5.249)
Further on in the same text (6.256.9-21):
Nourished by the taste of devotion and service to the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s> (the bow),
those great souls, most fortunate, servants at the feet of the Lord, (Lbh 1.5.250)

children.text: tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ dhāma yānti prema-sukha-pradam |
children.translated_text: they go to that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, which bestows the bliss of <s>prema</s> (divine love),
filled with various communities — that <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the abode of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: prakāraiś ca vimānaiś ca saudhai ratnamayair vṛtam // Lbh_1,5.251 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by ramparts, aerial vehicles, and palaces made of jewels. (Lbh 1.5.251)

children.text: tan madhye nagarī divyā sāyondhyeti prakīrtitā |
children.translated_text: In the midst of it is a divine city, celebrated as <s>Sā-Ayodhyā</s>,
surrounded by walls and gateways adorned with gems and gold, resplendent,
having four gates, enclosed by jeweled tower-gates. (Lbh 1.5.252)
Well-guarded by door-keepers beginning with <s>Caṇḍa</s>, and <s>Kumuda</s> and others:
<s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Pracaṇḍa</s> at the eastern gate, <s>Bhadra</s> and <s>Subhadra</s> at the southern,
<s>Jaya</s> and <s>Vijaya</s> at the western, <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> at the northern. (Lbh 1.5.253)
<s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Kumudākṣa</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>Vāmana</s>,
<s>Śaṅku-karṇa</s>, <s>Sarva-netra</s>, <s>Sumukha</s>, and <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s> —

children.text: ete dik-patayaḥ proktāḥ pūryām atra śubhānane // Lbh_1,5.254 //
children.translated_text: these are declared the guardians of the directions in the city, O beautiful-faced one. (Lbh 1.5.254)
Surrounded by rows of houses blazing like millions of fires,
filled with eternal divine women and men in the bloom of youth. (Lbh 1.5.255)

children.text: antaḥpuras tu devasya madhye pūryā manoharam |
children.translated_text: The inner palace of the Lord, in the center of the city, is enchanting,
fitted with jeweled ramparts, graced with excellent gateways,

children.text: vimānair gṛhamukhyaiś ca prāsādair bahubhir vṛtam |
children.translated_text: surrounded by aerial vehicles, chief mansions, and many palaces,
adorned on all sides by hosts of divine <s>Apsaras</s> women. (Lbh 1.5.256)

children.text: madhye tu maṇḍapaṃ divyaṃ rājasthānaṃ mahotsavam |
children.translated_text: In the center is a divine pavilion, the royal hall of great celebration,
adorned with thousands of ruby pillars, made of jewels, auspicious,
filled with eternally liberated souls, graced by the singing of <s>Sāma</s> hymns. (Lbh 1.5.257)
In the center is a beautiful throne, consisting of all the <s>Vedas</s>, auspicious,
surrounded by the eternal presiding deities — <s>Dharma</s> and others — who embody the <s>Vedas</s>,
with <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Jñāna</s>, <s>Mahā-aiśvarya</s>, and <s>Vairāgya</s> as its feet. (Lbh 1.5.258)
In the same text (6.256.23-54):
In the center there abide Fire, Sun, and Moon,

children.text: kūrmaś ca nāgarājaś ca vainateyas trayīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kūrma</s> (Tortoise), the king of serpents (<s>Nāgarāja</s>), <s>Vainateya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), and the lord of the <s>Vedas</s>;
the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic meters) and all <s>mantras</s> have assumed the form of the seat —

children.text: sarvākṣaramayaṃ divyaṃ yoga-pīṭham iti smṛtam // Lbh_1,5.259 //
children.translated_text: this divine seat, consisting of all syllables, is known as the <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s>. (Lbh 1.5.259)
In its center is an eight-petaled lotus, of radiance equal to the rising sun;
in the center, upon its pericarp, upon <s>Sāvitrī</s>, O beautiful-visioned one,

children.text: īśvaryā saha deveśas tatrāsīnaḥ paraḥ pumān // Lbh_1,5.260 //
children.translated_text: the Lord of lords sits together with <s>Īśvarī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — the Supreme Person. (Lbh 1.5.260)
Dark as a blue lotus petal, of brilliance equal to ten million suns,

children.text: yuvā kumāraḥ snigdhāṅgaḥ komalāvayavair yutaḥ // Lbh_1,5.261 //
children.translated_text: youthful, a prince, with smooth limbs and delicate features, (Lbh 1.5.261)
with lotus feet and hands soft as blooming red lotuses,
with eyes like fully-opened white lotuses, marked with beautiful brow-creepers, (Lbh 1.5.262)
of fine nose, rich beautiful cheeks, and a lotus-like face of great beauty,
with pearl-like teeth, and coral-red lips bearing a gentle smile, (Lbh 1.5.263)
with a lotus face resembling the full moon, graced by a gentle smile,
resplendent with two earrings of the hue of the young sun. (Lbh 1.5.264)
adorned with deeply glistening dark curly locks of hair,
resplendent with <s>Mandāra</s> and <s>Pārijāta</s> flowers, His hair braided into a coiffure. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.265 //
Adorned with the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem resembling the rising morning sun with its thousand rays,
resplendent with a conch-like neck adorned with necklaces and golden garlands. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.266 //
Resplendent with shoulders high and full, resembling those of a lion,
adorned with four arms that are full, rounded, and long. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.267 //
Adorned with finger-rings, bracelets, and armlets,
with excellent ornaments such as the <s>Kaustubha</s>, resembling tens of millions of rising suns,
His great chest shining, decorated with a forest garland (<s>vanamālā</s>). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.268 //
Adorned with a navel-lotus that is the birthplace of the Creator (<s>Vidhātṛ</s>),
wearing smooth yellow garments resembling the radiance of the young sun. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.269 //
Resplendent with a pair of ankle-ornaments variegated with many gems,
surrounded by rows of toenails resembling the moon with its light. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.270 //
<s>Acyuta</s> (the Infallible One), possessing the charm of ten million <s>Kandarpa</s>-s (Cupids), a treasury of beauty,
His body anointed with divine sandalwood paste, adorned with a forest garland,
resplendent with two upraised arms holding conch and discus,
and likewise with the other two hands showing the gestures of boon-granting (<s>varada</s>) and fearlessness (<s>abhaya</s>). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.271 //
Seated on His left side is the Goddess <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, the great sovereign lady,
golden-complexioned, radiant, wearing garlands of gold and silver. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.272 //
Endowed with all auspicious marks, Her body in the bloom of youth,
wearing jeweled earrings, with dark curling hair. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.273 //
Her body anointed with divine sandalwood paste, adorned with divine flowers,
Her beautiful tresses decorated with <s>Mandāra</s>, <s>Ketakī</s>, and <s>Jātī</s> flowers. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.274 //
With beautiful eyebrows, beautiful nose, beautiful hips, and full, high breasts,
Her lotus-face graced with a sweet smile resembling the full moon. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.275 //
Resplendent with a pair of earrings the color of the young sun,
Her complexion like molten gold, Her ornaments of molten gold. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.276 //
Endowed with four hands, adorned with golden lotuses,
with a garland of golden lotuses variegated with many gems,
adorned with necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and finger-rings. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.277 //
Resplendent with a pair of upraised lotuses held in two hands,
Her hands adorned with a <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron) fruit made of gold. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.278 //
Thus with <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, who is eternally inseparable from Him, the Great Lord

children.text: modate parama-vyomni śāśvate sarvadā prabhuḥ // Lbh_1,5.279 //
children.translated_text: rejoices always in the eternal supreme sky (<s>parama-vyoman</s>), the almighty Lord. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.279 //
On either side are seated <s>Bhū</s> (Earth) and <s>Līlā</s>, with auspicious faces,

children.text: aṣṭa-dikṣu dalāgreṣu vimalādyāś ca śaktayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.280 //
children.translated_text: and at the tips of the eight directional petals are <s>Vimalā</s> and the other <s>śakti</s>-s (powers). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.280 //

children.text: vimalotkarṣiṇī jñānā kriyā yogā tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Jñānā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Yogā</s>, and likewise
<s>Prahvī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and <s>Īśānā</s> — these are the consorts of the Supreme Self.
Holding divine fly-whisks radiant as the moon,
endowed with all auspicious marks, they delight in their husband <s>Acyuta</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.281 //
Groups of divine <s>Apsaras</s>-es, five hundred women in number,
dwelling in the inner chambers, adorned with all ornaments,
all holding lotuses in their hands, radiant as tens of millions of fires,
endowed with all auspicious marks, their faces like the cool-rayed moon —

children.text: tābhiḥ parivṛto rājā śuśubhe paramaḥ pumān // Lbh_1,5.282 //
children.translated_text: surrounded by them, the Supreme Person, the King, shone forth resplendently. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.282 //
Attended by <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s> (the lord of birds), <s>Senānī</s> (Viṣvaksena), and other lords of the gods,

children.text: anyaiḥ parijanair nityair muktaiś ca parisaṃvṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: and by other eternally-liberated attendants and liberated souls,

children.text: modate ramayā sārdhaṃ bhogaiśvaryaiḥ paraḥ pumān // Lbh_1,5.283 //
children.translated_text: the Supreme Person rejoices with <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī), in enjoyment and sovereignty. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.283 //
Here are the summarizing verses (<s>kārikā</s>-s):

children.text: arthataḥ śabdataś cātra yat punaḥ punar ucyate |
children.translated_text: That which is stated here again and again, in meaning and in words,
is because it is a matter beyond ordinary comprehension — for the conviction of those who argue from reason. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.284 //
The <s>Veda</s>-s are embodied forms of the breath of the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>;

children.text: tatas tad-aṅgato jātāḥ svedāḥ parama-pāvanāḥ // Lbh_1,5.285 //
children.translated_text: from that, born from His limbs, are the supremely purifying perspiration-drops (the subsidiary texts). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.285 //

children.text: tripād-vibhūter dhāmatvāt tripādbhūtaṃ tu tat padam |
children.translated_text: Because it is the abode of the three-quarter splendor (<s>tripād-vibhūti</s>), that realm is called 'three-quartered';

children.text: vibhūtir māyikī sarvā proktā pādātmikā yataḥ // Lbh_1,5.286 //
children.translated_text: all <s>māyic</s> (illusory) splendor is declared to constitute one quarter. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.286 //

children.text: amṛtaṃ suṣṭhu madhuraṃ śāśvatas tu muhur navam |
children.translated_text: It is immortal, exceedingly sweet, eternal yet ever new;

children.text: śuddha-sattvas tu tat proktaṃ sattvam aprākṛtaṃ tu tat |
children.translated_text: it is called pure <s>sattva</s> (<s>śuddha-sattva</s>), a <s>sattva</s> that is transcendental (<s>aprākṛta</s>);
by terms such as 'eternal' and 'imperishable,' the absence of the six transformations is indicated. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.287 //
Moreover, verses concerning matters not yet raised:
The first enclosure is understood in the eight directions beginning with the east,
consisting of the <s>vyūha</s>-s (emanated forms) — <s>Vāsudeva</s> and the others — accompanied by <s>Lakṣmī</s> and others. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.288 //

children.text: pūryo lakṣmyāḥ sarasvatyā rateḥ kānter anukramāt |
children.translated_text: The cities of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Rati</s>, and <s>Kānti</s>, in order,
are proclaimed in the intermediate directions of the supreme sky, beginning with the southeast. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.289 //
By the twenty-four forms beginning with <s>Keśava</s>, the second enclosure is formed;

children.text: aṣṭāsu kila kāṣṭhāsu teṣāṃ jñeyaṃ trayaṃ trayam // Lbh_1,5.290 //
children.translated_text: in the eight directions, groups of three for each should be known. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.290 //
By the ten <s>avatāra</s>-s beginning with <s>Matsya</s> and <s>Kūrma</s>, in the ten directions, the third enclosure is formed. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.291 //
By <s>Satya</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, <s>Gajānana</s> (Gaṇeśa),

children.text: śaṅkha-padma-nidhibhyāṃ ca turyam aṣṭāsu dikṣv idam // Lbh_1,5.292 //
children.translated_text: and the two treasures <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s> — the fourth enclosure in the eight directions. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.292 //
By the four <s>Veda</s>-s beginning with the <s>Ṛg Veda</s>, by <s>Sāvitrī</s>, by <s>Garuḍa</s>,

children.text: tathādharma-sakhābhyāṃ ca pañcamaṃ pūrvavan matam // Lbh_1,5.293 //
children.translated_text: and by <s>Adharma</s> and his companion — the fifth, understood as before. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.293 //
By conch, discus, mace, lotus, sword, <s>Śārṅga</s> (bow), plough,

children.text: mūṣaleṇa ca ṣaṣṭhaṃ syād indrādyai saptamaṃ tathā // Lbh_1,5.294 //
children.translated_text: and pestle — the sixth; and by <s>Indra</s> and others, the seventh likewise. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.294 //

children.text: sādhyā marud-gaṇais caiva viśvadevās tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: The <s>Sādhya</s>-s, the <s>Marut</s> hosts, the <s>Viśvedeva</s>-s likewise,

children.text: nityāḥ sarve pare dhāmni ye cānye tridivaukasaḥ |
children.translated_text: and all the eternals in the supreme abode, and whatever other celestial beings —

children.text: te vai prākṛtanāke'smin na nityās tridiveśvarāḥ // Lbh_1,5.295 //
children.translated_text: they are eternal in the supreme realm; in this material heaven, the lords of heaven are not eternal. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.295 //
Of the seventy forms beginning with <s>Vāsudeva</s>, in groups of four,

children.text: lokās tu tāvat-saṅkhyākāḥ pare dhāmni cakāsati // Lbh_1,5.296 //
children.translated_text: the corresponding number of worlds shine in the supreme abode. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.296 //
Among the three <s>Puruṣa</s> incarnations, and from <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Padmabhava</s> (Brahmā) as well,
by the determination made by <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others, <s>Viṣṇu</s> alone is the greatest.

children.text: kiṃ punaḥ puruṣas tatra vāsudevo'tra kintarām |
children.translated_text: How much more so the <s>Puruṣa</s> there; how much more so <s>Vāsudeva</s> here;
and how much more so this one — the Lord of <s>Mahā-Vaikuṇṭha</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.297 //

children.text: sadāśivākhyo yaḥ śambhuḥ sa caiśānyāvṛtir matā // Lbh_1,5.298 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śambhu</s> known as <s>Sadāśiva</s> is understood as the guardian of the <s>Īśāna</s> (northeast) enclosure. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.298 //

children.text: ato bruve'nayoḥ prāyo vailakṣaṇyaṃ dvayor na hi |
children.translated_text: Therefore I say: between these two there is generally no great difference,
for they are like a lamp and the lamp lit from it — the <s>vilāsa</s> (playful expansion) and the source of the expansion are alike. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.299 //

children.text: maivaṃ vādīr mahāvādin adhunā tvam apeśalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Do not speak thus, O great debater! You are now being unskilful;
you have not tasted the relish of understanding the profound divine opulence. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.300 //
The essence of all <s>Vedānta</s>, the fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of the <s>Veda</s>-s —

children.text: śrī-bhāgavatam evātra pramāṇaṃ sarvato varam // Lbh_1,5.301 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> alone is the supreme authority in all matters. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.301 //
As stated in <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, Third Canto (3.2.21):
He Himself, without equal or superior, the Lord of three realms,
who by His own sovereign splendor has attained all desires,
by the long-lived world-guardians who bring tribute,
whose footstool is praised by the tips of their millions of crowns. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.302 //
Thus.
Here are the summarizing verses:
In the analysis 'there is no equal or superior to any other' —
since <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s superiority over all His own forms is demonstrated,

children.text: ādhikyaṃ parama-vyoma-nāthād apy asya darśitam // Lbh_1,5.303 //
children.translated_text: His supremacy even over the Lord of <s>Parama-vyoman</s> (the supreme sky) is shown. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.303 //
And by the word '<s>svayam</s>' (Himself), His independence from all others is expressed. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.304 //
That <s>Rāma</s> too was said to be 'the abode freed from superior and equal' —
there, due to the absence of the word '<s>svayam</s>,' that applies to Him through oneness with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: nara-līlādi-sādharmyāt preṣṭhaṃ rūpaṃ tad asya yat // Lbh_1,5.305 //
children.translated_text: due to similarity in human pastimes and so forth, that is His most beloved form. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.305 //
As stated in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'<s>Matsya</s>, <s>Kūrma</s>, and the other <s>avatāra</s>-s are My innermost essential forms;
and this one here, the glorious son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, is so with His entire being.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.306 //
Thus.

children.text: svayaṃ tv asāmyātiśayaḥ kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam |
children.translated_text: 'He Himself, without equal or superior' and '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed the Supreme Lord Himself' —
in describing His special supreme sovereignty,

children.text: padasya svayam ity asya dviruktir bodhayaty asau |
children.translated_text: the twofold use of the word '<s>svayam</s>' (Himself) indicates
that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s superiority over His own other forms is absolute in every way. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.307 //
'Lord of three' (<s>tryadhīśa</s>) — refers to the three abodes named <s>Goloka</s>, <s>Mathurā</s>, and <s>Dvārakā</s>;
He who is the sovereign of those three abodes is the supreme Lord.
Or, He is the Lord above the three — the Lord of <s>Prakṛti</s>, the <s>Virāṭ</s>, and the Indweller (<s>Antaryāmin</s>), the one reclining on the Ocean of Milk —

children.text: trayāṇām uparīśo'yaṃ try-adhīśa iti vā smṛtaḥ // Lbh_1,5.308 //
children.translated_text: being the Lord above these three, He is remembered as '<s>tryadhīśa</s>' (Lord of three). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.308 //
'By His own sovereign splendor' — by that too He has attained all desires;
by His own Self, by His own innate supreme power (<s>śakti</s>),

children.text: rājatīti svarāṭ tasya bhāvaḥ svārājyam ucyate ||
children.translated_text: He rules — thus He is '<s>svarāṭ</s>' (self-sovereign); the state of that is called '<s>svārājya</s>' (sovereignty).

children.text: tad eva lakṣmīḥ sarvātiśāyinī sampad etayā |
children.translated_text: That itself is '<s>lakṣmī</s>' — the all-surpassing wealth; by this

children.text: āptāḥ samastāḥ kāmā yaṃ kāmāḥ preṣṭhārtha-siddhayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.309 //
children.translated_text: all desires are fulfilled for Him — desires meaning the attainment of the most cherished objects. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.309 //
'<s>Cira</s>' means long-lived; '<s>lokapā</s>-s' are the world-guardians such as <s>Padmaja</s> (Brahmā) and others.
By the tips of their crowns — by hundreds of billions of their diadems —

children.text: īḍite saṃstute pāda-pīṭhe yasyeti vigrahaḥ // Lbh_1,5.310 //
children.translated_text: the footstool of Him whose feet are praised is the meaning of the compound. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.310 //
By the contact of crowns set with diamonds and other gems against the footstool,

children.text: janitena svanaughena bāḍham utprekṣitā stutiḥ // Lbh_1,5.311 //
children.translated_text: the sound produced is imaginatively conceived as praise. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.311 //
By those world-guardians such as <s>Brahmā</s> and others, through their steadfast performance of their respective duties,

children.text: ājñāpālanam evāsya baler haraṇam ucyate // Lbh_1,5.312 //
children.translated_text: the obedience to His command itself is called 'bringing of tribute' (<s>bali-haraṇa</s>). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.312 //

children.text: athātra prakriyā khyātā paruāṇy eṣā vilikhyate // Lbh_1,5.313 //
children.translated_text: Now the well-known procedure at this point is written out in detail. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.313 //
Infinite <s>brahmāṇḍa</s>-s (cosmic eggs), mostly of various kinds,
shine forth in clusters within the power of the Lord. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.314 //
Some cosmic eggs measure a hundred <s>koṭi</s> (billion) <s>yojana</s>-s,
and they shine due to the variety of <s>Hari</s>'s power. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.315 //

children.text: kānicic ca nikharveṇa teṣāṃ padmāyutena ca |
children.translated_text: Some extend over a <s>nikharva</s> (hundred billion), some over ten thousand <s>padma</s>-s,
and some are expanded over a hundred <s>parārdha</s>-s of those. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.316 //

children.text: madhye teṣām ajāṇḍeṣu keṣucid viṃśatiḥ kṛtā |
children.translated_text: Within those cosmic eggs, in some there are twenty realms (<s>bhuvana</s>-s),

children.text: bhuvanānāṃ ca pañcāśat kutracit sapatatis tathā |
children.translated_text: in some fifty, in others seventy,

children.text: śataṃ sahasram ayutaṃ lakṣaṃ kvacana rājati // Lbh_1,5.317 //
children.translated_text: and in some, a hundred, a thousand, ten thousand, or a hundred thousand shine forth. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.317 //
In those, world-guardians beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, of various forms, shine forth,
attended on all sides by thousands of supreme powers.
In some, <s>Indra</s> and others live for hundreds of great <s>kalpa</s>-s,
and <s>Brahmā</s> and others possess lifespans of half a <s>parārdha</s> of great <s>kalpa</s>-s. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.318 //
Those various <s>Brahmā</s>-s, <s>Indra</s>-s, and others are called the 'long-lived world-guardians';
this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s footstool is praised by the tips of their millions of crowns. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.319 //
Once, in <s>Dvārakā</s> city, in the <s>Sudharmā</s> assembly hall, when the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>)
was presiding, the gatekeeper approached and announced:
'Desiring to see the lotus feet of the Lord, <s>Brahmā</s> stands at the gate.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.320 //

children.text: āgataḥ katamo brahmā dvārīti paripṛccha tam |
children.translated_text: 'Which <s>Brahmā</s> has come?' — the gatekeeper was asked thus by the Lord.

children.text: ity acyuta-giraṃ śṛṇvan etya dvārādhipaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing these words of <s>Acyuta</s>, the chief of the gatekeepers went forth again,

children.text: pṛṣṭvā brahmānam āgatya kṛṣṇāgre ca tam abravīt |
children.translated_text: asked <s>Brahmā</s>, returned, and said before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>:
'The four-faced one, father of <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, has come.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.321 //

children.text: ānayeti harer vācā tena brahmā praveśitaḥ |
praṇaman daṇḍavat pṛṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇena kim ihāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: Prostrating like a staff, he was asked by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, 'Why have you come

children.text: tvam iti prāha taṃ brahmā devāgamana-kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: here?' <s>Brahmā</s> spoke to Him the reason for the Lord's visit:

children.text: vakṣye paścād yadātthādya brahmā karama ity adaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I shall tell later; but first, as You just now asked "which <s>Brahmā</s>?" —

children.text: jñātum icchāmi tan nātha brahmā nānyo'sti mad yataḥ // Lbh_1,5.322 //
children.translated_text: I wish to know the reason for that, O Lord, since there is no other <s>Brahmā</s> besides me.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.322 //
'Bring him in' — at <s>Hari</s>'s word, <s>Brahmā</s> was ushered in by him.

children.text:
atha smitvā mukundena dvāravatyāṃ drutaṃ tadā |
smṛtvā brahmāṇḍa-koṭibhyo loka-pālāḥ samāgatāḥ |

children.translated_text: Eight-faced, sixty-four-faced, hundred-faced,
thousand-faced, hundred-thousand-faced, ten-million-faced <s>Viriñcas</s> (Brahmās),
and <s>Rudras</s> with twenty faces, as well as fifty-faced ones,
hundred-faced, thousand-faced, bearing a hundred thousand arms and heads,
Then, smiling, <s>Mukunda</s> instantly summoned from tens of millions of <s>brahmāṇḍa</s>-s into <s>Dvāravatī</s> the world-guardians, who arrived.
and <s>Purandaras</s> (Indras) with a hundred thousand and ten million eyes, and others,
and other <s>Lokapālas</s> (world-guardians) adorned with various forms and ornaments,
having arrived before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, bowed down at his footstool.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā vismayāt tasmin unmamāda caturmukhaḥ // Lbh_1,5.323 //
children.translated_text: Seeing them, the four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>) became bewildered with astonishment. [Lbh 1.5.323]
Moreover —
It is stated in the <s>Viṣṇudharmottara</s> that all the spheres of <s>brahmāṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs)

children.text: deśato jīvataś cāpi tulya-rūpa bhavanty amī // Lbh_1,5.324 //
children.translated_text: are uniform in region and in living beings. [Lbh 1.5.324]
As follows —
All the <s>aṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs) are of one form, O lord of men,

children.text: tulya-deśa-vibhāgāś ca tulyajantava eva ca // Lbh_1,5.325 //
children.translated_text: having equal divisions of regions and equal living beings as well. [Lbh 1.5.325]
Thus.
When a contradiction arises here, a reconciliation is provided. [Lbh 1.5.326]
Since in the <s>Śrī Kūrma Purāṇa</s> —

children.text: virodho vākyayor yatra nāprāmāṇyaṃ tad iṣyate |
children.translated_text: Where there is a contradiction between two statements, invalidity is not accepted;

children.text: yathāviruddhatā ca syāt tathārthaḥ kalpyate tayoḥ // Lbh_1,5.327 //
children.translated_text: rather, the meaning of both is to be construed in such a way that there is no contradiction. [Lbh 1.5.327]
Thus.

children.text: yugapat sakalāṇḍāni jātu saṃharate hariḥ // Lbh_1,5.328 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> at times withdraws all the <s>aṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs) simultaneously. [Lbh 1.5.328]
As stated in the <s>Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara</s> (1.77.9) —

children.text: anantāni tavoktāni yāny aṇḍāni mayā purā |
children.translated_text: The infinite <s>aṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs) that were previously described by me to you,
having withdrawn all of them simultaneously, the Lord of the universe

children.text: prakṛtau tiṣṭhati tadā sā rātris tasya kīrtitā // Lbh_1,5.329 //
children.translated_text: then rests in <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature) — that is declared to be His night. [Lbh 1.5.329]
Thus.

children.text: ataḥ saṃhṛtya sarvāṇi punar aṇḍāny asau sṛjan |
children.translated_text: Therefore, having withdrawn all the <s>aṇḍas</s>, when He creates them again,

children.text: viṣamāṇi sṛjej jātu kadācic ca samāny api // Lbh_1,5.330 //
children.translated_text: He may sometimes create them unequal, and sometimes equal as well. [Lbh 1.5.330]

children.text: ity aupodghātikaṃ procya prakṛtaṃ parilikhyate // Lbh_1,5.331 //
children.translated_text: Having stated this introductory matter, the main topic is now set forth. [Lbh 1.5.331]
That which was assumed for the sake of His human pastimes (<s>martya-līlā</s>), displaying the power of His own
<s>yoga-māyā</s> (divine creative potency),
which is astonishing even to Himself, the supreme abode of the wealth of beauty,
whose limbs are the ornament of ornaments. [Lbh 1.5.332]
Moreover, in the same [<s>Bhāgavata</s>] (3.2.12) —
Thus.
Here are the explanatory verses (<s>kārikās</s>) —

children.text: yad bimbaṃ martya-līlānāṃ bhaved aupāyikaṃ param |
children.translated_text: That which is the archetype (<s>bimba</s>) — supremely suitable for human pastimes (<s>martya-līlā</s>) —
the <s>bimba</s> (original form) established in the preceding verse, which is indicated by the word 'yat'. [Lbh 1.5.333]
Due to the presence of wondrous sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>), valor, and sovereignty (<s>aiśvarya</s>),
His human pastimes (<s>martya-līlā</s>) are more captivating than His divine and other pastimes. [Lbh 1.5.334]
By the word '<s>bimba</s>' (archetype) it is implied that He is in every way
the root of all His own respective forms, which are endowed with hosts of excellent qualities. [Lbh 1.5.335]
Therefore, that very form, being the substratum of all qualities and forms without remainder,
is declared to be supremely suitable for the variegated human pastimes. [Lbh 1.5.336]
<s>Sva-yoga-māyā</s> is the <s>cit-śakti</s> (spiritual potency); its 'power' (<s>bala</s>) is its capacity.
By 'displaying' it, He directly manifests and reveals it.
'Behold the wondrous glory of My <s>cit-śakti</s> (spiritual potency)!
Even the fragrance of which cannot be found in the most divine of divine worlds —
such a world-enchanting form has been manifested by her' —

children.text: sva-yoga-māyety ādyasya bhāvo'yam iti gamyate // Lbh_1,5.337 //
children.translated_text: this is understood to be the purport of the phrase beginning with '<s>sva-yoga-māyā</s>'. [Lbh 1.5.337]
Even for Himself — that is, for the Lord of <s>Parama-vyoma</s> (the supreme sky) and other forms who behold the Self —
it is supremely astonishing, producing ever-fresh rapturous wonder. [Lbh 1.5.338]
<s>Saubhagardhi</s> means the ultimate limit of wondrous beauty;
its 'supreme abode' (<s>paraṃ padam</s>) is the excellent seat of eternally surpassing splendor. [Lbh 1.5.339]
Now, the ornaments such as the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, the king of fish (<s>makara</s>-shaped earrings), and <s>kuṇḍalas</s> (earrings),

children.text: tasyāpi bhūṣaṇāny aṅgāny asyeti sati vigrahe |
children.translated_text: the limbs of His body are ornaments even for those ornaments — thus, with regard to His divine form,
the incomparable excellence of that sacred form (<s>śrī-vigraha</s>) is proclaimed. [Lbh 1.5.340]
Because both are of the dense nature of <s>sat-cit-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss), and there is no distinction between them,
the difference between body and embodied soul here is merely figurative (<s>aupacārika</s>). [Lbh 1.5.341]

children.text: deha-dehi-bhidā cātra neśvare vidyate kvacit // Lbh_1,5.342 //
children.translated_text: There is never any distinction between body and embodied soul in the Lord. [Lbh 1.5.342]
And so in the <s>Śrī Kūrma Purāṇa</s> —
Thus.
Moreover, in the <s>Śrī Daśama</s> (Tenth Canto), in the speech of the women of the city (<s>Śrī Mathurā</s>) (10.44.14) —

children.text: gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran yad amuṣya rūpaṃ
children.translated_text: What <s>tapas</s> (austerities) did the <s>gopīs</s> perform, that they may drink with their eyes
the essence of beauty, incomparably excellent, self-accomplished,
ever-new at every moment, difficult to attain,
the exclusive abode of fame, beauty, and sovereignty? [Lbh 1.5.343]
Thus.
As stated by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> to <s>Śrī Baladeva</s> (10.15.8) —
How blessed is this earth with its grasses and herbs touched by Your
feet, the trees and creepers caressed by Your fingernails,
the rivers, mountains, birds and animals graced by Your compassionate glances,

children.text: gopyo'ntareṇa bhujayor api yat-spṛhā śrīḥ // Lbh_1,5.344 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>gopīs</s> embraced between Your arms — for which even <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) yearns. [Lbh 1.5.344]
Thus.
Here are the explanatory verses (<s>kārikās</s>) —
With a heart overflowing with the sweetness of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> and its residents,
when <s>Hari</s> began a eulogy that culminated in His own supreme excellence,

children.text: tam ālocya tato rāmam apadiśya vyadhāyi saḥ // Lbh_1,5.345 //
children.translated_text: noticing that, He then attributed it to <s>Rāma</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) instead. [Lbh 1.5.345]
Therefore, the purport here is not the glorification of <s>Rāma</s>'s excellence;

children.text: sakhya-bhāvāt tadā rāme narmaṇaivedam īritam // Lbh_1,5.346 //
children.translated_text: rather, out of the mood of friendship (<s>sakhya-bhāva</s>), this was spoken to <s>Rāma</s> in jest. [Lbh 1.5.346]

children.text: bhujāntaraṃ tu vakṣas te tena dhanyā vrajāñganāḥ |
children.translated_text: The 'space between the arms' means Your chest — therefore blessed are the women of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: yat-spṛhā vakṣase yasmai śrīr apy ācarati spṛhām // Lbh_1,5.347 //
children.translated_text: for even <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) cherishes the desire for that chest for which she yearns. [Lbh 1.5.347]

children.text: yat-spṛhaiva paraṃ tasyā na tu tat-prāpti-yogyatā // Lbh_1,5.348 //
children.translated_text: She has only the longing for it, but not the eligibility to attain it. [Lbh 1.5.348]
Even though <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) always resides on the chest of the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,
due to her longing for the chest of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, this reveals the superior excellence of His form. [Lbh 1.5.349]

children.text: paurāṇikam upākhyānam atra saṅkṣipya likhyate // Lbh_1,5.350 //
children.translated_text: A <s>Paurāṇika</s> (Purāṇic) narrative is here summarized and recorded. [Lbh 1.5.350]

children.text: śrīḥ prekṣya kṛṣṇa-saundaryaṃ tatra lubdhā tatas tapaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), beholding the beauty of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, became covetous; thereupon she performed <s>tapas</s> (austerities).

children.text: kurvatīṃ prāha tāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kiṃ te tapasi kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> asked her who was performing austerities, 'What is the reason for your <s>tapas</s>?'
She said, 'I wish to sport with You in the cowherd settlement in the form of a <s>gopī</s>.'

children.text: tad durlabham iti proktā lakṣmīs taṃ punar abravīt ||
children.translated_text: Told that this was difficult to attain, <s>Lakṣmī</s> again addressed Him:

children.text: svarṇa-rekheva te nātha vastum icchāmi vakṣasi |
children.translated_text: 'Like a golden line, O Lord, I wish to dwell upon Your chest.'

children.text: evam astv iti sā tasya tad-rūpā vakṣasi sthitā // Lbh_1,5.351 //
children.translated_text: 'So be it' — and thus she, assuming that form, remained on His chest. [Lbh 1.5.351]
As stated in the <s>Śrī Daśama</s> (Tenth Canto) by the wives of the serpent (<s>Nāga</s>) (10.16.36) —
Desiring whom, <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), the goddess, performed <s>tapas</s> (austerities),
abandoning desires and observing vows for a long time. [Lbh 1.5.352]
Thus.
The glory of even His name is declared to be supreme above all. [Lbh 1.5.353]
As in the <s>Śrī Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> —

children.text: sahasra-nāmnāṃ puṇyānāṃ trir āvṛtya tu yat phalam |
children.translated_text: The fruit obtained by thrice repeating a thousand holy names,

children.text: ekāvṛttyā tu kṛṣṇasya nāmaikaṃ tat prayacchati // Lbh_1,5.354 //
children.translated_text: is bestowed by a single utterance of the one name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. [Lbh 1.5.354]
Sweeter than the sweetest, this is the most auspicious of all auspicious things,
the true fruit of all the creepers of the <s>Vedas</s> (<s>Nigamas</s>), of the nature of pure consciousness (<s>cit-svarūpa</s>);

children.text: sakṛd api parigītaṃ śraddhayā helayā vā
children.translated_text: whether sung even once with faith or even carelessly,
O best of the <s>Bhṛgus</s>, the name of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> delivers any human being.
And in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s> —
Thus. [Lbh 1.5.355]

children.text: ataḥ svayaṃ-padādibhyo bhagavān kṛṣṇa eva hi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, from the word '<s>svayam</s>' (Himself) and other terms, <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone
is clearly established as <s>svayaṃ-rūpa</s> (the original personal form) in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> and other scriptures. [Lbh 1.5.356]
As stated in the <s>Śrī Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.1, 5.39) —
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is the Supreme Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>), whose form is <s>sat-cit-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss),
who is without beginning yet the origin of all, <s>Govinda</s>, the cause of all causes. [Lbh 1.5.357]
He manifested various <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations) in the worlds; but

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ samabhavat paramaḥ pumān yo
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself appeared as the Supreme Person —

children.text: govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi // Lbh_1,5.358 //
children.translated_text: I worship that primeval Lord, <s>Govinda</s>, that original person (<s>ādi-puruṣa</s>). [Lbh 1.5.358]
Presiding through His portions (<s>kalās</s>) in the forms of <s>Rāma</s> and others,
Thus.
Therefore, even the Lord of <s>Parama-Vaikuṇṭha</s> (the supreme <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>) is His <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime expansion). [Lbh 1.5.359]

children.text: ato militvā śrutibhiḥ sva-sāro yaḥ stavaḥ kṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the hymn composed by the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedic scriptures) assembled together, whose purport establishes this,

children.text: tat tātparya-kṛtī kṛṣṇam eva devarṣir ānamat // Lbh_1,5.360 //
children.translated_text: the divine sage (<s>Devarṣi</s> <s>Nārada</s>) bowed down to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone. [Lbh 1.5.360]

children.text: namas tasmai bhagavate kṛṣṇāya ityādi // Lbh_1,5.361 //
children.translated_text: 'Obeisance to that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — and so forth. [Lbh 1.5.361]
(<s>Bhāgavata</s> 10.87.46)
Now, if this scion of the <s>Yadu</s> dynasty appeared at the end of <s>Dvāpara</s> (age),

children.text: sa vaikuṇṭheśvaro'hādis tad-vilāsaḥ kathaṃ bhavet // Lbh_1,5.362 //
children.translated_text: and if He is the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> without beginning, how can He be His own <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime expansion)? [Lbh 1.5.362]
Not so — for this one who is without beginning, even His birth-pastime is beginningless;

children.text: svacchandato mukundena prākaṭyaṃ nīyate muhuḥ // Lbh_1,5.363 //
children.translated_text: by His own will, <s>Mukunda</s> brings about His manifestation again and again. [Lbh 1.5.363]
When His own devotees of peaceful disposition were being
oppressed by others of hostile forms,
He, the Lord of higher and lower, compassionate in heart, endowed with the great portions (<s>mahad-aṃśa</s>),

children.text: hy ajo 'pi jāto bhagavān yathāgniḥ // Lbh_1,5.364 //
children.translated_text: though unborn, was born like fire, that <s>Bhagavān</s>. [Lbh 1.5.364]
And so in the <s>Śrī Tṛtīya</s> (Third Canto) (3.2.15) —
Thus.
Here are the explanatory verses (<s>kārikās</s>) —

children.text: sve bhaktāḥ sve ca te śānta-rūpāś cety atra vigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'His own' means devotees; and they are 'of peaceful disposition' — this is the analysis here.

children.text: śāntis tan-niṣṭhatā buddheḥ śāntās tan-niṣṭha-buddhayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.365 //
children.translated_text: 'Peacefulness' (<s>śānti</s>) means steadfast devotion of the intellect; the 'peaceful' are those whose intellects are firmly established in Him. [Lbh 1.5.365]
Among those such as <s>Sūra-suta</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>) and others, and <s>Nanda</s> and other saintly persons,
by others opposed to them — <s>Kaṃsa</s> and other demons and such —

children.text: svarūpaiḥ suṣṭhv arūpair ity arūpatvaṃ virūpatā |
children.translated_text: 'with their own forms (<s>svarūpa</s>) that are exceedingly formless' — 'formlessness' means deformity,

children.text: ghorātivikaṭākārair ity arthaḥ sphuṭam īritaḥ // Lbh_1,5.366 //
children.translated_text: that is, with terrifyingly hideous appearances — this meaning is clearly stated. [Lbh 1.5.366]
'Being oppressed' means being subjected to great calamities on all sides.
Compassionate in mind; the 'higher' are those free from the connection of <s>māyā</s> (illusion);
chief among them is <s>Goloka</s>; the 'lower' are the material cosmic egg-spheres.

children.text: pareṣām avareṣāṃ ca teṣām īśo'dhināyakaḥ // Lbh_1,5.367 //
children.translated_text: He is the Lord, the supreme ruler, of both the higher and the lower. [Lbh 1.5.367]
The 'great' ones are known for being supremely, exceedingly great;

children.text: te paravyoma-nāthaś ca vyūhāś ca vasu-saṅkhyakāḥ // Lbh_1,5.368 //
children.translated_text: they are the Lord of <s>Paravyoma</s> (the spiritual sky) and the eight <s>Vyūhas</s> (emanations). [Lbh 1.5.368]
The <s>Vyūhas</s> beginning with <s>Vāsudeva</s> that belong to the Lord of <s>Paravyoma</s> —
even superior to them are <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>Vyūhas</s>, according to the view of the saintly.
Thus these, together with the <s>Vyūhas</s> of the Lord of <s>Paravyoma</s>,
came here along with His own <s>vilāsa</s> (pastime) expansions and manifested. [Lbh 1.5.369]
His portions (<s>aṃśas</s>) — the well-known <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations) such as the <s>Puruṣa</s> and others,
likewise <s>Śrī Jānakī-nātha</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Kroḍa</s> (<s>Varāha</s>), <s>Vāmana</s>,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> accompanied by <s>Nara</s>, <s>Hayaśīrṣa</s> (<s>Hayagrīva</s>), <s>Ajita</s>, and others — [Lbh 1.5.370]

children.text: ebhir yuktaḥ sadā yogam avāpyayan avasthitaḥ // Lbh_1,5.371 //
children.translated_text: accompanied by all of these, having attained union, He eternally abides. [Lbh 1.5.371]
Therefore, in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, the manifestation of each respective pastime is seen. [Lbh 1.5.372]
The pastime of the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> that was shown here to <s>Viriñca</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) —
the wondrous multitude of billions of material cosmic eggs with their presiding lords in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> —

children.text: saiva jñeyā yataḥ svāṃśa-dvāraivāsau prakāśitā // Lbh_1,5.373 //
children.translated_text: that is to be understood as manifested through His own portions (<s>svāṃśa</s>). [Lbh 1.5.373]
The pastimes of <s>Vāsudeva</s> and others, however, in <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Dvārakā</s>, and other places,

children.text: tat-tad-rūpair vrajāntas tu bālyehābhiś ca darśitāḥ |
children.translated_text: those entering <s>Vraja</s> in their respective forms, were displayed through childhood pastimes as well.

children.text: yathā śrī-dāmni tārkṣyatvaṃ prāpte so'pi caturbhujaḥ |
children.translated_text: For example, when <s>Śrī Dāma</s> (<s>Śrīdāman</s>) attained the form of <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>), He too assumed a four-armed form;

children.text: ādityeṣv atha labdheṣu babhau dvādaśabhir bhujaiḥ // Lbh_1,5.374 //
children.translated_text: and when the twelve <s>Ādityas</s> (sun-gods) were obtained, He shone with twelve arms. [Lbh 1.5.374]
Likewise, the pastimes belonging to <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, including the slaying of demons,
and the forms of <s>Śrī Pradyumna</s> and <s>Aniruddha</s> shine forth in the <s>Mathurā</s> pastimes,

children.text: yāḥ śrī-gopāla-tāpanyāṃ vārāhādiṣu ca śrutaḥ // Lbh_1,5.375 //
children.translated_text: as heard in the <s>Śrī Gopāla-tāpanī</s> (<s>Upaniṣad</s>) and in the <s>Vārāha</s> and other <s>Purāṇas</s>. [Lbh 1.5.375]
Thus the manifestation of the <s>Puruṣa</s> pastimes here in the <s>Mathurā</s> pastimes
is accomplished through the excellent forms of the one who reclines on <s>Ananta</s> (<s>Ananta-śāyī</s>). [Lbh 1.5.376]

children.text: yadā yadā ca sā līlā kṛṣṇena prakaṭīkṛtā |
children.translated_text: And whenever that pastime is manifested by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: bhavvet tat-tad-upākhyānaṃ purāṇeṣv iti viśrutam // Lbh_1,5.377 //
children.translated_text: a corresponding narrative is celebrated in the <s>Purāṇas</s> — this is well known. [Lbh 1.5.377]
The forms of <s>Rāma</s> and others that He manifested in His own sports —
they shine even today in the <s>Mathurā</s> pastimes as presiding forms (<s>ādhiṣṭhāna-rūpa</s>). [Lbh 1.5.378]
A milk ocean was produced from the torrents of milk from multitudes of cows numbering a <s>parārdha</s>,
and in the form of <s>Ajita</s>, He churned it with the cowherd boys acting as gods and demons. [Lbh 1.5.379]
He who is the four-armed <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Puruṣottama</s> in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: ya eva śvetadvīpeśo naro nārāyaṇaś ca yaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is the Lord of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (the White Island), and He who is <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> —
He Himself is the one who sports in the land of Vṛndāvana, the son of Nanda. // Lbh_1,5.380 //
Therefore in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> —
Of this very one, there are innumerable other enchanting <s>avatāras</s> (incarnations);

children.text: mahāgner iha yadvat syur ulkāḥ śata-sahasraśaḥ |
children.translated_text: just as from a great fire there may be hundreds of thousands of sparks,

children.text: tatraiva līnā ekatvaṃ vrajeyus te harau tathā // Lbh_1,5.381 //
children.translated_text: which merge back into that very fire and become one — so too they return to <s>Hari</s>. // Lbh_1,5.381 //
Thus.

children.text: iti siddhā prabhor asya mahad-aṃśais tu yuktatā // Lbh_1,5.382 //
children.translated_text: Thus is established this Lord's connection with the great portions (<s>mahad-aṃśas</s>). // Lbh_1,5.382 //
Therefore, in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and other texts, some sages speak of Him as the companion of <s>Nara</s>,
some as the younger brother of <s>Mahendra</s> (Vāmana), some as the one reclining on the ocean of milk,
some as the thousand-headed one, and some as the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> —
the sages describe <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> thus, each following the particular narrative they are engaged in. // Lbh_1,5.383 //

children.text: upodghātaṃ samāpyātha prakṛtaṃ likhyate punaḥ // Lbh_1,5.384 //
children.translated_text: Having completed the introduction (<s>upodghāta</s>), the main subject is now written again. // Lbh_1,5.384 //
The unborn one (<s>aja</s>), though devoid of birth, was born — He enacted a birth. // Lbh_1,5.385 //

children.text: nanv ekasya kilājatvaṃ janmitvaṃ ca virudhyate |
children.translated_text: Now, the unbornness and the being-born of one and the same entity are contradictory —
anticipating this objection, the Lord of inconceivable sovereign power says: // Lbh_1,5.386 //

children.text: tatra tatra yathā vahnis tejo-rūpeṇa sann api |
children.translated_text: Just as fire, though existing everywhere in the form of heat,

children.text: jāyate maṇi-kāṣṭhāder hetuṃ kañcid avāpya saḥ ||
children.translated_text: appears to be born from a jewel, wood, etc. upon obtaining some cause,
so too <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, His beginningless pastime of birth and so forth, so wonderfully,

children.text: hetunā kenacit kṛṣṇaḥ prāduṣkuryāt kadācana // Lbh_1,5.387 //
children.translated_text: may sometimes manifest through some cause. // Lbh_1,5.387 //
The desire to show compassion to the worlds through the spread of the fame of His own pastimes —

children.text: asya janmādi-līlānāṃ prākaṭye hetur uttamaḥ // Lbh_1,5.388 //
children.translated_text: this is the supreme cause for the manifestation of His pastimes of birth and so forth. // Lbh_1,5.388 //
And also, when His beloved ones are tormented by most terrifying demons,

children.text: priyeṣu karuṇāpy atra hetur ity uttameva hi // Lbh_1,5.389 //
children.translated_text: compassion too is a cause here — and indeed the supreme one. // Lbh_1,5.389 //
The entreaty by <s>Brahmā</s> and other lords of the gods

children.text: abhyarthanaṃ tu yat tasya tad bhaved ānuṣaṅgikam // Lbh_1,5.390 //
children.translated_text: for the removal of the earth's burden — that would be merely incidental. // Lbh_1,5.390 //
If even now His own dear ones, distressed by longing, wish to see Him,

children.text: tāṃ tāṃ līlāṃ tataḥ kṛṣṇo darśayet tān kṛpā-nidhiḥ // Lbh_1,5.391 //
children.translated_text: then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the treasury of mercy, would show them those respective pastimes. // Lbh_1,5.391 //
By certain supreme devotees (<s>bhāgavatottamas</s>) who have been overwhelmed by <s>prema</s> (divine love),

children.text: adyāpi dṛśyate kṛṣṇaḥ krīḍan vṛndāvanāntare // Lbh_1,5.392 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is seen even now, sporting within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. // Lbh_1,5.392 //

children.text: kiṃ cāsya pārṣadādīnām apy uktā nitya-mūrtitā |
children.translated_text: Moreover, even His associates (<s>pārṣadas</s>) and others are said to have eternal forms;
so what is remarkable about the eternal form of Him, the Lord of lords? // Lbh_1,5.393 //
Nevertheless, for the silencing of those dry disputants
who are devoted solely to argumentation, statements from the <s>Purāṇas</s> and other texts are cited. // Lbh_1,5.394 //
Thus, in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, in the prayer of <s>Brahmā</s> (10.14.22) —
In You, who are an infinite embodiment of eternal bliss and consciousness,

children.text: māyāt udyad api yat sad ivāvabhāti // Lbh_1,5.395 //
children.translated_text: even that which arises from <s>māyā</s> (illusion) appears as if real. // Lbh_1,5.395 //
And in the <s>Śrī Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s> —

children.text: anādeyam aheyaṃ ca rūpaṃ bhagavato hareḥ |
children.translated_text: The form of the Lord <s>Hari</s> is neither to be assumed nor to be discarded;
'manifestation' and 'disappearance' are the terms used for His appearance and withdrawal. // Lbh_1,5.396 //
In the <s>Śrī Bṛhad-vaiṣṇava Purāṇa</s> —
The Lord is of eternal incarnation, of eternal form, the master of the universe;
of eternal beauty, eternal fragrance, experiencing eternal sovereignty and bliss. // Lbh_1,5.397 //
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the conversation between <s>Śrī Vyāsa</s> and <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Vyāsa</s> to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> (4.73.12-13):

children.text: tvām ahaṃ draṣṭum icchāmi cakṣurbhyāṃ madhusūdana |
children.translated_text: I wish to see You with my eyes, O <s>Madhusūdana</s> (slayer of <s>Madhu</s>);

children.text: yat tat satyaṃ paraṃ brahma jagad-yoniṃ jagat-patim |
children.translated_text: that which is the true, supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the source of the universe, the lord of the world,

children.text: vadanti veda-śirasaś cakṣuṣaṃ nātha me'stu tat // Lbh_1,5.398 //
children.translated_text: which the crown of the <s>Vedas</s> (the <s>Upaniṣads</s>) proclaim — O Lord, may that be visible to me. // Lbh_1,5.398 //
Behold — I shall show you the essential form (<s>svarūpa</s>) concealed by the <s>Vedas</s>.
Then I saw, O king, a boy of the hue of a dark rain-cloud,
a cowherd surrounded by cowherd girls, laughing with cowherd boys,
seated at the root of a <s>Kadamba</s> tree, wearing yellow garments — <s>Acyuta</s> (the Infallible). // Lbh_1,5.399 //
The words of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> (PadmaP 4.73.17-19) —

children.text: tato mām āha bhagavān vṛndāvana-caraḥ svayam |
children.translated_text: Then the Lord Himself, the one who roams <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, said to me:

children.text: yad idaṃ me tvayā dṛṣṭaṃ rūpaṃ divyaṃ sanātanam |
children.translated_text: 'This form of Mine that you have seen — divine, eternal,
without parts, without action, peaceful, an embodiment of <s>sat-cit-ānanda</s> (being-consciousness-bliss),

children.text: pūrṇaṃ padma-palāśākṣaṃ nātaḥ parataraṃ mama // Lbh_1,5.400 //
children.translated_text: complete, with eyes like lotus petals — there is nothing higher than this of Mine.' // Lbh_1,5.400 //
Further on in the same text (4.73.23-25) —

children.text: idam eva vadany ete vedāḥ kāraṇa-kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: 'This very thing the <s>Vedas</s> declare to be the cause of causes,

children.text: satyaṃ vyāpi parānandaṃ cid-ghanaṃ śāśvataṃ śivam // Lbh_1,5.401 //
children.translated_text: true, all-pervading, of supreme bliss, a mass of consciousness, eternal, and auspicious.' // Lbh_1,5.401 //
In the <s>Śrī Vāsudeva Upaniṣad</s> (3.5) —
'My form is the non-dual <s>Brahman</s>, devoid of middle, beginning, and end,

children.text: sva-prabhaṃ sac-cid-ānandaṃ bhaktyā jānāti cāvyayam // Lbh_1,5.402 //
children.translated_text: self-luminous, of the nature of <s>sat-cit-ānanda</s> — one knows it as imperishable through <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).' // Lbh_1,5.402 //
Thus.

children.text: nanv arūpaḥ kṛṣṇo dṛśyo māyika-rūpataḥ // Lbh_1,5.403 //
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is formless; He is seen through an illusory form. // Lbh_1,5.403 //
Even so, in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s>, the words of the Lord are as follows (MBh 12.326.42-43):

children.text: etat tvayā na vijñeyaṃ rūpavān iti dṛśyate |
children.translated_text: 'This should not be understood by you — that He is seen as having form;

children.text: icchan muhūrtān naśyeyam īśo 'haṃ jagato guruḥ // Lbh_1,5.404 //
children.translated_text: if I wish, I could disappear in an instant — I am the Lord, the teacher of the universe.' // Lbh_1,5.404 //

children.text: māyā hy eṣā mayā sṛṣṭā yan māṃ paśyasi nārada |
children.translated_text: 'This is <s>māyā</s> (illusive power) created by Me, by which you see Me, O <s>Nārada</s>;

children.text: sarvabhūtaguṇair yuktaṃ naivaṃ tvaṃ jñātum arhasi // Lbh_1,5.405 //
children.translated_text: endowed with all the qualities of material beings — you should not understand Me thus.' // Lbh_1,5.405 //
Thus.
And in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> —
'This Lord <s>Hari</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the sovereign, is without name and form;

children.text: akarteti ca yo vedaiḥ smṛtibhiś cābhidhīyate // Lbh_1,5.406 //
children.translated_text: and He is called the non-doer — thus by the <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Smṛtis</s>.' // Lbh_1,5.406 //
Thus.
Here the resolution, as stated in the <s>Śrī Vāsudevādhyātma</s> —
'Because His qualities are not publicly known, He is called 'nameless';
because He is non-material, even though He has form, He is called 'formless.'

children.text: sambandhena pradhānasya harer nāsty eva kartṛtā |
children.translated_text: In relation to <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), <s>Hari</s> has no agency whatsoever;

children.text: akartāram ataḥ prāhuḥ purāṇaṃ taṃ purāvidaḥ // Lbh_1,5.407 //
children.translated_text: therefore the ancient knowers call Him 'the non-doer.'' // Lbh_1,5.407 //
Thus.

children.text: ataś ca mokṣadharmīya-vacanaṃ yogyam eva tat // Lbh_1,5.408 //
children.translated_text: And therefore, the statement from the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> is entirely appropriate. // Lbh_1,5.408 //
That is to say —

children.text: rūpīti hetor dṛśyeta yathaiva prākṛto janaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'He should not be thought to be visible as one having form, just as an ordinary person is;

children.text: tathāsau dṛśyata iti tvayā mā sma vicāryatām // Lbh_1,5.409 //
children.translated_text: do not consider that He is seen in that manner.' // Lbh_1,5.409 //

children.text: ity uktvā svasya rūpitve'py adṛśyatvam udīritam |
children.translated_text: Having said this, even though His form exists, its invisibility has been stated;
thereby the non-material nature of His own essential form has been demonstrated. // Lbh_1,5.410 //

children.text: tad-darśane tv akuṇṭhātmā mamecchaiva ca kāraṇam |
children.translated_text: 'My will alone, unobstructed, is the cause for seeing that form' —

children.text: ity āhecchan muhūrtād ity ardha-padyaṃ svayaṃ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: thus He Himself says with the half-verse 'if I wish, in an instant...' and further,

children.text: naśyeyam ity adṛśyaḥ syāṃ yato naśira-darśane // Lbh_1,5.411 //
children.translated_text: 'I would disappear' means 'I would become invisible,' since 'naś' means 'to become invisible.' // Lbh_1,5.411 //
'Nevertheless, that you see Me as possessing the qualities of material beings —

children.text: eṣā māyā mayā sṛṣṭā naivaṃ tvaṃ jñātum arhasi // Lbh_1,5.412 //
children.translated_text: this is <s>māyā</s> created by Me; you should not understand Me thus.' // Lbh_1,5.412 //
The word '<s>māyā</s>' in some contexts refers to the <s>cit-śakti</s> (consciousness-power). // Lbh_1,5.423 //
In the <s>Caturveda-śikhā</s> —
'Endowed with the eternal power called <s>māyā</s>, which is intrinsic to His essential nature;
therefore they call <s>Viṣṇu</s> 'made of <s>māyā</s>' — the eternal one.' —

children.text: ity eṣā darśitā madhvācāryair bhāṣye nije śrutiḥ // Lbh_1,5.414 //
children.translated_text: this <s>śruti</s> (Vedic text) has been cited by <s>Madhvācārya</s> in his commentary. // Lbh_1,5.414 //
indeed:
Pleased, the ancient Lord, the god of gods, then

children.text: sākṣāt taṃ darśayām āsa so 'dṛśyo 'nyena kena cit // Lbh_1,5.415 //
children.translated_text: showed Himself directly to him — He who was invisible to anyone else. // Lbh_1,5.415 //
There, the quality of self-revelation by His own will alone is found in the <s>Mokṣadharma</s> (MBh 12.323.11, 13, 15-16, 18) [Alternative numbering: 12.338.13-20.]

children.text: bṛhaspatis tataḥ kruddhaḥ sruvam udyamya vegitaḥ
ākāśaṃ ghnan sruvaḥ pātai roṣād aśrūṇy avartayat // Lbh_1,5.416 //
children.translated_text: striking the sky with blows of the ladle, shed tears of anger: // Lbh_1,5.416 //
Then <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, enraged, swiftly raising his sacrificial ladle,

children.text: udyatā yajñabhāgā hi sākṣāt prāptāḥ surair iha |
children.translated_text: 'The sacrificial portions have been duly offered, directly received by the gods here;

children.text: kimartham iha na prāpto darśanaṃ sa harir vibhuḥ // Lbh_1,5.417 //
children.translated_text: why then has <s>Hari</s>, the all-pervading Lord, not come here to be seen?' // Lbh_1,5.417 //

children.text: tataḥ sa taṃ samuddhūtaṃ bhūmipālo mahān vibhuḥ |
children.translated_text: Then that great, powerful king

children.text: prasādayām āsa muniṃ sadasyās te ca sarvaśaḥ // Lbh_1,5.418 //
children.translated_text: pacified the agitated sage, along with all the assembled priests. // Lbh_1,5.418 //

children.text: aroṣaṇo hy asau devo yasya bhāgo 'yam udyataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'That god, for whom this offering has been raised, is free from anger;

children.text: na sa śakyas tvayā draṣṭum asmābhir vā bṛhaspate |
children.translated_text: He cannot be seen by you, nor by us, O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>;

children.text: yasya prasādaṃ kurute sa vai taṃ draṣṭum arhati // Lbh_1,5.419 //
children.translated_text: only the one upon whom He bestows His grace is worthy of seeing Him.' // Lbh_1,5.419 //
There, the passage of <s>Ekata</s>, <s>Dvita</s>, and <s>Trita</s> (MBh 12.338.25-27 or 323.23) —
Then, at the concluding bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>) of the observance, a disembodied voice spoke,
with an affectionate, deep voice, bringing joy to the Lord:
[Alternative reading —
Then, at the concluding bath of the observance, a disembodied voice spoke:
'Well-performed is your austerity, O ascetic sages, with a serene inner self.']

children.text: yūyaṃ jijñāsavo bhaktāḥ kathaṃ drakṣyatha taṃ prabhum // Lbh_1,5.420 //
children.translated_text: 'You are inquiring devotees — how shall you see that Lord?' // Lbh_1,5.420 //
Then, by His power of self-manifestation, which reveals according to His own will,

children.text: so'bhivyakto bhavet netre na netra-viṣayatvataḥ // Lbh_1,5.421 //
children.translated_text: He becomes manifest to the eye — not because He is an object of the senses. // Lbh_1,5.421 //
As stated in the <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇādhyātma</s> —
'The Lord, though eternally unmanifest, is seen by His own power;

children.text: tām ṛte paramātmānaṃ kaḥ paśyetām itaṃ prabhum // Lbh_1,5.422 //
children.translated_text: without that, who could see the <s>Paramātmā</s> (Supreme Self), the almighty Lord?' // Lbh_1,5.422 //
And in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> —
'Because His form is of the nature of <s>sat-cit-ānanda</s> (being-consciousness-bliss), <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed beyond sense perception (<s>adhokṣaja</s>);

children.text: nija-śakteḥ prabhāvena svaṃ bhaktān darśayet prabhuḥ // Lbh_1,5.423 //
children.translated_text: yet by the power of His own <s>śakti</s> (energy), the Lord reveals Himself to His devotees.' // Lbh_1,5.423 //

children.text: ya eva vigraho vyāpī paricchinnaḥ sa eva hi |
children.translated_text: 'That very same form which is all-pervading is also delimited;
of this one alone, at the same time, the dual nature shines forth.' // Lbh_1,5.424 //
As in the glorious Tenth Canto (10.9.13-14) —

children.text: na cāntar na bahir yasya na pūrvaṃ nāpi cāparam |
children.translated_text: 'He who has no interior or exterior, no before or after,

children.text: pūrvāparaṃ bahiś cāntar jagato yo jagac ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: who is the before and after, the exterior and interior of the universe, and who is the universe itself —
regarding Him as her child, unmanifest, bearing a mortal guise, beyond sense perception,

children.text: gopikolūkhale dāmnā babandha prākṛtaṃ yathā // Lbh_1,5.425 //
children.translated_text: the cowherd woman (<s>gopī</s>) bound Him to a mortar with a rope, as if He were an ordinary being.' // Lbh_1,5.425 //
By this pair of verses, regarding the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>,
the dual nature is made evident precisely at the moment of the rope-binding. // Lbh_1,5.426 //
And likewise in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> and others,

children.text: śrūyate kṛṣṇa-līlānāṃ nityatā sphuṭam eva hi // Lbh_1,5.427 //
children.translated_text: the eternality of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s pastimes is clearly heard. // Lbh_1,5.427 //
'Oh, how supremely praiseworthy is the dynasty of <s>Yadu</s>!
Oh, how supremely meritorious is the forest of <s>Madhu</s> (Mathurā)!

children.text: yad eṣa puṃsām ṛṣabhaḥ śriyaḥ patiḥ
children.translated_text: For this foremost of persons, the Lord of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī),
graces it with His birth and His wanderings!' // Lbh_1,5.428 //
As, for example, the words of the residents of <s>Śrī Dvārakā</s> in the First Canto (1.10.26) —
The word 'añcati' is in the present tense;

children.text: dvārakā-vāsinām uktau līlānāṃ vakti nityatām // Lbh_1,5.429 //
children.translated_text: in the utterance of the residents of <s>Dvārakā</s>, it declares the eternality of the pastimes. // Lbh_1,5.429 //
'Victorious is He who dwells among the people, whose birth in <s>Devakī</s> is celebrated,
who, surrounded by the assembly of the best of the <s>Yadus</s>, dispels <s>adharma</s> with His own arms,
the destroyer of the sins of all moving and stationary beings, who, with His gently smiling beautiful face,
increases <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the god of love) for the women of <s>Vraja</s>-city.' // Lbh_1,5.430 //
In the glorious Tenth Canto, in the words of <s>Śrī Śuka</s> (10.90.48) —
In the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Mathurā-khaṇḍa</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Nārada</s> to <s>Śrī Yudhiṣṭhira</s> —

children.text: vatsair vatsatarībhiś ca sākaṃ krīḍati mādhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Mādhava</s> plays together with the calves and young cows,
within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, accompanied by <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma), surrounded by boys.' // Lbh_1,5.431 //

children.text: yad-ānayos tu saṃvādo dvāravatyāṃ haris tadā |
children.translated_text: Although the conversation between these two was in <s>Dvārakā</s>, <s>Hari</s> was at that time (also in Vṛndāvana);

children.text: tathāpi vartamānatvenoktis tan naity avācikā // Lbh_1,5.432 //
children.translated_text: nevertheless, the use of the present tense does not become meaningless. // Lbh_1,5.432 //
In the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, <s>Pātāla-khaṇḍa</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Rudra</s> (Śiva) to <s>Śrī Pārvatī</s> —

children.text: aho madhu-purī dhanyā yatra tiṣṭhati kaṃsahā |
children.translated_text: 'Oh, how blessed is the city of <s>Madhu</s> (Mathurā), where the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> abides!

children.text: tatra devā muniḥ sarve vāsam icchanti sarvadā // Lbh_1,5.433 //
children.translated_text: There all gods and sages always desire to dwell.' // Lbh_1,5.433 //
The companions of His pastimes (<s>līlā-parikara</s>) are the people of <s>Goṣṭha</s> (the cowherd settlement) and the <s>Yādavas</s>,
and also gods such as <s>Brahmā</s>, the enemy of <s>Jambha</s> (Indra), the sons of <s>Kuvera</s>, and others,

children.text: nāradādyāś ca danuja-nāga-yakṣādayaś ca te // Lbh_1,5.434 //
children.translated_text: <s>Nārada</s> and others, as well as demons, <s>Nāgas</s>, <s>Yakṣas</s>, and so forth. // Lbh_1,5.434 //

children.text: prakaṭāprakaṭā ceti līlā seyaṃ dvidhocyate // Lbh_1,5.435 //
children.translated_text: This pastime is said to be twofold: manifest (<s>prakaṭa</s>) and unmanifest (<s>aprakaṭa</s>). // Lbh_1,5.435 //
That is to say —

children.text: sadānantaiḥ prakāśaiḥ svair līlābhiś ca sa dīvyati |
children.translated_text: He always sports with His infinite self-manifestations and pastimes;
through one such manifestation, at some time, within the universe,

children.text: sahaiva sva-parīvārair janmādi kurute hariḥ // Lbh_1,5.436 //
children.translated_text: together with His own retinue, <s>Hari</s> enacts His birth and other pastimes. // Lbh_1,5.436 //
In accordance with the nature of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that power itself is called <s>līlā</s> (pastime);

children.text: teṣāṃ parikarāṇāṃ ca taṃ taṃ bhāvaṃ vibhāvayet // Lbh_1,5.437 //
children.translated_text: one should meditate upon the respective moods (<s>bhāvas</s>) of those associates (<s>parikaras</s>). (Lbh 1.5.437)
That <s>līlā</s> (pastime) which falls within the scope of the material world is known as <s>prakaṭa</s> (manifest);

children.text: anyās tv aprakaṭā bhānti tādṛśyas tad-agocarāḥ // Lbh_1,5.438 //
children.translated_text: the others, however, shine forth as <s>aprakaṭa</s> (unmanifest) — of the same nature, yet beyond its reach. (Lbh 1.5.438)
In the <s>prakaṭa-līlā</s> alone do the comings and goings occur,

children.text: gokule mathurāyāṃ ca dvāravatyāṃ ca śārṅgiṇaḥ // Lbh_1,5.439 //
