children.translated_text: of the wielder of <s>Śārṅga</s> — in <s>Gokula</s>, in <s>Mathurā</s>, and in <s>Dvāravatī</s>. (Lbh 1.5.439)

children.text: yās tatra tatrāprakaṭās tatra tatraiva santi tāḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>aprakaṭa</s> pastimes in each of those places exist in those very places forever;
this is conveyed by the verse beginning 'jayati' and similar passages, repeatedly. (Lbh 1.5.440)
When the descent of the portions of the gods and others was initiated by the command of <s>Padmaja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),
those who were the celestial portions of <s>Vasudeva</s> and others — <s>Kaśyapa</s> and the rest —
were merged with the eternal associates <s>Vasudeva</s> and others situated in other eternal pastimes,

children.text: sāyujyam aṃśibhis tatra jāyante śūra-mukhyataḥ // Lbh_1,5.441 //
children.translated_text: attaining <s>sāyujya</s> (merging) with their sources; thus they take birth, beginning with <s>Śūra</s>. (Lbh 1.5.441)
He whose expansion (<s>vilāsa</s>) is the great Lord of <s>Śrī</s> — that <s>Līlā-Puruṣottama</s> (Supreme Lord of pastimes),
wishing to manifest, first reveals <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>;
with the other <s>Vyūha</s> forms to be manifested dwelling within, the Lord

children.text: hṛdaye prakaṭas tasya bhavaty ānakadundubheḥ // Lbh_1,5.442 //
children.translated_text: becomes manifest in the heart of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>). (Lbh 1.5.442)
at the end of the <s>Dvāpara</s> age, in this twenty-eighth <s>catur-yuga</s>,
that form which is the one reclining on the Milk Ocean, known as <s>Aniruddha</s>,
having merged with the form dwelling in the heart of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>,

children.text: aikyaṃ prāpya tato gacchet prākaṭyaṃ devakī-hṛdi // Lbh_1,5.443 //
children.translated_text: then proceeds to manifest in the heart of <s>Devakī</s>. (Lbh 1.5.443)
For the removal of the earth's burden, at the request of the gods,
Nourished by the nectars of loving bliss (<s>premānanda</s>), which are of the very nature of parental affection (<s>vātsalya</s>),

children.text: lālyamāno haris tatra vadhate candramā iva // Lbh_1,5.444 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> grows there, like the moon. (Lbh 1.5.444)
Then, on the eighth day (<s>aṣṭamī</s>) of the dark fortnight of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, at the great midnight,
disappearing from her heart, in the prison, in the birthing chamber,

children.text: devakī-śayane tatra kṛṣṇaḥ prādurbhavaty asau // Lbh_1,5.445 //
children.translated_text: on the bed of <s>Devakī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> manifests there. (Lbh 1.5.445)
From 'the mother' and other such terms, it is understood

children.text: laukikena prakāreṇa sukhaṃ śiśur ajāyata // Lbh_1,5.446 //
children.translated_text: that the child was born happily in an ordinary manner. (Lbh 1.5.446)
Whether in His four-armed or two-armed form, He never abandons His <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-nature,
for His essential character, qualities, form, and activities remain the same. (Lbh 1.5.447)
Nevertheless, the two-armed form is declared primary in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;

children.text: gūḍhatvād eva ca kvāpi gauṇatvam iva kīrtyate |
children.translated_text: and due to its being hidden, it is sometimes spoken of as if secondary.

children.text: gūḍhaṃ paraṃ brahma manuṣya-liṅgam iti hi prathā // Lbh_1,5.448 //
children.translated_text: 'The Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, concealed in human semblance' — so goes the tradition. (Lbh 1.5.448)
Then <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), entering the home of the queen of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: tatra nyasya sutaṃ tasyāḥ sutām ādāya niḥsaret // Lbh_1,5.449 //
children.translated_text: placed his son there, and taking her daughter, departed. (Lbh 1.5.449)
This very <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, being eternally her son, has shone as hers from beginningless time;

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ prakaṭa-līlāyāṃ tad-dvāreṇāpy abhūt tathā // Lbh_1,5.450 //
children.translated_text: in the <s>prakaṭa-līlā</s> (manifest pastime), He became so through that means as well. (Lbh 1.5.450)
Then, when the great celebration arranged by the king of <s>Vraja</s> became manifest,

children.text: tatra prakaṭayaty eṣa līlā bālyādikā kramāt |
children.translated_text: He manifests there, in sequence, His childhood pastimes and so on —

children.text: karoti yāḥ prakāśeṣu koṭiśo'prakaṭeṣv api // Lbh_1,5.451 //
children.translated_text: those which He performs in millions of <s>aprakaṭa</s> (unmanifest) realms as well. (Lbh 1.5.451)

children.text: preṣṭhānandair vraje tais tair ātmano'pi vimohanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: With the delights of His beloved ones in <s>Vraja</s>, each one enchanting even Himself,
the glorious <s>Līlā-Puruṣottama</s> sports with exuberant pastime-joy. (Lbh 1.5.452)
With unequaled and unsurpassed parental affection from the king and queen of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: sutatvenaiva sa tayor ātmānaṃ vetti sarvadā // Lbh_1,5.453 //
children.translated_text: He always considers Himself their son alone. (Lbh 1.5.453)

children.text: kecid bhāgavatāḥ prāhur evam atra purātanāḥ |
children.translated_text: Some ancient <s>Bhāgavatas</s> (devotees) state the following:
The first <s>Vyūha</s> manifested in the home of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>,

children.text: goṣṭhe tu māyayā sārdhaṃ śrī-līlā-puruṣottamaḥ // Lbh_1,5.454 //
children.translated_text: while in <s>Gokula</s>, the glorious <s>Līlā-Puruṣottama</s> appeared together with <s>Māyā</s>. (Lbh 1.5.454)

children.text: gatvā yaduvaro goṣṭhaṃ tatra sūtī-gṛhaṃ viśan |
children.translated_text: The foremost of the <s>Yadus</s>, having gone to <s>Gokula</s> and entering the birthing chamber,

children.text: kanyām eva paraṃ vīkṣya tām ādāyāvrajat puram |
children.translated_text: seeing only a girl, took her and returned to the city;
<s>Vāsudeva</s> then entered into <s>Śrī Līlā-Puruṣottama</s>. (Lbh 1.5.455)
And this, being extremely confidential, was not stated in the sequence of the narrative;

children.text: kintu kvacit prasaṅgena sūcyate śrī-śukādibhiḥ // Lbh_1,5.456 //
children.translated_text: but is hinted at here and there in passing by <s>Śrī Śuka</s> and others. (Lbh 1.5.456)

children.text: nandas tv ātmaja utpanne jātāhlādo mahā-manāḥ // Lbh_1,5.457 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s>, upon the birth of his son, became overwhelmed with joy, being great-minded.' (Lbh 1.5.457)
As in the glorious Tenth Canto (10.5.1):

children.text: nandaḥ sva-putram ādāya pretyāgatam udāra-dhīḥ // Lbh_1,5.458 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Nanda</s>, of noble intellect, taking his own son who had returned from death.' (Lbh 1.5.458)
As also there (10.6.43):

children.text: nāyaṃ sukhāpo bhagavān dehināṃ gopikā-sutaḥ // Lbh_1,5.459 //
children.translated_text: 'This Lord, the son of the <s>Gopī</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>), is not easily attained by embodied beings.' (Lbh 1.5.459)
And also (10.9.21):
And in the prayer of <s>Śrī Brahmā</s> there (10.14.1):
'To Him whose beauty is a forest garland, a morsel of food, a stick, a horn, and a flute,
whose glory is enhanced by soft feet — to the son of the cowherd chief.' (Lbh 1.5.460)
They also cite the statement of the <s>Śrī Yāmala</s>:

children.text: kṛṣṇo'nyo yadu-sambhūto yaḥ pūrṇaḥ so'sty ataḥ param |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> born among the <s>Yadus</s> is another; He who is the complete one exists beyond that.

children.text: vṛndāvanaṃ parityajya sa kvacit naiva gacchati // Lbh_1,5.461 //
children.translated_text: Never does He leave <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and go anywhere. (Lbh 1.5.461)

children.text: dvibhujaṃ sarvadā so'tra na kadācit caturbhujaḥ |
children.translated_text: He is always two-armed there, never four-armed;

children.text: gopyaikayā yutas tatra parikrīḍati nityadā // Lbh_1,5.462 //
children.translated_text: accompanied by one <s>Gopī</s>, He eternally plays there.' (Lbh 1.5.462)
Thus.
Now, when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> goes to the city of the <s>Yadus</s> in manifest form,
concealing His identity as the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, and revealing His identity as the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>,

children.text: yo vāsudevo dvibhujas tathā bhāti caturbhujaḥ // Lbh_1,5.463 //
children.translated_text: He who is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, two-armed, also appears as four-armed. (Lbh 1.5.463)
His own words, as in the glorious Tenth Canto (10.39.35):

children.text: tās tathā tapyatīr vīkṣya sva-prasthāne yadūttamaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Seeing them thus burning in grief at His departure, the best of the <s>Yadus</s>

children.text: sāntvayāmāsa sapremair āyāsya iti dyautakaiḥ // Lbh_1,5.474 //
children.translated_text: consoled them with loving messages, saying "I shall return."' (Lbh 1.5.474)

children.text: yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān |
children.translated_text: 'Go, dear ones, to <s>Vraja</s>. We shall come to see our kinsmen

children.text: jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṃ sukham // Lbh_1,5.475 //
children.translated_text: who are grieving out of affection, after bringing happiness to our friends.' (Lbh 1.5.475)
Thus.
The very same promise, through the words of <s>Uddhava</s>, the minister of the <s>Yadus</s>, His own most beloved,

children.text: etade eva vacaḥ svīyaṃ punas tanojjvalīkṛtam // Lbh_1,5.476 //
children.translated_text: was again reinforced and made brilliant. (Lbh 1.5.476)
As also there (10.46.35):
'Having slain <s>Kaṃsa</s> in the arena, the adversary of all <s>Sātvatas</s>,

children.text: yad āha vaḥ samāgatya kṛṣṇaḥ satyaṃ karoti tat // Lbh_1,5.477 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> will fulfill what He said to you when He comes.' (Lbh 1.5.477)
'O lotus-eyed one, when You departed from us
to the <s>Kurus</s> or to the <s>Madhus</s>, to visit friends,
each moment seemed like ten million years,

children.text: raviṃ vinākṣṇor iva nas tavācyuta // Lbh_1,5.479 //
children.translated_text: as for eyes without the sun, O <s>Acyuta</s>.' (Lbh 1.5.479)
As in the glorious First Canto (1.11.9):
'O lotus-eyed one, to see friends — <s>Nanda</s> and others —
You departed from us, leaving us, and went to the <s>Madhus</s> —'
meaning to <s>Mathurā</s>; this clearly refers to <s>Vraja</s> within the <s>Mathurā</s> region,

children.text: tadānīṃ suhṛdāṃ tatra madhupuryām abhāvataḥ // Lbh_1,5.480 //
children.translated_text: since at that time there were no friends in the city of <s>Mathurā</s>. (Lbh 1.5.480)
Here are the summarizing verses:
Furthermore:

children.text: rathena mathurāṃ gatvā dantavakraṃ nihatya ca
children.translated_text: 'Having gone to <s>Mathurā</s> by chariot and having slain <s>Dantavakra</s>,

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ pādme purāṇe'sya kṛṣṇasyoktā vrajāgatiḥ // Lbh_1,5.481 //
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s going to <s>Vraja</s> is clearly stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>.' (Lbh 1.5.481)

children.text:
tad-gadyaṃ padyaṃ ca yathā (PadmaP 6.279.24-26) -
kṛṣṇo'pi taṃ hatvā yamunām uttīrya nanda-vrajaṃ gatvā sotkaṇṭhau pitarāv
abhivādyāśvāsya tābhyāṃ sāśru-sekam āliṅgitaḥ sakala-gopa-vṛddhān praṇamy
children.translated_text: and consoling them, was embraced by them with a shower of tears; bowing to all the elder cowherds,
consoling them, He gratified all those present with abundant jewels, diamonds, and ornaments
and other gifts.' (Lbh 1.5.482)

The prose and verse passage is as follows (PadmaP 6.279.24-26): '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having slain him, crossed the <s>Yamunā</s>, went to the settlement of <s>Nanda</s>, and paying respects to His longing parents
'On the beautiful bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), adorned with auspicious trees,
<s>Keśava</s> sported ceaselessly with the cowherd women.
The Lord, wearing the garb of a cowherd, with the pleasure of delightful play,
dwelt there for two months, with abundant <s>prema-rasa</s> (essence of divine love).'
Thus. (Lbh 1.5.483)
Here are the summarizing verses:
The word 'having crossed' (<s>uttīrya</s>) indicates bathing (immersion);

children.text: duṣṭaṃ hatvā vraje yānaṃ snāna-pūrvam ihocitam // Lbh_1,5.484 //
children.translated_text: having slain the wicked one, going to <s>Vraja</s> preceded by bathing is appropriate here. (Lbh 1.5.484)

children.text: ataḥ prakaṭa-līlāyām apy ayogo'lpa eva hi |
children.translated_text: Therefore, even in the <s>prakaṭa-līlā</s>, the separation is indeed very brief;

children.text: iti dhāma-traye kṛṣṇo viharaty eva sarvadā // Lbh_1,5.485 //
children.translated_text: thus <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> always sports in the three abodes. (Lbh 1.5.485)

children.text: vrajāgamana-kāle ca pādmokte'nyac ca vartate // Lbh_1,5.486 //
children.translated_text: And there is more described in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> regarding the time of His return to <s>Vraja</s>. (Lbh 1.5.486)

children.text: atha tatrasthā nanda-gopādayaḥ sarve janāḥ putra-dārādi-sahitāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Then all the people there, <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd chief and others, together with their sons and wives,

children.text: paśu-pakṣi-mṛgādayaś ca vāsudeva-prasādena divya-rūpadharā vimānam ārūḍhāḥ
children.translated_text: and the cattle, birds, deer, and other creatures, by the grace of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, assuming divine forms, mounted aerial vehicles
and attained the supreme <s>Vaikuṇṭha-loka</s>.'
As follows (PadmaP 6.279.27):
Thus. (Lbh 1.5.487)
Here are the summarizing verses:
Those who descended as portions — <s>Droṇa</s> and others — who were the partial beings of the king of <s>Vraja</s> and others,

children.text: kṛṣṇas tān eva vaikuṇṭhe prāhiṇod iti sāmpratam // Lbh_1,5.488 //
children.translated_text: it is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who sent them to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, as now understood. (Lbh 1.5.488)
With persons dearer than even His dearest, the residents of <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: vṛndāraṇye sadaivāsau vihāraṃ kurute hariḥ // Lbh_1,5.489 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> eternally performs His pastimes in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. (Lbh 1.5.489)
As is heard in the <s>Skānda</s> section on the glory of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, regarding <s>Saumitri</s> (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>): (Lbh 1.5.490)
As follows:
'Then, when <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, true to his vow of battle, had attained the state of <s>Śeṣa</s>,

children.text: uvāca madhuraṃ śakraḥ sarvasvaṃ ca sa paśyataḥ // Lbh_1,5.491 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>) spoke to him sweetly, while he (<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>) beheld everything.' (Lbh 1.5.491)

children.text: lakṣmaṇottiṣṭha śīghraṃ tvam ārohasva padaṃ svakam |
children.translated_text: '<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, rise quickly and ascend to your own station.
The work of the gods has been accomplished by you, O hero, O destroyer of enemies.

children.text: vaiṣṇavaṃ paramaṃ sthānaṃ prāpnuhi svaṃ sanātanam |
children.translated_text: Attain the supreme eternal abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, your own;
your very form has come — <s>Śeṣa</s> with shining hoods.' (Lbh 1.5.492)
<s>Indra</s> said:
Then:
'Having spoken thus, <s>Indra</s>, the king of the gods, accompanied by the celestials,
dispatching <s>Śeṣa</s> to <s>Pātāla</s> (the netherworld), capable of bearing the weight of the earth,

children.text: lakṣmaṇaṃ yānam āropya pratasthe divam ādarāt // Lbh_1,5.493 //
children.translated_text: placed <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> on a vehicle and departed for heaven with reverence.' (Lbh 1.5.493)
Thus.
Wishing to perform the <s>aprakaṭa-līlā</s> (unmanifest pastime) there, in <s>Dvāravatī</s>,
He Himself engineers the artifice of the sage's curse and the like. (Lbh 1.5.494)
Those who descended as portions of the gods among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,

children.text: kṣīrābdhi-śāyi-rūpas taiḥ sārdhaṃ svapadam āpnuyāt // Lbh_1,5.495 //
children.translated_text: together with the form reclining on the Milk Ocean, attain their own abode. (Lbh 1.5.495)
Those who are the eternal associates in pastimes — <s>Yaduvara</s> (<s>Uddhava</s>) and others —

children.text: taiḥ sārdhaṃ bhagavān kṛṣṇo dvārvatyām eva dīvyati // Lbh_1,5.496 //
children.translated_text: with them, Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> eternally plays in <s>Dvāravatī</s> itself. (Lbh 1.5.496)

children.text: dhāmāsya dvividhaṃ proktaṃ māthuraṃ dvārvatī tathā |
children.translated_text: His abode is said to be of two kinds: <s>Māthura</s> and <s>Dvāravatī</s>.

children.text: māthuraṃ ca dvidhā prāhur gokulaṃ puram eva ca // Lbh_1,5.497 //
children.translated_text: And <s>Māthura</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>Gokula</s> and the city (<s>Mathurā</s>) itself. (Lbh 1.5.497)

children.text: yat tu goloka-nāma syāt tac ca gokula-vaibhavam |
children.translated_text: That which is called <s>Goloka</s> is indeed the glory of <s>Gokula</s>;

children.text: sa goloko yathā brahma-saṃhitāyām iha śrutaḥ // Lbh_1,5.498 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Goloka</s>, as heard here in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>: (Lbh 1.5.498)
'In His own abode called <s>Goloka</s>, and below it,
in the abodes of <s>Devī</s>, <s>Maheśa</s>, and <s>Hari</s>, in each and every one,

children.text: te te prabhāva-nicayā vihitāś ca yena
children.translated_text: those respective arrays of powers were established by whom —

children.text: govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi // Lbh_1,5.499 //
children.translated_text: that primeval person <s>Govinda</s>, Him I worship.' (Lbh 1.5.499)
<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.43
And further on (<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.56):
'The <s>Śrīs</s> (Lakṣmīs) are the beloveds, the beloved is the Supreme Person; the wish-fulfilling trees
are the trees; the land is made of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems); the water is nectar;

children.text: kathā gānaṃ nāṭyaṃ gamanam api vaṃśī priya-sakhi
children.translated_text: speech is song; movement is dance; the flute is the dear companion;

children.text: cid-ānandaṃ jyotiḥ param api tad āsvādyam api ca // Lbh_1,5.500 //
children.translated_text: the light is consciousness-bliss, supreme, and yet relishable. (Lbh 1.5.500)

children.text: sa yatra kṣīrābdhiḥ sravati surabhībhyaś ca su-mahān
children.translated_text: Where a great ocean of milk flows from the <s>Surabhī</s> cows,

children.text: nimeṣārdhākhyo vā vrajati na hi yatrāpi samayaḥ |
children.translated_text: and not even a half-moment of time passes;

children.text: bhaje śvetadvīpaṃ tam aham iha golokam iti yaṃ
children.translated_text: I worship that <s>Śvetadvīpa</s> (White Island), which those few saints,

children.text: vidantas te santaḥ kṣiti-virala-cārāḥ katipaye // Lbh_1,5.501 //
children.translated_text: rare wanderers on this earth, know as <s>Goloka</s>.' (Lbh 1.5.501)
Thus.
And its being the glory of His own self is due to the eminence of that greatness. (Lbh 1.5.502)
As stated in the <s>Pātāla-khaṇḍa</s>:

children.text: aho madhupurī dhanyā vaikuṇṭhāc ca garīyasī |
children.translated_text: 'Ah, blessed is <s>Madhupurī</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>), greater even than <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>!

children.text: dinam ekaṃ nivāsena harau bhaktiḥ prajāyate // Lbh_1,5.503 //
children.translated_text: By residing there for even one day, devotion to <s>Hari</s> arises.' (Lbh 1.5.503)

children.text: ayodhyā mathurā māyā kāśī kāñcī avantikā |
children.translated_text: '<s>Ayodhyā</s>, <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Māyā</s> (Haridvāra), <s>Kāśī</s>, <s>Kāñcī</s>, <s>Avantikā</s>,

children.text: purī dvāravatī caiva saptaitā mokṣa-dāyikāḥ // Lbh_1,5.504 //
children.translated_text: and the city of <s>Dvāravatī</s> — these seven bestow liberation.' (Lbh 1.5.504)

children.text: evaṃ sapta-purīṇāṃ tu sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ tu māthuram |
children.translated_text: 'Of these seven cities, the supremely exalted is <s>Māthura</s> (<s>Mathurā</s>);
hear, O <s>Devī</s>, its glory, the best among <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> realms.' (Lbh 1.5.505)
Thus.
That it is the site of eternal pastimes (<s>nitya-līlā</s>) has been shown previously;

children.text: atevāsya pādme ca śrūyate nitya-rūpatā // Lbh_1,5.506 //
children.translated_text: therefore in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> too, its eternal nature is heard: // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.506 //

children.text: nityāṃ me mathurāṃ viddhi vanaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ tathā
yamunāṃ gopa-kanyāś ca tathā gopāla-bālakān // Lbh_1,5.507 //
children.translated_text: and the <s>Yamunā</s>, and the cowherd maidens, and the cowherd boys.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.507 //
'Know My <s>Mathurā</s> to be eternal, and the forest <s>Vṛndāvana</s> likewise,
Thus.
That realm, though appearing as the land of <s>Mathurā</s>, concealed, is yet wondrous;

children.text: sphāraḥ saṅkucitaś ca syāt kṛṣṇa-līlānusārataḥ // Lbh_1,5.508 //
children.translated_text: it expands and contracts in accordance with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s pastimes. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.508 //
Here indeed even a garland of cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>-s) finds accommodation;
even in a semblance of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, this was experienced by <s>Brahmā</s> himself. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.509 //

children.text: ity ato rāsa-līlāyāṃ puline tatra yāmune |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>rāsa-līlā</s> (divine dance), on the sandy bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: pradaāśata-koṭyo'pi mamūr yat tat kim adbhutam // Lbh_1,5.510 //
children.translated_text: even tens of billions danced — what wonder is there in that? // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.510 //

children.text: svaiḥ svair līlā-parikarair janair dṛśyāni nāparaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Those pastimes and their settings are visible only to their respective participants, not to others;
indeed, they manifest as appropriate at the time of each respective pastime. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.511 //
Wondrously, even while existing simultaneously in one place,
they are in every way mutually non-interfering in their essential natures. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.512 //
Adorned on all sides with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s childhood and other pastimes,
the hills, cow-stations, forests, and other places have many forms. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.513 //
A place rich with His pastimes is sometimes seen as empty

children.text: śūnya evekṣate dṛṣṭi-yogyair apy aparair api // Lbh_1,5.514 //
children.translated_text: by some, even by those who are qualified to see. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.514 //

children.text: ataḥ prabhoḥ priyāṇāṃ ca dhāmnaś ca samayasya ca |
children.translated_text: Therefore, since the Lord, His beloved ones, His abode, and the occasions

children.text: avicintya-prabhāvatvād atra kiṃ ca na durghaṭam // Lbh_1,5.515 //
children.translated_text: all have inconceivable power, nothing here is impossible. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.515 //

children.text: evam eva dvārakāyāṃ jñeyaṃ sarvaṃ vicakṣaṇaiḥ // Lbh_1,5.516 //
children.translated_text: The same should be understood by the discerning regarding <s>Dvārakā</s> as well. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.516 //
As stated at the end of the Eleventh Canto (11.31.23-24):
'<s>Dvārakā</s>, abandoned by <s>Hari</s>, was instantly flooded by the ocean,
except, O great king, for the blessed abode of the Lord.
Whose mere remembrance destroys all inauspiciousness, the most auspicious of all auspicious things —

children.text: nityaṃ sannihitas tatra bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ // Lbh_1,5.517 //
children.translated_text: the Lord <s>Madhusūdana</s> is eternally present there.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.517 //
Thus.
Now another splendor of His is made manifest through <s>Śrī Nārada</s>'s vision,
wherein the wondrous variety of His many forms appears simultaneously in one place. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.518 //
And in the <s>Sammohana Tantra</s>:
'His <s>avatāra</s>-s, O greatly fortunate one, are thousands;
among those incarnations, boyhood (<s>bālatva</s>) is most rare.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.521 //
Thus.
Here is the explanatory verse:

children.text: tridhā bhaved vayo bālyaṃ yauvanaṃ vṛddhatety api |
children.translated_text: Age is threefold: childhood, youth, and old age.

children.text: varṣād ā-ṣoḍaśād bālyam iti loke mahāntaram // Lbh_1,5.522 //
children.translated_text: Childhood extends from the first year to sixteen — this is the widely accepted view. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.522 //
And in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: santi bhūrīṇi rūpāṇi mama pūrṇāni ṣaḍ-guṇaiḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I have many forms complete with the six divine qualities (<s>ṣaḍ-guṇa</s>);

children.text: bhaveyus tāni tulyāni na mayā gopa-rūpiṇā // Lbh_1,5.523 //
children.translated_text: but they would not be equal to Me in My cowherd form (<s>gopa-rūpin</s>).' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.523 //
Thus.
Here in this very context, great <s>mantra</s>-s adorned with great glory,
of ten syllables, eighteen syllables, and so forth, are celebrated in many <s>tantra</s>-s. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.524 //
Superior to all authorities is the <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s> (<s>Upaniṣad</s>),

children.text: svayam ādau vidhātre yā proktā gopāla-rūpiṇā // Lbh_1,5.525 //
children.translated_text: which was spoken at the beginning by the Cowherd-formed Lord Himself to <s>Brahmā</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.525 //

children.text: caturdhā mādhurī tasya vraja eva virājate |
children.translated_text: His fourfold sweetness (<s>mādhurī</s>) shines forth in <s>Vraja</s> alone:

children.text: aiśvarya-krīḍayor veṇos tathā śrī-vigrahasya ca // Lbh_1,5.526 //
children.translated_text: the sweetness of divine opulence (<s>aiśvarya</s>), of play (<s>krīḍā</s>), of the flute (<s>veṇu</s>), and of His divine form (<s>śrī-vigraha</s>). // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.526 //
Regarding the sweetness of opulence:
Served by an unprecedented flood of sweet majesty,

children.text: sevyamāno haris tatra vihāraṃ kurute vraje // Lbh_1,5.527 //
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> sports there in <s>Vraja</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.527 //
Where, though praised by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others, out of awe,

children.text: dṛg-anta-pātam apy eṣu kurute na tu keśavaḥ // Lbh_1,5.528 //
children.translated_text: <s>Keśava</s> does not even cast a sidelong glance at them. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.528 //
As stated in the <s>Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Nārada</s>:

children.text: ye daityā duḥśakaṃ hantuṃ cakreṇāpi rathāṅginā |
children.translated_text: 'Those demons who were difficult to kill even with the discus by the Discus-bearer —

children.text: te tvayā nihatāḥ kṛṣṇa navyayā bālya-līlayā ||
children.translated_text: they were slain by You, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, through Your ever-fresh childhood pastimes.

children.text: sārdhaṃ mitrair hare krīḍan bhrū-bhaṅgaṃ kuruṣe yadi |
children.translated_text: When You, O <s>Hari</s>, playing with Your friends, merely knit Your brow,

children.text: sa-śaṅkā brahma-rudrādyāḥ kampate kha-sthitās tadā // Lbh_1,5.529 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and the others, standing in the sky, tremble with apprehension.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.529 //
Thus.
'Expert in the various ways of cowherds,
skilled in many kinds of flute-playing,
Your son, when the flute was placed on His bimba-red lower lip,
drew forth the musical modes.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.530 //
As stated in <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, Tenth Canto (10.35.14):
Regarding play — as stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
'All the deeds of <s>Kṛṣṇa-deva</s> are entirely wondrous;
and among them, the cowherd pastimes (<s>gopāla-līlā</s>) are in every way the most enchanting.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.531 //
In the <s>Bṛhad-Vāmana Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: santi yadyapi me prājyā līlās tās tā manoharāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Though I have abundant and enchanting pastimes of various kinds,

children.text: na hi jāne smṛte rāse mano me kīdṛśaṃ bhavet // Lbh_1,5.532 //
children.translated_text: I do not know what becomes of My mind when the <s>rāsa</s> (divine dance) is remembered.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.532 //
Thus.

children.text:
veṇoḥ yathā -
yāvatī nikhile loke nādānām asti mādhurī |

children.translated_text: all of it drowns in the supreme particle of the sound of the <s>vaṃśikā</s> (bamboo flute).
When both the moving and the stationary are plunged into intense supreme bliss,

children.text: bhaved dharma-viparyāso yasmin dhvanati mohane // Lbh_1,5.533 //
children.translated_text: there occurs a reversal of <s>dharma</s> (natural order) — when that enchanting sound resounds. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.533 //

Regarding the flute:
'Whatever sweetness exists among all sounds in the entire world,

children.text: mohanaḥ ko'pi mantro vā padārtho vādbhutaḥ paraḥ |
children.translated_text: Is it some inconceivable <s>mantra</s>, or some wondrous supreme substance,

children.text: śruti-peyo'yam ity uktvā yatrāmuhyan śivādayaḥ // Lbh_1,5.534 //
children.translated_text: to be drunk by the ears?' — saying thus, even <s>Śiva</s> and the others were bewildered. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.534 //
Hearing that at every <s>savana</s> (pressing/occasion), the lords of the gods,
led by <s>Indra</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>,
the wise ones, with bowed necks and minds,
fell into bewilderment, unable to ascertain the truth of it. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.536 //
In the twenty-first and thirty-fifth chapters is praised

children.text: mādhurī vraja-devībhir veṇor eva mahādbhutā // Lbh_1,5.537 //
children.translated_text: the most wondrous sweetness of the flute itself, by the goddesses of <s>Vraja</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.537 //
Regarding the divine form (<s>śrī-vigraha</s>), as stated:
'An ocean of the nectar of waves of sweetness without equal or superior,
the son of the chief of cowherds (<s>Gopendra-nandana</s>), whose form delights all moving and stationary beings.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.538 //
'The beauty of whose form would put to shame the splendor of tens of billions of <s>Kandarpa</s>-s (Cupids),
whose lotus-toe-nails are worthy of worship (<s>nīrājya</s>) by them,
whose charm is lovely beyond anything ever seen or heard —
I shall describe the supreme meditation on the son of <s>Nanda</s>.' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.539 //
As stated in a <s>Tantra</s>:
And in <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, Tenth Canto (10.29.40):
'What woman in the three worlds, O dear one, would not stray from the path of propriety,
being enchanted by the sweet, prolonged, captivating notes of Your melody?
Seeing this form which is the fortune of all three worlds,
which causes horripilation in cows, brāhmaṇas, trees, and deer!' // <s>Lbh</s> 1.5.540 //

children.text:
iti śrī-rūpa-gosvāmi-pāda-kṛte śrī-laghu-bhāgavatāmṛte
śrī-kṛṣṇāmṛta-nāma pūrva-khaṇḍaṃ samāptam ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Pūrva-khaṇḍa</s> (First Part) named <s>Śrī-Kṛṣṇāmṛta</s> (The Nectar of Śrī Kṛṣṇa) in the <s>Śrī Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> composed by <s>Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī</s>.

<s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s>
<s>Uttara-khaṇḍa</s> (Second Part)
Oṃ. Obeisance to those who relish the nectar of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s <s>rasa</s>.
Now, <s>Śrī Bhaktāmṛta</s> (The Nectar of Devotees).
Just as the worship of <s>Mukunda</s> is essential,

children.text: tathā tadīya-bhaktānāṃ no ced doṣo'sti dustaraḥ // Lbh_2,1.1 //
children.translated_text: so too is the worship of His devotees; if not, there is an insurmountable fault. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.1 //
As stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
'<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: puṇḍarīko baliḥ śambhuḥ prahlādo viduro dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, <s>Bali</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Vidura</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>,

children.text: dālbhyaḥ parāśaro bhīṣmo nāradādyāś ca vaiṣṇavaiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Dālbhya</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and others — these <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>-s

children.text: sevyā hariṃ niṣevyāmī no ced āgaḥ paraṃ bhavet // Lbh_2,1.2 //
children.translated_text: should be served after serving <s>Hari</s>; otherwise, there arises the greatest offense.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.2 //
And in the <s>Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya</s> (16.76):

children.text: arcayitvā tu govindaṃ tadīyān nārcayanti ye |
children.translated_text: 'Those who worship <s>Govinda</s> but do not worship His devotees —

children.text: na te viṣṇoḥ prasādasya bhājanaṃ dāmbhikā janāḥ // Lbh_2,1.3 //
children.translated_text: those hypocritical people are not fit vessels for <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s grace.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.3 //
In the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
'Of all forms of worship, the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is supreme;

children.text: tasmāt parataraṃ devi tadīyānāṃ samarcanam // Lbh_2,1.4 //
children.translated_text: yet superior even to that, O Goddess, is the worship of His devotees.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.4 //
And in the same text:

children.text: arcayitvā tu govindaṃ tadīyān nārcayet tu yaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'One who worships <s>Govinda</s> but does not worship His devotees

children.text: na sa bhāgavato jñeyaḥ kevalaṃ dāmbhikaḥ smṛtaḥ // Lbh_2,1.5 //
children.translated_text: should not be considered a <s>Bhāgavata</s>; he is merely regarded as a hypocrite.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.5 //
Thus.
In the <s>Ādi Purāṇa</s>:

children.text: mama bhaktā hi ye pārtha na me bhaktās tu te matāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Those who are My devotees, O <s>Pārtha</s>, are not considered My devotees (directly);

children.text: mad-bhaktasya tu ye bhaktās te me yuktatamā matāḥ // Lbh_2,1.6 //
children.translated_text: but those who are devotees of My devotees — they are deemed most devoted to Me.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.6 //

And in <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> (11.19.21):
'The worship of My devotee is superior.' Thus. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.7 //

children.text: eteṣām api sarveṣāṃ prahlādaḥ pravaro mataḥ |
children.translated_text: Among all these devotees, <s>Prahlāda</s> is considered the foremost;

children.text: sarveṣu hari-bhakteṣu prahlādo hi mahattamaḥ // Lbh_2,1.8 //
children.translated_text: among all devotees of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s> is indeed the greatest. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.8 //
As stated in the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Rudra</s>:

children.text: bhakta eva hi tattvena kṛṣṇaṃ jānāti na tv aham |
children.translated_text: 'A devotee alone truly knows <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, not I;
among all devotees of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s> is the most exalted.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.9 //
'Where am I, born in a family of demons, in this existence dominated by <s>rajas</s> and <s>tamas</s>,
O Lord, and where is Your compassion!

children.text: na brahmaṇo na tu bhavasya na vai ramāyā
children.translated_text: Neither upon <s>Brahmā</s>, nor upon <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), nor upon <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī)

children.text: yan me 'rpitaḥ śirasi padma-karaḥ prasādaḥ // Lbh_2,1.10 //
children.translated_text: has the grace of Your lotus hand been placed upon their heads as it has upon mine.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.10 //
In the Seventh Canto of <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Prahlāda</s> himself (7.9.26):
In the same context, the words of <s>Śrī Nṛsiṃha</s> (7.10.21):

children.text: bhavanti puruṣā loke mad-bhaktās tvām anuvratāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'In this world, people become My devotees following your example;

children.text: bhavān me khalu bhaktānāṃ sarveṣāṃ pratirūpa-dhṛk // Lbh_2,1.11 //
children.translated_text: you are indeed the model for all My devotees.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.11 //

children.text: pāṇḍavāḥ sarvataḥ śreṣṭhāḥ prahlādād īdṛśād api |
children.translated_text: The <s>Pāṇḍava</s>-s are superior in every way even to <s>Prahlāda</s> of such stature;

children.text: śrī-bhāgavatam evātra pramāṇaṃ sphuṭam īkṣyate // Lbh_2,1.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> itself is clearly seen as the authority here. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.12 //
As stated in the Seventh Canto, the words of <s>Śrī Nārada</s> (7.10.48-50, 7.15.75-77):
'You in the human world are indeed greatly fortunate!
Sages who purify the worlds approach
the homes in which dwells directly,
in disguise, the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.13 //
'He, this very <s>Brahman</s>, sought by the greatest sages,
the experience of the bliss of <s>kaivalya</s> (absolute liberation) and <s>nirvāṇa</s> —
He is your beloved, your friend, your maternal cousin,
your very Self, worthy of your worship, the performer of duties, and your Guru.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.14 //
'He whose form is not described in its true reality
even by <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), <s>Padmaja</s> (Brahmā), and others through their intellects —
worshipped through silence, devotion, and tranquility,

children.text: prasīdatām eṣa sa sātvatāṃ patiḥ // Lbh_2,1.15 //
children.translated_text: may He, the Lord of the <s>Sātvata</s>-s, be pleased.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.15 //
Thus.
And this is explained by <s>Śrī Svāmī-pāda</s> (Śrīdhara Svāmī):

children.text: aho prahlādasya bhāgyaṃ yena devo dṛṣṭaḥ | vayaṃ tu manda-bhāgyāḥ iti
viṣīdantaṃ rājānaṃ praty āha yūyam iti tribhiḥ // Lbh_2,1.16 //
children.translated_text: to the king who was despondent, he (<s>Nārada</s>) spoke with three verses beginning with 'You.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.16 //
'Alas, what fortune of <s>Prahlāda</s>, by whom the Lord was seen! We are indeed of meager fortune' — thus

children.text:
na tu prahlādasya gṛhe paraṃ brahma vasati, na ca tad-darśanārthaṃ munayas
tad-gṛhān abhiyanti | na ca tasya brahma mātuleyādi-rūpeā vartate | na ca svayam
eva prasannaṃ | ato yūyam eva tato'py asmatto'pi bhūri-bhāgāḥ iti

children.translated_text: is the purport. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.17 //

But the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> does not dwell in <s>Prahlāda</s>'s home, nor do sages approach his home for the purpose of seeing Him; nor does <s>Brahman</s> exist for him in the forms of maternal cousin and so forth; nor is He spontaneously pleased with him. Therefore, 'you are even more greatly fortunate than he, and than us as well' — this
Due to their constant extreme proximity and <s>Hari</s>'s greater possessiveness toward them,

children.text: pāṇḍavebhyo'pi yadavaḥ kecit śreṣṭhatamā matāḥ // Lbh_2,1.18 //
children.translated_text: some <s>Yādava</s>-s are considered even superior to the <s>Pāṇḍava</s>-s. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.18 //
As stated in the Tenth Canto (10.82.28, 30):

children.text: aho bhoja-pate yūyaṃ janma-bhājo nṝṇām iha |
children.translated_text: 'O lord of the <s>Bhoja</s>-s! You here are truly blessed among mortals,

children.text: yat paśyathāsakṛt kṛṣṇaṃ durdarśam api yoginām // Lbh_2,1.19 //
children.translated_text: for you behold <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> constantly — He who is difficult to see even for <s>yogin</s>-s.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.19 //
'The seeing, touching, walking alongside, conversing,
sleeping, sitting, eating, sharing a bed, and kinship-bond with Him —
for you who tread the path of hellish existence in your homes,
<s>Viṣṇu</s> Himself became the cessation of heaven and liberation.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.20 //
'In resting, sitting, walking, talking, playing, bathing, eating, and other activities,

children.text: na viduḥ santam ātmānaṃ vṛṣṇayaḥ kṛṣṇa-cetasaḥ // Lbh_2,1.21 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>-s, whose minds were absorbed in <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, did not know their own true selves.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.21 //
Even more distinguished than all the <s>Yadu</s>-s is the glorious <s>Uddhava</s>;
his wondrous glory is heard in <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.22 //
As stated in the Eleventh Canto, the words of the Lord Himself (SB 11.14.15):

children.text: na tathā me priyatama ātma-yonir na śaṅkaraḥ
children.translated_text: 'Neither <s>Ātma-yoni</s> (Brahmā), nor <s>Śaṅkara</s> (Śiva) is so dear to Me,

children.text: na ca saṅkarṣaṇo na śrīr naivātmā ca yathā bhavān // Lbh_2,1.23 //
children.translated_text: nor <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, nor <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī), nor indeed My own Self, as you are.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.23 //
'Among <s>Bhāgavata</s>-s (devotees), you are I.' // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.24 //
Thus.

children.text: ābālyād eva govinde bhaktir asyākhilottamā // Lbh_2,1.25 //
children.translated_text: From childhood itself, his devotion to <s>Govinda</s> is the most supreme of all. // <s>Lbh</s> 2.1.25 //
As stated in the Third Canto (3.2.2):
He who, at five years of age, when asked by his mother for the morning meal,

children.text: tan naicchad racayan yasya saparyāṃ bāla-līlayā // Lbh_2,1.26 //
children.translated_text: did not desire that, but instead arranged worship of Him through childhood play. // Lbh_2,1.26 //
Therefore, in that very place, the words of the <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> (3.4.31) —
<s>Uddhava</s> is not in the slightest inferior to Me,
because he is a master not afflicted by the <s>guṇas</s> (material qualities). // Lbh_2,1.27 //
Thus.

children.text:
asyārthaḥ | yad-guṇaiḥ yasya uddhavasya guṇaiḥ, prabhur apy ahaṃ na arditaḥ | na
yācitaḥ | yad vā yat yasmāt | uddhavaḥ guṇaiḥ sattvādibhiḥ | na arditaḥ na pīḍitaḥ
| guṇātīta ity arthaḥ | tatra hetuḥ prabhuḥ bhaktir asāṃvāde

children.translated_text: is supremely powerful. // Lbh_2,1.28 //

The meaning of this: "by whose qualities" means by the qualities of <s>Uddhava</s>; even I, the Lord, am "not afflicted" — not entreated. Or alternatively, "yat" means "because": <s>Uddhava</s> is "not afflicted" by the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities) such as <s>sattva</s> and the rest — not tormented; the meaning is that he is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (<s>guṇātīta</s>). The reason for this is "<s>prabhu</s>" — <s>bhakti</s> (devotion), when there is no contradiction,
The ladies of <s>Vraja</s> are superior even to such an <s>Uddhava</s>,

children.text: yad āsāṃ prema-mādhuryaṃ sa eṣo'py abhiyācate // Lbh_2,1.29 //
children.translated_text: for he himself prays for the sweetness of their <s>prema</s> (divine love). // Lbh_2,1.29 //
These cowherd women of <s>Vraja</s> are the highest among embodied beings on earth,
for they have deeply established love for <s>Govinda</s>, the Soul of all;

children.text: vāñchanti yad bhava-bhiyo munayo vayaṃ ca
children.translated_text: that which sages fearful of material existence and we ourselves desire —
of what use are births even as <s>Brahmā</s> for one who relishes the narratives of the Infinite? // Lbh_2,1.30 //
As stated in the glorious Tenth Canto (10.47.58) —
And in the <s>Śrī Bṛhad-vāmana</s>, the words of <s>Śrī Brahmā</s> addressed to <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others —
For sixty thousand years I performed <s>tapas</s> (austerities) in ancient times,
in order to obtain the dust of the feet of the women of <s>Nanda Gopa</s>'s <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: tathāpi na mayā prāptās tāsāṃ vai pāda-reṇavaḥ // Lbh_2,1.31 //
children.translated_text: yet even so, I did not obtain the dust of their feet. // Lbh_2,1.31 //
The words of <s>Bhṛgu</s> and others —
The dust of the feet of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> (devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>) is accepted even by those like you;

children.text: santi te bahavo loke vaiṣṇavā nāradādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there are many <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> in the world, such as <s>Nārada</s> and others.

children.text: teṣāṃ vihāya gopīnāṃ pāda-reṇus tvayāpi yat |
children.translated_text: Setting them aside, that you seek the foot-dust of the <s>gopīs</s> —

children.text: gṛhyate saṃśayo me'tra ko hetus tadvat prabho // Lbh_2,1.32 //
children.translated_text: I have a doubt here: what is the reason for this, O Lord? // Lbh_2,1.32 //
The words of <s>Śrī Brahmā</s> —

children.text: na striyo vraja-sundaryaḥ putra śreṣṭhāḥ śriyo'pi tāḥ |
children.translated_text: O son, the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s> are not merely women; they are superior even to <s>Śrī</s> (the goddess of fortune);

children.text: nāhaṃ śivaś ca śeṣaś ca śrīś ca tābhiḥ samāḥ kvacit // Lbh_2,1.33 //
children.translated_text: neither I, nor <s>Śiva</s>, nor <s>Śeṣa</s>, nor <s>Śrī</s> can ever be equal to them. // Lbh_2,1.33 //
And in the <s>Ādi Purāṇa</s>, the words of <s>Śrīmad Arjuna</s> —

children.text: trailokye bhagavad-bhaktāḥ ke tvāṃ jānanti marmaṇi |
children.translated_text: In the three worlds, which devotees of the Lord know You in essence?

children.text: keṣu vā tvaṃ sadā tuṣṭaḥ keṣu prema tavātulam // Lbh_2,1.34 //
children.translated_text: With whom are You always pleased? In whom does Your matchless <s>prema</s> (love) reside? // Lbh_2,1.34 //
The words of <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> —

children.text: na tathā me priyatamo brahmā-rudraś ca pārthiva |
children.translated_text: Neither <s>Brahmā</s> nor <s>Rudra</s> are as dear to Me, O king,

children.text: na ca lakṣmīr na cātmā ca yathā gopījano mam // Lbh_2,1.35 //
children.translated_text: nor <s>Lakṣmī</s>, nor even My own Self, as the <s>gopī</s> people are to Me. // Lbh_2,1.35 //

children.text: bhaktā mamānuraktāś ca kati santi na bhūtale |
children.translated_text: How many devoted and loving devotees of Mine exist on earth?
Yet the <s>gopī</s> people are dearer to Me than My very life-breath. // Lbh_2,1.36 //

children.text: na māṃ jānanti munayo yoginaś ca parantapa |
children.translated_text: Neither the sages nor the <s>yogīs</s> know Me, O scorcher of foes,

children.text: na ca rudrādayo devā yathā gopyo vidanti mām // Lbh_2,1.37 //
children.translated_text: nor do <s>Rudra</s> and the other gods know Me as the <s>gopīs</s> know Me. // Lbh_2,1.37 //

children.text: na tapobhir na vedaiś ca nācārair na ca vidyayā |
children.translated_text: Not by austerities, not by the <s>Vedas</s>, not by proper conduct, nor by learning,

children.text: vaśo'smi kevalaṃ premṇā premāṇaṃ tatra gopikā // Lbh_2,1.38 //
children.translated_text: am I controlled — solely by <s>prema</s> (pure love), and the repository of that <s>prema</s> is the <s>gopikās</s>. // Lbh_2,1.38 //
My greatness, My worship, faith in Me, and the thoughts directed toward Me —

children.text: jānanti gopikāḥ pārtha nānye jānanti marmaṇi // Lbh_2,1.39 //
children.translated_text: the <s>gopikās</s> know these in essence, O <s>Pārtha</s>; no others know them truly. // Lbh_2,1.39 //

children.text: nijāṅgam api yā gopyo mameti samupāsate |
children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s> who worship even their own bodies as "belonging to Me" —

children.text: tābhyaḥ paraṃ na me pārtha nigūḍha-prema-bhājanam // Lbh_2,1.40 //
children.translated_text: there is none greater than them, O <s>Pārtha</s>, as vessels of My most intimate <s>prema</s> (love). // Lbh_2,1.40 //
Thus.

children.text: na citraṃ prema-mādhuryam āsāṃ vāñched yad uddhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: It is no wonder that <s>Uddhava</s> desires the sweetness of the <s>prema</s> (love) of these <s>gopīs</s>,
he who prays even for a birth as grass sprinkled by the dust of their feet. // Lbh_2,1.41 //
Oh, may I become any one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
that are blessed by the dust of the feet of these <s>gopīs</s>;

children.text: yā dustyajaṃ sva-janam ārya-pathaṃ ca hitvā
children.translated_text: who, abandoning their own kinsmen — so difficult to forsake — and the path of chastity,
worshipped the path of <s>Mukunda</s>, which is sought by the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedic scriptures). // Lbh_2,1.42 //
As stated in the glorious Tenth Canto (BhP 10.47.61) —
Thus, having first served <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the people who are worshippers of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>
must certainly worship the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s> with flowers of grace and the like. // Lbh_2,1.43 //
And among all the <s>gopīs</s>, <s>Rādhikā</s> is supremely the greatest,
for She is declared as possessing all superiority in the <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Āgamas</s>, and other scriptures. // Lbh_2,1.44 //
As stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> —

children.text: yathā rādhā priyā viṣṇos tasyāḥ kuṇḍaṃ priyaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Rādhā</s> is dear to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, so too is Her pond (<s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s>) equally dear;
among all the <s>gopīs</s>, She alone is the most beloved of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. // Lbh_2,1.45 //
And in the <s>Ādi Purāṇa</s> —

children.text: trailokye pṛthivī dhanyā yatra vṛndāvanaṃ purī |
children.translated_text: In the three worlds, the earth is blessed, for upon it stands the city of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>;

children.text: tatrāpi gopikāḥ pārtha tatra rādhābhidhā mama // Lbh_2,1.46 //
children.translated_text: and there, O <s>Pārtha</s>, among the <s>gopikās</s>, the one named <s>Rādhā</s> is Mine. // Lbh_2,1.46 //

children.text:
iti śrī-laghu-bhāgavatāmṛte śrī-bhaktāmṛtaṃ nāmottara-khaṇḍaṃ samāptam |
iti śrī-laghu-bhāgavatāmṛtaṃ sampūrṇam |
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Uttara-khaṇḍa</s> named <s>Śrī Bhaktāmṛta</s> (the nectar of devotion) of the <s>Śrī Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s>. Thus the <s>Śrī Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> is complete.
